title: Senior Client Director, Strategic Accounts
description:
Senior Client Director,

AI-Driven Commercial Effectiveness

ABOUT ODAIA

ODAIA noun o·da·ia | 'oh-day-yeah
An Ancient Greek word referring to "ōdē," the word for song and the root of melody, harmony, and orchestra. We chose it deliberately: the best commercial intelligence doesn't just inform it orchestrates.

ODAIA delivers AI-powered commercial intelligence for life sciences - unifying data, accelerating results, and helping commercial teams deepen engagement to enhance care for providers and patients. ODAIA's AI platform transforms complex data into predictive, personalized insights, enabling commercial leaders to understand their customers, anticipate prescribing behaviors, and make the informed, strategic decisions that bring therapies to patients faster.

OUR MISSION

Reducing patients’ time to therapy by facilitating meaningful interactions with healthcare providers, through human-centric software powered by AI.

WHAT’S ON OFFER

Reporting to the Managing Principal, AI-Driven Commercial Effectiveness, the Senior Client Director is the commercial engine within ODAIA’s cross-functional GTM team. This is not a traditional account management role;It is a high-autonomy, high-impact sales leadership position designed for a strategist who thrives at the intersection of complex selling and long-term account growth.

The Mission: A “Hunter with a Farmers Mindset”

You will own the full commercial lifecycle, from identifying "white space" and qualifying high-value prospects to orchestrating complex deal executions and securing the close. Your success isn't just measured by the initial contract, but by the executive-level relationships and account depth you build to drive sustained, multi-year expansion.

The Pod Structure: Integrated Execution

You won't operate in a silo. You will lead and collaborate within a cross functional, specialized team (Pod) alongside:

Managing Principals: Your strategic partners and executive sponsors. They provide the high-level industry vision, navigate C-suite blockers, and ensure your pod’s commercial strategy aligns with ODAIA’s AI roadmap.
Solution Engineers: To bridge the gap between AI capabilities and client needs.
Business Acceleration Partners: To ensure seamless onboarding and rapid time-to-value.
Marketing Leads: To sharpen the narrative and drive demand within your target accounts.

WHAT YOU WILL DO

Enterprise Sales & Revenue Growth

  • Own and drive new business acquisition across mid-market and enterprise Life Sciences organizations, with full accountability for pipeline generation, deal progression, and revenue targets
  • Lead complex, multi-stakeholder sales cycles, navigating commercial, SIP, SFE, and IT buying groups to build consensus and close
  • Identify whitespace opportunities across business units, therapeutic areas, and brands to expand ODAIA’s footprint within strategic accounts
  • Develop compelling business cases that connect ODAIA’s AI-driven insights to measurable commercial outcomes - revenue acceleration, field productivity, and competitive advantage

Consultative Client Engagement

  • Lead with outcomes, not features - challenge the status quo and help clients rethink how predictive intelligence and Next Best Action strategies can transform commercial performance
  • Conduct strategic discovery conversations that uncover pain points across commercial organizations, translating complex analytics into executive-ready narratives
  • Build and deepen executive-level relationships with decision-makers across Director, VP, and C-suite levels, positioning ODAIA as a long-term transformation partner - not a transactional vendor
  • Serve as the primary commercial point of contact for key accounts, maintaining alignment across internal and client stakeholders throughout the customer lifecycle

Pod Collaboration & Deal Execution

  • Operate within ODAIA’s cross-functional pod model alongside Solution Architecture, Business Acceleration, Product, and Customer Success to co-create value-driven proposals and demonstrations
  • Partner with the Managing Principal to shape account strategy, prioritize high-value opportunities, and ensure seamless transition from strategic win to activation
  • Translate ODAIA’s predictive modeling, AI orchestration, and platform capabilities into clear commercial impact during client-facing engagements
  • Maintain disciplined pipeline management, forecasting, and CRM hygiene (Salesforce), ensuring pipeline health through proactive opportunity development

Market Intelligence & Product Influence

  • Bring real-world market insights, competitive intelligence, and client transformation needs back to Engineering and Product to influence roadmap priorities
  • Identify emerging shifts in omnichannel strategy, NBA orchestration, and AI adoption across the pharma landscape
  • Represent the voice of the customer internally to help inform product evolution and market positioning

WHAT YOU BRING
Sales Track Record & Commercial Pharma Expertise

  • 8-12+ years of enterprise SaaS, analytics, or technology sales experience within the Life Sciences commercial ecosystem, with a consistent track record of exceeding quota
  • Proven success managing complex sales cycles with multi-stakeholder buying groups across pharma commercial, SIP, SFE, and IT organizations
  • Deep understanding of the pharma commercial landscape, including brand launch strategies, field effectiveness, omnichannel strategy, and how AI/predictive analytics drive commercial impact

Consultative Selling & Executive Presence

  • Strong consultative selling skills with the ability to lead value-based discussions, reframe client challenges, and build business cases that connect technology to P&L outcomes
  • Demonstrated ability to engage with and influence senior executives (VP, C-suite) across complex enterprise organizations
  • Excellent communication, negotiation, and presentation skills - able to translate “technical jargon” into “Commercial ROI” with clarity and confidence

Operational Agility & Growth Mindset

  • Self-starter who thrives in a lean, high-autonomy, high-growth environment and finds building the engine while mid-flight exhilarating
  • Can shift from strategic account planning to hands-on deal execution in the same hour - a bias for action over perfection
  • Experience using CRM and sales engagement tools to manage pipeline, reporting, and account strategy
  • Hands-on experience leveraging AI tools and agentic workflows to accelerate productivity - at ODAIA, we don’t just deliver AI, we live it

WHAT WE OFFER

Values-Based Culture

  • We Ignite Innovation, Own It, and Stand Together

AI-Native Environment

  • At ODAIA, we don't just deliver AI - we live it. We use AI and agentic automation to 10x our efficiency and impact, encouraging constant curiosity in leveraging and integrating AI

Comprehensive Rewards

  • Meaningful stock option grants, immediate medical/dental enrollment, and flexible time off

Remote-First Flexibility

  • WFH flexibility with intentional, high-value in-person collaboration and socials

LOCATION & BUSINESS TRAVEL

ODAIA is a remote first organization, with employees located across Canada and the U.S. Our primary office hub is located in central downtown Toronto and walking distance from Union Station.

This role requires travel within the US and Canada to support strategic customer meetings, industry conferences and internal meetings and offsites.

EMPLOYMENT VERIFICATION

Any conditional offer of employment made to a successful candidate will be subject to the full satisfaction with the results of any background and reference checks.

ODAIA does not use artificial intelligence (AI) to review applications, filter or analyze resumes.

Our recruitment team may use an AI-powered meeting assistant to record and transcribe interviews for note-taking purposes only. This role is also eligible for health benefits, stock options, and flexible time off policies as mentioned above.

title: Chesapeake - American Red Cross First Aid/CPR/AED Instructor/ Instructor Trainer
description:
About Us

At ALLCPR, we are committed to elevating community health and safety standards nationwide. We operate at more than 200 locations across the United States, providing American Heart Association Basic Life Support courses, American Red Cross First Aid/CPR/AED and Basic Life Support courses, and related CPR and life-saving training programs.

With an annual training volume of more than 80,000 participants, ALLCPR stands for the belief that all of us should learn CPR. It is our mission to ensure that everyone has the knowledge and skills to save lives.

Our Work Environment Includes

The Instructor will teach American Red Cross First Aid/CPR/AED courses and train students through the American Red Cross.﻿

The Instructor Trainer will be responsible for teaching American Red Cross First Aid/CPR/AED Instructor courses, training instructor candidates to become certified American Red Cross instructors.

The Instructor Trainer will prepare for training sessions, demonstrate proper techniques, and evaluate candidates' performance to ensure they have achieved proficiency.

The Instructor Trainer will work in various settings, including offices, schools, community centers, hospitals, and other locations.

Note: The Instructor Trainer's teaching methods and content must comply with American Red Cross requirements.

License / Certification

  • American Red Cross First Aid/CPR/AED Instructor Certification, r.25 — Required if you are looking for an instructor role
  • American Red Cross First Aid/CPR/AED Instructor Trainer Certification, r.25 — Required﻿ ﻿if you are looking for an instructor trainer role
  • American Red Cross BLS Instructor Trainer Certification — Preferred
  • American Heart Association BLS Instructor Certification — Preferred
  • Other equivalent Instructor Trainer certifications may be considered where an approved bridging pathway is available; we can provide bridging guidance.

Teaching Equipment

The Instructor Trainer must own at least 3 manikin sets.

Key Responsibilities

  • Prepare for American Red Cross First Aid/CPR/AED courses.
  • Deliver instructor-level training sessions to individuals or groups.
  • Demonstrate proper CPR/AED techniques that comply with American Red Cross requirements.
  • Provide feedback to candidates to help them improve their performance.
  • Monitor and evaluate candidate progress to ensure proficiency.
  • Complete and submit course records in accordance with American Red Cross requirements.
  • Ensure training materials are up-to-date and comply with relevant program requirements.
  • Participate in ongoing professional development to stay current with CPR and AED training best practices.
  • Provide excellent customer service to clients and candidates.

Requirements

  • Current American Red Cross First Aid/CPR/AED Instructor certification.
  • Strong knowledge of CPR and AED techniques and best practices.
  • Excellent communication and interpersonal skills.
  • Ability to prepare and deliver effective training sessions.
  • Attention to detail and the ability to provide constructive feedback to candidates.
  • Strong organizational and time-management skills.
  • High school diploma or equivalent.

Physical Demands

  • Must be able to stand for extended periods.
  • Must be able to lift and carry training equipment, up to 50 pounds.
  • Must be able to demonstrate proper CPR and AED techniques.

Working Conditions

  • Work may be performed in various settings, including schools, community centers, hospitals, and corporate offices.
  • Work may be performed primarily during weekends.

Salary and Benefits

Salary: $30.00 - $40.00 per teaching hour, commensurate with experience and length of working relationship with ALLCPR.

Additional Compensation: $10.00 per enrolled student. (Only for instructor trainer role)

Job Classification: 1099 Contractor or Part-Time Employee (Certain States).

Benefits

  • Flexible schedule.

Schedule

  • Day shift.
  • Weekend/Weekday availability.

Ability to Commute / Relocate

Location: Local area as per job post

Reliably commute or plan to relocate before starting work (Required).

Experience

  • Teaching: 2+ years (Preferred).

Job Type

  • Part-time
  • Contract

Work Location: In person

title: Fire Operations Supervisor
description:
About BurnBot
BurnBot provides systematic fuels treatment services to prevent destructive wildfires. We're firefighters, scientists, engineers, prescribed fire practitioners, ecologists, and community members who are answering the call to scale fuel treatment capacity. Our modern fuel treatment system recognizes and supports conservation efforts with a clean, smoke-free process. We need technology to amplify our workforces with targeted use of synthetic fire to treat fuel loads 10x faster than previously possible.

The Role
BurnBot is seeking a Fire Operations Specialist (FOS) to perform middle leadership oversight within the Fire Program. This role mixes supervisory oversight of BurnBot Fire Modules with responsibility for field-based project operational oversight as well as performing client-focused tasks.

This role, while in the field a majority of the time, may be based in Placerville, CA, Medford, OR, or our South San Francisco, CA Headquarters.

Administrative tasks include day to day management of 5-person Fire Modules. The FOS will have primary responsibility for recruitment and retention of 1-3 Modules as well as performing supervisory duties including onboarding, ensuring administrative tasks are carried out to BurnBot standards, providing performance feedback, coordinating training, and providing direction leadership in lieu of the Module Leader when they are unavailable. The FOS will help to coordinate Module mobilizations as well as their own in coordination with other FOS and Fire overhead.

Field based tasks will include:

  • Planning for and/or execution of prescribed fire (broadcast burning, pile burning, air curtain burning, RX2/PFV burning, etc)

  • Module leadership for wildfire mobilization and/or mobilization coordination across multiple types of equipment (Type 5 or 6 engines, chippers, heavy equipment, etc)

  • Conducting or coordinating Defensible Space Inspections

  • The FOS is expected to serve as a project manager/POC or Burn Boss for field projects and maintain a consistent field presence to support Fire Modules, evaluate conditions, and ensure alignment between planning and execution.

  • Performs job walks and field verification for proposal building

  • In coordination with organizational stakeholders, ensure all projects comply with OSHA, environmental regulations, and fire requirements

  • Maintains day-to-day relationship touchpoints at the site and project level

  • Captures issues early and escalates effectively through the Fire Director staff or Program leads

  • Maintains project artifacts including scope documentation, maps/GIS inputs, schedules, and acceptance checklists

  • Other duties as assigned



Administrative Tasks:

title: Secondary Mathematics Teaching & Learning Officer - Australia Fiji Education Program
description:
Fiji Program Support Platform (FPSP)

  • Locally Engaged Employee - 18-months contract with possible extension
  • Please apply online by submitting a cover letter addressing how you meet the requirements of this role and an up-to-date comprehensive CV
  • Education Districts: Lautoka/Nadi/Yasawa/Nadroga/Navosa

Program Overview:

FPSP, also referred to as the ‘Platform’, a Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade (DFAT) investment, will contribute to the delivery of Fiji’s national development priorities, in line with the Australia’s International Development Policy, the Fiji-Australia Vuvale Partnership and the Development Partnership Plan.

The Platform will deliver key bilateral programs, such as health, education, scholarships, social infrastructure, governance, climate and emergency preparedness and response. Platform activities will identify and address climate risks, promote climate action, and gender equality, disability and social inclusion (GEDSI) across and beyond the sector programs.

The Platform has three functional Outcomes:

  1. The Platform has delivered its sector program outcomes, including through supporting strategic coherence, planning, partnerships management, data and learning across the portfolio of investments.
  2. The Platform has prioritised gender equality, disability-inclusive development, and climate and disaster resilience, in its systems and practices. This includes in how it undertakes sector programming and its engagement with selected Government of Fiji (GoF) agencies.
  3. The Platform administers timely and efficient programming that is: value for money; maximises use of local supply chains; and supports good governance, and public diplomacy, effective decision making and risk management.

The Platform implements over fifty percent of Australia’s bilateral development support to Fiji across a range of sector programs in education, health, Australia Awards, disaster response, cyclone recovery, social infrastructure and technical assistance to improve public sector governance in Fiji.

The Platform integrates cross-cutting themes, including gender equality, disability and social inclusion (GEDSI), climate and disaster resilience, across sector programs. In particular, the Platform seeks to strengthen program outcomes by better addressing the needs of targeted populations including those who are often marginalised.

AFEP Overview:

The Australian Government is supporting Fiji’s education sector through the Australia Fiji Education Program (AFEP, the Program) working with the Ministry of Education (MoE).

The objective of the AFEP is “to work with the Government of Fiji under the Vuvale Partnership to catalyse quality education delivery for all Fijian children”.

The changes expected by the end of the five-year program are:

  • EOPO 1: Schools, particularly trial schools, have improved student literacy and numeracy outcomes, supported by enabling policies, plans and data from the Ministry of Education.
  • EOPO 2: Heads of schools and teachers, supported by enabling policies and data from the Ministry of Education, provide a safe, resilient and inclusive learning environment for all students, particularly in trial schools.

Four intermediate outcomes will provide pathways to meet these end of program outcomes in priority areas, like implementation of the revised literacy and numeracy curriculum in primary and secondary schools, professional development interventions, analysis and improvement of the Fiji Education Management Information System (FEMIS), as well as GEDSI and student wellbeing.

The funding for the program is approximately AUD45 million over 9 years (5 years, with an option to extend for a further 4 years) and delivered through a range of activities to achieve the program’s objectives. Implementation modalities include technical advice, procurement of technical services and goods, minor works and infrastructure upgrades, capacity building and training support, support to Ministry led initiatives and innovations, and grants to civil society organisations (CSOs).

Position Summary:

In coordination with the Curriculum Advisory Unit (CAS) of the Ministry of Education, the Secondary Mathematics Teaching & Learning Officers (TLO) will support the rollout of the Revised Secondary Mathematics Curriculum (RSMC) across Focus schools on each of the nine education districts.

TLO will work with Secondary Mathematics Heads of Department (HOD), Heads of School and teachers (School Staff) and students to support implementation of the RSMC and related changes to classroom pedagogy through direct training, in-classroom mentoring, and the provision of professional development support.

Additionally, TLO will administer pre and post assessment according to a set evaluation plan and collaborate with Secondary Mathematics Team and CAS to develop an inclusive Continuous Professional Development (CPD) Plan for their assigned schools. TLO will also participate in the revision of secondary mathematics curriculum.

TLO will support Focus School Staff by modelling lessons, team teaching and planning to improve the teaching and learning of the RSMC. Furthermore, they will assist Focus Schools in supporting other schools in their clusters and engage in professional development activities based on teacher feedback, observations and data.

Each TLO will be based within a District Education Office, reporting to the Senior Education Advisor (SEA) and AFEP Maths Coordinator. The expectation is that they will be working either directly or online with schools for most of the time.

TLO will work collaboratively with Divisional and District Education officers (Senior Education Advisor and Education Advisor), School Staff and students in schools throughout Fiji. Full training will be provided to ensure that all TLO understand the coaching model, the RSMC, the pedagogies, and the teaching strategies required for the revised curriculum. TLO will need to demonstrate a commitment to their role as change agents within the education sector

Key Responsibilities:

The Secondary Mathematics TLO will:

  • Coaching/mentoring School Staff and students to become competent, engaged stakeholders in using the RSMC and related teaching and learning approaches.
  • Collaborating with the CAS Secondary Mathematics Team to develop and model practical units and lessons based on the RSMC’s teaching strategies.
  • Supporting School Staff in the development of teaching and learning resources that are contextually appropriate with real life connections.
  • Providing professional development and supporting School Staff to provide professional development for school staff, as required.
  • Supporting SEA and District Education Advisors (EA) in their monitoring and oversight of delivery of secondary school mathematics
  • Collecting and evaluating data – including applying PM Benchmark assessments and Mathematics Diagnostic during pre and post assessments (training will be provided).
  • Assisting School Staff to understand, plan and implement differentiated teaching and learning strategies through their planning and practice -including students that are at-risk, those with a disability and those that are gifted.
  • Communicating with stakeholders, the CAS Secondary Mathematics Team and respective CAS Officers.
  • Performing other duties as required by the Mathematics Coordinator (Secondary) and SEA within the parameters of this Terms of Reference

Key Deliverables:

  • Supporting Focus Schools to build mathematics department teaching capacity for improved learning outcomes
  • Supporting Focus Schools for leading cluster professional development activities for secondary mathematics
  • Developing positive working partnerships with School Staff, SEA, EA, the CAS Secondary Mathematics Team and relevant MOE staff.
  • Supporting the design and delivery of high-quality teaching resources and training
  • Acting as a trusted adviser in building knowledge and capacity of counterparts

Key Working Relationships:

  • The Secondary Mathematics TLO will be accountable to the Coordinator Mathematics Curriculum (Secondary).
  • Curriculum Advisory Services (CAS) Maths Specialists
  • District SEA and EA
  • Heads of Schools, Heads of Department (HODs)
  • Relevant teachers within the Ministry of Education (MOE)

Selection Criteria:

Qualifications

  • A minimum of bachelor’s degree in education with a major in Mathematics or a bachelor’s degree in mathematics with a secondary education teaching diploma, or equivalent

Experience

  • Demonstrable knowledge and experience of student-centered pedagogy is a requirement
  • Comprehensive understanding of teaching and learning for children across a variety of abilities across secondary education years
  • Capacity to model and present confidently in classroom situations and in working with teaching staff.
  • Excellent communication skills and ability to build positive relationships
  • Computer skills for planning, communication and recording data
  • Fiji Teachers Registration Authority (FTRA) registration is a requirement
  • At least 3 years school experience as a teacher in secondary schools
  • Recent experience in the past 5 years of teaching mathematics is desirable

Skills and Knowledge

  • Knowledge of numeracy teaching and learning strategies and procedures and how to apply them effectively in the classroom.
  • Understanding of teaching and learning for children across a variety of year levels and with diverse learning needs.
  • Understanding of how to work in a child safe and child friendly environment.
  • Understanding of cultural sensitivity, gender equity, violence against women, people with disabilities, child protection, environment.
  • Demonstrated ability to develop and share a vision and deliver strategic approach.
  • Sensitivity to other cultures and the ability to act appropriately in the context of Fijian culture and the workplace
  • Ability to work according to agreed principles and model the Abt/Platform’s principles including transparency, accountability, fairness, and collaboration.
  • Strong communication and interpersonal skills.
  • Committed to coaching, mentoring and a team player.
  • A demonstrated commitment to child protection and the prevention of Sexual Exploitation, Abuse and Harassment (PSEAH) and a robust fraud control and anti-corruption environment.
  • Ability to plan and organise work systematically and meet deadlines.

Please apply online by submitting a cover letter addressing how you meet the requirements of this role and an up-to-date comprehensive CV.

title: Staff Research Scientist
description:
As a Staff Researcher, you will work on research questions that most AI labs simply do not have access to. ServiceNow AI Research is chartered to build the future of enterprise agentic AI, from a rare vantage point: we see how agents actually behave, inside complex enterprise environments, at scale.

You will contribute to research initiatives on how agents accumulate and reuse tacit knowledge, learn and improve continuously, and on their resilience, their safety, and the privacy of the data they handle. These are the real obstacles to enterprise agentic deployment today, and they surface in operational reality well before they appear in the literature.

While much of the AI and NLP community concentrates on core agent capabilities, our team explores the dimensions that determine real adoption: safety mechanisms, threat detection, privacy guarantees, and responsible AI practices. You will have the freedom to publish and advance the state of the art, with the rare advantage of testing your hypotheses against real deployments rather than against benchmarks.

  • PhD in computer science, machine learning, or a related field, or equivalent research experience
  • 2 or more years of research experience post-PhD, a significant portion of it in an industrial setting or in direct contact with deployed systems
  • Established publication record at top-tier venues (NeurIPS, ICML, ICLR, ACL, EMNLP, or equivalents), with contributions recognized as influential in your field
  • Demonstrated track record of setting/executing research agenda, not only executing one: you have chosen problems before the community turned to them, and you can explain why
  • Experience working on cross-disciplinary teams or projects collaborating with researchers and engineers
  • Strong software development skills: you write, maintain, and optimize high-quality research code, and you know what it takes for a result to survive the move into production
  • Advanced use of agentic tools in your own research practice, and a willingness to advance the team's practices in this area
  • Demonstrated ability to influence technical decisions beyond your own team, particularly with product and engineering teams
  • Excellent communication skills, including the ability to explain complex technical work to non-specialist audiences and to executives

Nice to have

  • Expertise in one or more of the following areas: agent memory and tacit knowledge, continual learning, safety and alignment, security and threat detection, privacy, agent evaluation
  • Experience with AI systems operating in real enterprise environments, with the compliance, governance, and scale constraints that entails
  • Contributions to open source software, datasets, or evaluation benchmarks used by the community
  • Scientific service roles: program committees, editorial work, workshop organization
  • Academic collaborations or supervision of doctoral students

For positions in this location, we offer a base pay of $202,500 - $354,400, plus equity (when applicable), variable/incentive compensation and benefits. Please note that the base pay shown is a guideline, and individual total compensation will vary based on factors such as qualifications, skill level, competencies, and work location. We also offer health plans, including flexible spending accounts, a 401(k) Plan with company match, ESPP, matching donations, a flexible time away plan and family leave programs. description:

As the tallest building west of Chicago, InterContinental Los Angeles Downtown will forever elevate the city skyline. Live, InterContinental Los Angeles Downtown leads the way as the new architectural icon of luxury hospitality.

The hotel features 889 guest rooms including 109 suites, and a host of culinary venues, including La Boucherie, an elegant American steakhouse with a French twist; lively Lobby Bar; and Spire 73 – the tallest open-air rooftop bar in the Western Hemisphere – located atop the 73rd floor, boasting breathtaking 360-degree views.

Bedecked in sustainable design, the hotel is the first LEED-Gold certified building in downtown Los Angeles for Building Design and Construction.

From intricate light fixtures inspired by L.A.’s infamous freeways to billboard-inspired headboards in each guest room reflecting L.A.’s classic beach towns, foothills, car culture and urban scene, the hotel aims to bring a fresh, iconic and elevated perspective of Los Angeles to travelers and locals alike.

title: Fire Module Leader
description:
About BurnBot


BurnBot provides systematic fuels treatment services to prevent destructive wildfires. We're firefighters, scientists, engineers, prescribed fire practitioners, ecologists, and community members who are answering the call to scale fuel treatment capacity. Our modern fuel treatment system recognizes and supports conservation efforts with a clean, smoke-free process. We need technology to amplify our workforces with targeted use of synthetic fire to treat fuel loads 10x faster than previously possible.


The Role


BurnBot is seeking a Fire Module Leader to lead fire/field crews executing wildfire, prescribed fire, UAS, DSI and related fire operations. The Foreman is responsible for direct supervision of Fire Module personnel, day-to-day operational execution, and field-level leadership across all aspects of the BurnBot Fire Program, as well as cross-vertical projects.

Preference will be given to individuals able to be based out of the Medford, OR or Placerville, CA Hub locations. However, all candidates will be considered regardless of their working location.

This role is hands-on and field-based. The Fire Module Leader works alongside crews while maintaining responsibility for safety, work quality, productivity, equipment readiness, and compliance with project plans and regulatory requirements. This position serves as the primary link between field execution and the supervisory Fire Operations Specialist.

This is a non-exempt role with an hourly rate $45-$56. Placement within the range depends on experience, certifications, and skills.


Essential Duties and Responsibilities

  • Directly supervises the Lead Fire Module Crewmember (1) and Fire Module Crewmembers (3) in daily field activities conducted in support of Fire Program projects (prescribed fire, wildfire, RX2 operations, DSI, UAS flights, and others).

  • Assign tasks, sequence work, and manage crew pacing to meet safety, quality, and productivity expectations

  • Provide real-time coaching, feedback, and corrective direction as needed

  • Ensure work is executed according to project scope, burn plans, wildfire mobilization standard operating procedures, and company standards

  • Identify hazards, manage risk, and exercise stop-work authority when conditions warrant

  • Maintain advanced proficiency in engine, RX2 machine, chainsaw, DSI, UAV, heavy equipment and other assigned operations within training and qualifications.

  • Ensure equipment, tools, and vehicles are staged, maintained, and used correctly; communicate equipment needs, failures, and logistical issues to Fire Operations Specialist or Fire Staff

  • Other duties as assigned


Required Qualifications

  • Ability to travel extensively (up to 75%)

  • Valid driver's license and ability to be insured under company policy (this role requires driving company vehicles and trailers to remote job sites)

  • 5+ years of experience in wildland fire, fuels mitigation, vegetation management, or prescribed fire operations

  • Demonstrated experience leading crews in field operations

  • Strong working knowledge of field safety practices and regulatory compliance

  • Physical ability to perform demanding field work (lifting up to 50 lbs, uneven terrain, long days outdoors)

  • NWCG qualified ENGB or CRWB


Desired Qualifications

  • Any of the following certifications: FIRB, RXB3/2/1, CRWB, ENGB, ICT5/4/3

  • Valid Class B Commercial Drivers License

  • Experience operating farm, forestry, or other heavy equipment, trucks and large trailers

  • Experience coordinating multi-crew or multi-equipment operations

  • FAA Part 107 certification

  • NFPA Certified Wildfire Mitigation Specialist


Still interested? Please apply at or by sending your resume to careers@burnbot.com.


Physical requirements and working conditions

This position is performed primarily outdoors at active fuels treatment and prescribed fire sites. Essential functions include: walking, standing, bending, kneeling, and climbing on uneven, steep, or unimproved terrain for extended periods; working full shifts in variable and adverse conditions, including heat, cold, wind, dust, and smoke; operating, carrying, and maintaining hand and power tools, including chainsaws; lifting and carrying up to 50 pounds, with or without reasonable accommodation, and occasionally more with assistance; wearing required personal protective equipment for the duration of the shift, including fire-resistant clothing, hard hat, hearing and eye protection, gloves, and safety footwear; maintaining situational awareness and communicating clearly by radio in high-noise environments; and traveling by vehicle and by air to remote sites, including overnight and multi-day assignments.

BurnBot provides reasonable accommodation to enable qualified individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions of this role. To request an accommodation, contact careers@burnbot.com or (415) 795-9124 x 1010.

title: Miami - American Red Cross First Aid/CPR/AED Instructor/ Instructor Trainer
description:
About Us

At ALLCPR, we are committed to elevating community health and safety standards nationwide. We operate at more than 200 locations across the United States, providing American Heart Association Basic Life Support courses, American Red Cross First Aid/CPR/AED and Basic Life Support courses, and related CPR and life-saving training programs.

With an annual training volume of more than 80,000 participants, ALLCPR stands for the belief that all of us should learn CPR. It is our mission to ensure that everyone has the knowledge and skills to save lives.

Our Work Environment Includes

The Instructor will teach American Red Cross First Aid/CPR/AED courses and train students through the American Red Cross.﻿

The Instructor Trainer will be responsible for teaching American Red Cross First Aid/CPR/AED Instructor courses, training instructor candidates to become certified American Red Cross instructors.

The Instructor Trainer will prepare for training sessions, demonstrate proper techniques, and evaluate candidates' performance to ensure they have achieved proficiency.

The Instructor Trainer will work in various settings, including offices, schools, community centers, hospitals, and other locations.

Note: The Instructor Trainer's teaching methods and content must comply with American Red Cross requirements.

License / Certification

  • American Red Cross First Aid/CPR/AED Instructor Certification, r.25 — Required if you are looking for an instructor role
  • American Red Cross First Aid/CPR/AED Instructor Trainer Certification, r.25 — Required﻿ ﻿if you are looking for an instructor trainer role
  • American Red Cross BLS Instructor Trainer Certification — Preferred
  • American Heart Association BLS Instructor Certification — Preferred
  • Other equivalent Instructor Trainer certifications may be considered where an approved bridging pathway is available; we can provide bridging guidance.

Teaching Equipment

The Instructor Trainer must own at least 3 manikin sets.

Key Responsibilities

  • Prepare for American Red Cross First Aid/CPR/AED courses.
  • Deliver instructor-level training sessions to individuals or groups.
  • Demonstrate proper CPR/AED techniques that comply with American Red Cross requirements.
  • Provide feedback to candidates to help them improve their performance.
  • Monitor and evaluate candidate progress to ensure proficiency.
  • Complete and submit course records in accordance with American Red Cross requirements.
  • Ensure training materials are up-to-date and comply with relevant program requirements.
  • Participate in ongoing professional development to stay current with CPR and AED training best practices.
  • Provide excellent customer service to clients and candidates.

Requirements

  • Current American Red Cross First Aid/CPR/AED Instructor certification.
  • Strong knowledge of CPR and AED techniques and best practices.
  • Excellent communication and interpersonal skills.
  • Ability to prepare and deliver effective training sessions.

title: Philanthropic Engagement Officer, Major Gifts
company: Lutheran School of Theology at Chicago
description:
Our Advancement team is vital to the mission of the Lutheran School of Theology at Chicago (LSTC), cultivating relationships and philanthropic partnerships that sustain theological education and help LSTC respond faithfully and creatively to the needs of church and world. Through this work, the Philanthropic Engagement Officer will invite donors into deeper relationship with LSTC's mission and help secure the resources necessary for the institution and its students to thrive for generations to come.


LSTC's commitments to justice, inclusion, and care for the whole createion shape not only what we teach, but how we understand community, stewardship, partnership, and philanthropy.


LSTC is seeking a relational, strategic, and results-oriented Philanthropic Engagement Officer to strengthen and expand the institution's major-gifts program.


Reporting to the Vice President for Advancement, the Philanthropic Engagement Officer will build authentic relationships with individuals who have the capacity and desire to make significant philanthropic investments in LSTC's mission. The PEO will manage a portfolio of approximately 100-125 qualified major-gift prospects, guiding relationships thoughtfully from identification and qualification through cultivation, solicitation, and stewardship. The position is expected to secure approximately $500,000-$750,000 in gifts annually, with particular attention to donors capable of making gifts of $5,000 to $250,000 or more.


This position will play an important role in The Campaign for LSTC – Phase II while helping establish a sustainable major-gifts program that extends beyond the campaign. Success requires equal parts relationship building, disciplined portfolio management, compelling communication, collaboration, and the ability to connect a donor's philanthropic aspirations with LSTC's mission and future.


This is a hybrid position with approximately 30% travel. When not traveling on behalf of LSTC, the position ordinarily works on campus two days per week.


Key Responsibilities

  • Major Gift Fundraising: Manage an active portfolio of approximately 100-125 qualified prospects, developing individualized strategies that lead to meaningful philanthropic engagement and gifts generally ranging from $5,000 to $250,000 or more. Work toward an annual fundraising goal of approximately $500,000-$750,000.
  • Donor Relationships: Build authentic, sustained relationships with donors and prospective donors by developing a deep understanding of their interests, motivations, values, and philanthropic aspirations. Create opportunities for them to connect meaningfully with LSTC's students, faculty, programs, leadership, and mission.
  • Cultivation & Solicitation: Design and execute personalized cultivation and solicitation strategies, including face-to-face and virtual donor visits, substantive engagement opportunities, proposals, and formal gift solicitations.
  • Prospect & Portfolio Management: Use a disciplined moves-management process to advance prospects through qualification, cultivation, solicitation, and stewardship. Maintain clear strategies, next steps, and timelines for portfolio relationships and accurately document donor activity in Raiser's Edge NXT and campaign strategy in Asana.
  • Stewardship & Donor Care: Ensure that donors experience timely, meaningful, and personalized stewardship. Share the impact of their generosity and cultivate sustained relationships that encourage continued giving, deeper engagement, and, when appropriate, consideration of planned gifts.
  • Campaign Engagement: Support the goals and priorities of The Campaign for LSTC – Phase II by partnering with Advancement colleagues, institutional leaders, campaign volunteers, and other ambassadors to cultivate and solicit prospective donors. Participate in campaign events and contribute to proposals and donor-facing materials.
  • Strategic Partnership: Collaborate closely with the Vice President for Advancement and colleagues across LSTC to strengthen the major-gift pipeline, identify emerging philanthropic opportunities, and develop strategies that advance institutional priorities.
  • Constituency Engagement: Represent LSTC at alumni gatherings, ELCA and Lutheran church events, donor meetings, and other gatherings that create opportunities to deepen relationships and introduce new people to LSTC's mission.
  • Analysis & Accountability: Monitor portfolio health, pipeline movement, donor engagement, solicitations, commitments, and revenue. Provide regular reporting and use data to refine fundraising strategies, identify opportunities, and responsibly steward LSTC's advancement resources.
  • Community Participation: Participate as an engaged member of the LSTC community, contributing to a collaborative culture rooted in hospitality, mutual respect, justice, care for the whole creation, and shared commitment to LSTC's mission.

title: VP of Operations Excellence
location: Grease Monkey International LLC - Greenwood Village, CO 80111
description:
Department: Operations

Reports To: COO

Exempt/Full-time

Based out of Denver, CO (DTC) with up to 50% travel commitment

We're looking for a VP of Operations Excellence who brings deep experience in process improvement, change management, and leading large-scale operational initiatives. This role is focused on building scalable processes, implementing solutions, and driving meaningful change across growing, multi-location organization. The ideal candidate knows how to turn strategy into execution, lead cross-functional initiatives, and ensure improvements are successfully adopted and sustained in the field.

_________________

POSITION SUMMARY:

FullSpeed Automotive is one of the largest and fastest-growing multi-brand automotive service platform companies in the country, operating thousands of locations across a portfolio of iconic brands. As we continue to scale, operational consistency, efficiency, and disciplined execution are critical to driving sustainable business performance.

The VP of Operations Excellence leads the operational infrastructure, services, and capabilities that enable consistent execution and performance across the organization. This role oversees key areas of operational reporting, process improvement, systems and tool implementation, and operational support, partnering closely with Field Operations and cross-functional leaders to simplify how work gets done and ensure the field has the tools, insights, and processes needed to perform effectively.

This is a hands-on leadership role responsible for taking operational initiatives from opportunity identification and design through implementation, adoption, and measurable results. The VP of Operations Excellence will use data and analytics to identify trends, challenge assumptions, measure impact, and ensure operational improvements translate into meaningful business outcomes.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES:

Operational Services & Performance

  • Identify and prioritize opportunities to improve operational efficiency, consistency, profitability, customer experience, and field execution across the organization.
  • Partner with Field Operations to develop and standardize scalable processes, tools, and best practices that simplify execution and support consistent performance across locations.
  • Evaluate operational challenges, identify root causes, and develop practical solutions that can be effectively implemented at the center level.
  • Establish and monitor key operational performance indicators, including car count, ARO, technician efficiency, bay utilization, parts fill rate, and customer satisfaction, to identify opportunities and measure the impact of improvement initiatives.
  • Leverage operational data, reporting, and field insights to identify trends, bottlenecks, and performance opportunities across locations, regions, and service lines.
  • Drive a culture of continuous improvement through disciplined evaluation of processes, results, and opportunities for ongoing improvement.

Implementation & Process Execution

  • Lead cross-functional implementation of new operational processes, systems, tools, and ways of working from design through rollout, adoption, and sustained execution in the field.
  • Build and manage implementation roadmaps, including timelines, ownership, resources, risks, communication, and success measures for multi-location initiatives.
  • Partner with IT, Finance, Field Operations, Training, Customer Experience, and other functions to ensure operational initiatives are practical, aligned with business needs, and deliver measurable results.
  • Establish effective change management, communication, and training practices to support successful adoption and reinforce new processes after implementation.
  • Evaluate the effectiveness of implemented solutions and make adjustments based on performance results and field feedback.

Operational Insights & Reporting

  • Ensure leaders have clear, reliable, and actionable visibility into operational performance through meaningful KPIs, dashboards, and reporting cadences.
  • Translate operational data into clear insights, recommendations, and priorities for field and executive leadership.
  • Partner with appropriate teams to improve reporting infrastructure, automation, data quality, and accessibility while reducing unnecessary manual reporting.
  • Establish consistent standards for operational reporting and measurement across the organization.

Team & Stakeholder Leadership

  • Build, lead, mentor, and develop a high-performing Operations Excellence team with clear ownership, accountability, and priorities.
  • Serve as a strategic partner between Operations and key cross-functional teams, ensuring alignment around operational priorities and execution.
  • Influence leaders across the organization to drive adoption, accountability, and sustained operational improvement.
  • Present recommendations, business cases, performance insights, and initiative progress to senior leadership and the board as needed.

Operational Strategy & Scalability

  • Advise the COO and executive team on operational performance, risks, opportunities, and priorities.
  • Develop and lead the Operations Excellence roadmap aligned with company strategy, growth plans, and operational priorities.
  • Evaluate processes, tools, systems, and operating practices to identify opportunities to increase efficiency, scalability, and business performance.
  • Ensure operational initiatives connect to broader business objectives and deliver measurable value to the organization.

QUALIFICATIONS:

  • Education: High school diploma or equivalent; Bachelor’s degree in Business, Operations, Analytics, Finance, or a related field preferred. Relevant education and/or equivalent years of professional experience considered.
  • Experience:
    • 10–12 years of progressive experience in operations, operations support/services, operational excellence, business transformation, or a related field, including 5+ years of leadership experience.
    • Demonstrated success improving operational performance through scalable processes, tools, systems, and support solutions that deliver measurable business results.
    • Proven experience supporting a large, multi-location or distributed field organization and developing solutions that balance enterprise consistency with practical field execution.
    • Demonstrated success leading complex, cross-functional initiatives from strategy and design through implementation, adoption, and sustained execution.
    • Strong understanding of operational KPIs, performance reporting, and business intelligence, with the ability to use data and field insights to identify opportunities, inform decisions, and measure results.
    • Experience with business intelligence tools such as Tableau, Power BI, or Looker preferred; familiarity with DMS/POS platforms and shop-level performance metrics is a plus.
    • Experience in automotive services, multi-site retail, fleet, dealership, or another distributed field-based operation preferred.
    • Proven ability to lead and develop high-performing teams while driving accountability and results across functions.
    • Strong executive communication and presentation skills with the ability to translate operational challenges and complex information into clear recommendations and actionable solutions; experience working with C-suite, ownership, or board-level stakeholders preferred.
    • Strong project, program, and change management capabilities; Lean, Six Sigma, PMP, or similar certification preferred.
  • Travel: Ability and willingness to travel up to 50% for site visits, operational meetings, and company events.
  • Physical Requirements: This position requires the ability to remain stationary while working on a computer and communicating via phone, video conferencing, and email, as well as move throughout the workplace and various centers during visits, with or without reasonable accommodations.

WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE:

  • Operational Performance: Operational improvements drive measurable gains in efficiency, consistency, profitability, customer experience, and overall business performance.
  • Scalable Operations: Processes, tools, and operating practices are simplified, standardized, and scalable across a growing multi-location organization.
  • Sustained Execution: Operational initiatives move successfully from concept through implementation and become embedded in day-to-day field execution.
  • Continuous Improvement: Operational challenges are proactively identified, root causes are addressed, and solutions are continuously refined based on results and field feedback.
  • Actionable Visibility: Leaders have clear, reliable performance insights that enable faster decisions, stronger accountability, and focused action.
  • Cross-Functional Alignment: Operations and key business partners are aligned around priorities, ownership, execution, and measurable outcomes.
  • Team Effectiveness: The Operations Excellence team has clear accountability, strong capabilities, and consistently delivers against the organization’s highest operational priorities.

The anticipated base salary range for this position is $130k–$150k annually, based on experience and qualifications. This position is also eligible for a performance-based bonus. Full-time employees are eligible for benefits, including medical, dental, and vision insurance; a 401(k) plan; paid time off; and paid holidays. Applications will be reviewed on a rolling basis, with an anticipated closing date of October 28, 2026.   • Et professionelt værksted, hvor du har ordentligt udstyr til at udføre dit arbejde.
  • Kurser og efteruddannelse, så du løbende kan udvikle dig inden for dit fag.
  • Gode kolleger, hvor man hjælper hinanden og løser opgaverne sammen.
  • En stor og veletableret organisation, der investerer i sine medarbejdere og værksteder.
  • Gode udviklingsmuligheder, hvis du på sigt får lyst til nye opgaver, mere ansvar eller en anden stilling internt.


Arbejdsopgaver

Du kommer til at arbejde med skadereparationer på varevogne, hvor opgaverne spænder fra mindre buler og udskiftning af karrosseridele til større skader, der kræver mere omfattende opretning.

Dine opgaver bliver blandt andet:

  • Reparation og opretning af karrosseriskader på varevogne
  • Udskiftning og tilpasning af karrosseridele
  • Afmontering og montering af karrosseridele og tilhørende komponenter
  • Svejsearbejde og øvrigt pladearbejde
  • Kontrol af det udførte arbejde, inden bilen går videre i processen


Hvem søger vi?

Vi søger dig, der er uddannet pladesmed eller karrosseritekniker.

Du kommer måske fra et personvognsskadecenter og har lyst til at prøve noget nyt, eller du har allerede erfaring med varevogne.

Det vigtigste er, at du har styr på dit håndværk, kan arbejde selvstændigt og går op i at levere et ordentligt stykke arbejde.

Du skal samtidig have lyst til at være en del af et værksted, hvor man hjælper hinanden og tager ansvar for de opgaver, der skal løses.


Praktisk information

Ansættelse: Fast fuldtidsstilling med direkte ansættelse hos virksomheden.

Vil du høre mere?

Du behøver ikke skrive en ansøgning eller have dit CV klar.

Send dit navn og telefonnummer til Glostrup-M@jobteam.dk og skriv “Karosseritekniker varevogn”, så ringer vi dig op og fortæller mere om jobbet.

Du er også velkommen til at ringe direkte på 21541034.

Vi tager samtaler løbende og ansætter, så snart vi har fundet den rette.

Stillingen er ikke et vikariat. Rekrutteringen håndteres af os, men du bliver ansat direkte hos virksomheden.


Sådan foregår rekrutteringen

Vi er rekrutteringspartner på stillingen og har til opgave at finde og præsentere relevante kandidater for virksomheden. Som en del af den opgave annoncerer vi jobbet uden virksomhedens navn og står for den indledende dialog med kandidaterne.

I den første del af processen er du som kandidat også anonym. Vi præsenterer dit CV for virksomheden uden navn og personlige oplysninger.

Hvis virksomheden gerne vil møde dig, fortæller vi dig, hvilken virksomhed det drejer sig om.

Herefter bestemmer du selv, om du ønsker at gå videre til en samtale. Først når du har sagt ja, deler vi dit navn og dine kontaktoplysninger med virksomheden.

Er du allerede i job, kan du derfor også undersøge en ny mulighed fortroligt, uden at din identitet bliver delt med virksomheden fra starten.

title: Automation Controls Specialist - Farm
description:
Forsman Farms is seeking an experienced Automation Controls Specialist to develop, support, troubleshoot, and improve the automation systems used throughout our farm operations. This position helps ensure our automated processes are reliable, efficient, and easy to operate and maintain.


This position is approximately 90% office-based and 10% field-based. The role works closely with operations, maintenance, electrical, management, and other departments to understand problems and opportunities and turn them into simple, intuitive, and reliable automation solutions.


Key Responsibilities:

  • Support, troubleshoot, maintain, and improve PLCs, HMIs, SCADA systems, VFDs, instrumentation, sensors, and other automation and control systems.
  • Work with operations, maintenance, electrical, and other departments to identify problems, understand needs, and develop practical solutions.
  • Program, modify, and troubleshoot control systems and automation applications.
  • Develop and maintain user interfaces and control solutions that are intuitive, reliable, and easy to operate and troubleshoot.
  • Troubleshoot communication and connectivity issues between control systems, equipment, and devices.
  • Support system upgrades, testing, commissioning, startup, and implementation of new automation solutions.
  • Provide remote and field-based troubleshooting and technical support as needed.
  • Identify opportunities to improve system reliability, efficiency, functionality, and ease of use.
  • Document system changes, troubleshooting activities, and other technical information as needed.
  • Use sound judgment when troubleshooting critical issues, including knowing when to involve others or seek additional support.

Qualifications:

  • Industrial controls and automation programming experience.
  • Experience with Allen-Bradley Studio 5000.
  • Experience with Inductive Automation's Ignition Vision and Perspective.
  • Working knowledge of industrial communications, such as Modbus, EtherNet/IP, or BACnet.
  • Ability to read electrical schematics and troubleshoot control systems.
  • Strong problem-solving and communication skills with the ability to work effectively with both technical and non-technical team members.
  • Experience with Python scripting, SQL/databases, industrial networking, VFDs, instrumentation, and electrical troubleshooting is helpful but not required.
  • Relevant field experience and demonstrated controls and automation ability are acceptable in place of formal education.


Resumen del Puesto

Forsman Farms busca un Especialista en Automatización y Controles con experiencia para desarrollar, brindar soporte, diagnosticar y mejorar los sistemas de automatización utilizados en nuestras operaciones agrícolas. Estos sistemas incluyen ventilación de los gallineros, alimentación, iluminación, recolección de huevos, manejo de estiércol y otros procesos automatizados.


Este puesto es aproximadamente 90% en oficina y 10% en campo. La persona en este puesto trabajará en estrecha colaboración con los equipos de operaciones, mantenimiento, electricidad, gerencia y otros departamentos para comprender problemas y oportunidades, y convertirlos en soluciones de automatización simples, intuitivas y confiables.


Responsabilidades principales:

  • Brindar soporte, diagnosticar, mantener y mejorar PLC, HMI, sistemas SCADA, VFD, instrumentación, sensores y otros sistemas de automatización y control.
  • Trabajar con los equipos de operaciones, mantenimiento, electricidad y otros departamentos para identificar problemas, comprender necesidades y desarrollar soluciones prácticas.
  • Programar, modificar y diagnosticar sistemas de control y aplicaciones de automatización.
  • Desarrollar y mantener interfaces de usuario y soluciones de control que sean intuitivas, confiables y fáciles de operar y diagnosticar.
  • Diagnosticar problemas de comunicación y conectividad entre sistemas de control, equipos y dispositivos.
  • Brindar soporte en actualizaciones de sistemas, pruebas, puesta en marcha, arranque e implementación de nuevas soluciones de automatización.
  • Proporcionar soporte técnico y diagnóstico de problemas de forma remota y en campo, según sea necesario.
  • Identificar oportunidades para mejorar la confiabilidad, eficiencia, funcionalidad y facilidad de uso de los sistemas.
  • Documentar cambios en los sistemas, actividades de diagnóstico y otra información técnica según sea necesario.
  • Utilizar buen criterio al atender problemas críticos, incluyendo saber cuándo involucrar a otras personas o solicitar apoyo adicional.

Requisitos:

  • Experiencia en controles industriales y programación de sistemas de automatización.
  • Experiencia con Allen-Bradley Studio 5000.
  • Experiencia con Inductive Automation Ignition Vision y Perspective.
  • Conocimientos prácticos de sistemas de comunicación industrial, como Modbus, EtherNet/IP o BACnet.
  • Capacidad para leer diagramas eléctricos y diagnosticar problemas en sistemas de control.
  • Fuertes habilidades para resolver problemas y comunicarse eficazmente con miembros de equipos técnicos y no técnicos.
  • Se prefiere, pero no es obligatorio, tener experiencia con programación en Python, SQL/bases de datos, redes industriales, VFD, instrumentación y diagnóstico de problemas eléctricos.
  • La experiencia relevante en el campo y la capacidad demostrada en controles y automatización pueden sustituir la educación formal.

title: Senior Substation Engineer (P. Eng.)
description:
Your new role

As our new Senior Substation Engineer, you will be the technical anchor and subject matter expert for medium and high voltage substation design projects across a diverse and growing Canadian and cross-border client base. You will lead engineering efforts from early concept and feasibility through detailed design and construction support, working closely with project managers, clients, and multidisciplinary design teams.

Your role will combine hands-on engineering with mentorship and technical leadership, helping to elevate the quality of our substation practice while delivering on a pipeline of challenging, high-profile projects.

Your key responsibilities will be:

Lead and perform electrical engineering design for medium and high voltage substation projects, including equipment specification and selection, single-line development, protection and control design, and layout optimization

Develop and review technical reports, engineering specifications, calculations, and design packages for substation facilities

Perform and review electrical engineering calculations, including short circuit analysis, overcurrent protection coordination, and arc flash studies using industry-standard software

Develop substation relay settings and protection schemes, ensuring compliance with applicable utility and interconnection requirements

Provide engineering support during construction, including shop drawing review, RFI responses, site inspections, and punch list development

Serve as technical reviewer and quality lead for work products developed by other engineers, ensuring compliance with the Canadian Electrical Code (CSA C22.1), IEEE/ANSI standards, and applicable provincial utility requirements

Contribute to the on-going development of substation standards to improve the efficiency of future projects

Mentor and develop early- and mid-career engineers, delegating appropriately and supporting their professional growth

Support preparation of engineering proposals and fee estimates, contributing technical depth to business development efforts

Coordinate with civil, structural, and protection and control disciplines to ensure integrated, constructible designs

Your new team

You will be part of an elite team of power system engineers and play a pivotal role in delivering advanced solutions for a wide variety of clients, including energy-intensive industries like semiconductor manufacturing, municipal entities, data center mega campuses, and pioneers in renewable energy. With our substantial growth, seize the opportunity to shape our strategy and contribute to our agile team's rich pipeline of projects.

With growth horizons in cutting-edge domains like HVDC, solar photovoltaics, and offshore wind, our energetic and inventive team, bolstered by global specialists, is committed to advancing Ramboll's reach across North America, notably in provinces and states championing progressive climate objectives and sustainability measures. At the heart of our mission is the conviction that electricity is the cornerstone of the green transition toward a carbon-neutral future. Join us in our unwavering pursuit to realize this vision.

About you

From the moment you start at Ramboll, we will support your personal and professional development so that you can continue to grow with the company. While we look forward to supporting your continued learning and development, for this role we have identified some qualifications, skills, and capabilities that will set you up for success.

These include:

Bachelor's degree in Electrical Engineering or Electrical Engineering Technology; Master's degree a plus

8+ years of progressive experience in substation engineering and design, with demonstrated ability to lead technical efforts on complex projects

Strong working knowledge of medium and high voltage equipment, substation layout, protection and control systems, and applicable industry codes and standards (CSA C22.1, IEEE/ANSI, and provincial utility requirements)

Proficiency in engineering calculation software for short circuit, protection coordination, and arc flash analysis (such as ETAP, SKM, or EasyPower)

Experience with Autodesk AutoCAD, Revit MEP, or Microstation for substation design and documentation

Professional Engineer (P.Eng.) license in good standing with a Canadian provincial or territorial engineering regulator (PEO preferred), or active pursuit of licensure, is strongly preferred

Strong communication and client-facing skills, with the ability to explain technical positions clearly to varied audiences

Experience with utility interconnection requirements and standards, including cross-border US/Canada projects, is a plus

Substation Protection Engineering or Substation Control and Integration experience is highly valued

What we can offer you

Flexible work environment

Investment in your development

Leaders you can count on, guided by our Leadership Principles

Be valued for the unique person you are

Never be short of inspiration from colleagues, clients, and projects

The long-term thinking of a foundation-owned company

Ready to join us?

​Please submit your application. Be sure to include all relevant documents including your CV, cover letter, etc.

Work at the heart of sustainable change

Ramboll is a global architecture, engineering, and consultancy company. We believe that the purpose of sustainable change is to create a thriving world for both nature and people. So, that’s where we start – and how we work. At Ramboll, our core strength is our people, and our history is rooted in a clear vision of how a responsible company should act. Being open and curious is a cornerstone of our culture. We embrace an inclusive mindset that looks for fresh, diverse, and innovative perspectives. We respect, embrace, and invite diversity in all forms to actively cultivate an environment where everyone can flourish and realize their full potential.

Where People Flourish

Our mission is to create sustainable societies where people and nature flourish. This means that a culture of inclusion is embedded in everything we do. Our people bring diverse backgrounds and experiences to the company, enabling us to deliver innovative and forward-thinking solutions to our clients. We also know how important it is to achieve the right balance of where, when, and how much you work. At Ramboll, we offer flexibility as part of our positive and inclusive approach to work. We are committed to equal employment opportunity, regardless of age, disability or medical condition, gender identity, marriage and domestic partnership, pregnancy and maternity, race, ancestry, or national origin, religion or belief, sex and sexual orientation, military service and veteran status, or any other protected characteristic. Ramboll wants to ensure opportunities are accessible to candidates with disabilities. So, please let us know if there are any changes we could make to the application process to make it more comfortable for you. You can contact us at job.advert.accessibility@ramboll.com with such requests.

Salary Transparency Statement

At Ramboll, we are committed to fair and transparent compensation practices that support our people and our purpose of creating sustainable societies. The anticipated base salary range for this position is $92,000 to $130,000 per year. This range reflects the compensation we reasonably expect to offer at the time of posting. Actual compensation will vary based on factors such as location, skills, experience, education, and internal equity. Because we operate across multiple U.S. markets, pay may differ depending on the cost of labor in specific locations. In addition to base salary, this position may be eligible for bonus, overtime or other forms of compensation and we offer a comprehensive benefits package that supports well-being, professional development, and work-life balance. title: Senior Staff AI Scientist
description:
Intuit Credit Karma is looking for a results-oriented and strategically innovative Senior Staff AI Scientist to lead the evolution of our recommendation engines from static eligibility matching to dynamic, intent-aware personalization. You will architect the systems that determine which financial products are shown to 100M+ members, balancing immediate monetization with long-term member trust.

As the Tech Lead, you will drive the technical vision for our user understanding and recommendation stacks. You will mentor junior scientists, set the standard for experimental rigor, and partner with senior leadership and product teams to define the future of our members’ financial journey.


Responsibilities

  • Lead the design and evolution of ML models that understand user intent, financial journeys, and engagement patterns, powering recommendation and ranking systems across Intuit Credit Karma's financial product ecosystem.
  • Serve as the primary technical authority for AI Science, partnering with product to define the multi-year roadmap and collaborating with engineering to ensure models are matched by scalable, low-latency production infrastructure.
  • Act as a force multiplier — setting modeling and coding standards, conducting deep-dive reviews, and building a culture of scientific rigor across the organization.
  • Partner across the organization to identify high-impact opportunities to leverage Intuit Credit Karma's rich dataset for Personal Finance personalization, targeting, approval odds, and marketing optimization.
  • Drive revenue growth through disruptive and continuous improvements in targeting, feature engineering, user profiles, and personalization models.
  • Represent AI Science in executive and business reviews, translating complex technical work into clear business impact.
  • Represent Intuit Credit Karma externally — at conferences, speaking engagements, and meetups — as a thought leader and talent magnet.
  • Participate in research on frontier areas including deep learning, recommender systems, multi-objective optimization, and financial AI.

  • Lead and mentor a high-performing AI Science team working on large-scale projects with direct member and business impact.

Qualifications

  • MS in Computer Science, Mathematics, Statistics, Physics or a related quantitative discipline
  • 7+ years of industrial experience in Machine Learning, with 3 years in a technical lead capacity specifically focused on Ranking, Search, or Recommendation Systems.
  • Proven track record of designing and deploying high-scale, multi-stage ranking pipelines in a production environment.
  • Exceptional ability to communicate technical complexity to executive leadership and influence stakeholders across product, business and engineering.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Personalization & Ranking: Experience with multi-objective optimization and ranking systems that manage competing business and user goals.
  • Lifecycle Modeling: Familiarity with survival analysis, time-series forecasting, or sequence-to-sequence modeling to predict user actions over time.
  • Business Acumen: Ability to translate high-level business goals into rigorous mathematical objective functions.
  • Communication: Exceptional ability to communicate technical concepts to non-technical stakeholders and drive organizational alignment.

Intuit provides a competitive compensation package with a strong pay for performance rewards approach. This position may be eligible for a cash bonus, equity rewards and benefits, in accordance with our applicable plans and programs (see more about our compensation and benefits at Intuit®: Careers | Benefits). Pay offered is based on factors such as job-related knowledge, skills, experience, and work location. To drive ongoing fair pay for employees, Intuit conducts regular comparisons across categories of ethnicity and gender.

The expected base pay range for this position is:
Oakland $226,000 - $306,000

title: Fire Suppression Technician
description:
JOB SUMMARY:

The purpose of the Fire Suppression Technician is to provide installation, inspection, service and/or repair of Fire Extinguishers, Emergency Exit Lights and/or any Pre-Engineered Suppression Systems including any associated Detection & Control Systems with minimal supervision.

ESSENTIAL JOB DUTIES:

  • Use required tools and test equipment such as power machines groovers, cutters, band saw, lifts, etc. to repair or replace fire extinguishers, pre-engineered systems, and/or Detection & Control systems components.
  • Comprehensive working knowledge of NFPA codes, standards, and systems such as all types of fire extinguishers, pre-engineered suppression systems and/or Detection & Control systems.
  • Troubleshoot and identify defective components of pre-engineered suppression systems.
  • Repair or replace damaged components of pre-engineered suppression systems as well as fire extinguishers and/or Detection & Control systems.
  • Communicate with internal and external customers in a professional manner.
  • Required to be punctual to required work locations and complete scheduled projects in timely manner.
  • Use Field Service Lightning to track work orders, materials needed, time on job, etc.
  • Complete documentation on work orders.
  • Understand and follow SFS’s Safety program, SDS book, Hazardous communication program, policies and procedures. Participate in weekly Toolbox talks. Employee must always know location all related safety documentation on each project.
  • Ensure company provided vehicle is clean and well maintained as required by company policies.
  • Periodically attend seminars or similar education/training sessions to stay abreast of latest technology, codes, and standards changes.
  • Other duties may be assigned.

QUALIFICATIONS:

The qualifications listed below are representative of the elements required to perform the job successfully, however in some cases, an equivalent combination of Education, Training, Certifications and Experience may meet the job qualifications.

Education, Training, Certifications:

  • High School Diploma or equivalent, required.
  • State or any required certification, preferred.

Experience, Knowledge, Skill Requirements:

  • 2 Fire Life Safety Industry experience specifically within Fire Suppression.
  • 2 years of professional computer skills.

Communication Skills:

  • Must have the ability to effectively read, write and communicate in English with employees and customers.

Other Qualifications:

  • Valid driver’s license with acceptable driving record required.
  • Must be able to comply with SFS’s Drug and Alcohol policy and Background screening requirements, which may also include customer specific requirements based on contractual agreement.
  • Must be able to travel 90% of the time.

PHYSICAL & WORK ENVIRONMENT REQUIREMENTS:

Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform Essential Job Duties.

Physical Requirements:

While performing the duties of this job, the employee is frequently required to bend, ascend and descend step stools, ladders and stairs, kneel, lift <50lbs, reach above and below shoulders, stand and walk for extended periods of time. Employee is required to see in color, close and far distances, peripheral, depth, and adjust focus. Employee will occasional be required to balance, crouch, drive, kneel, lift >50lbs, sit, stoop, twist, and work at heights.

Work Environment:

Employees will regularly be required to work outside, and be exposed to hot/cold temperatures, dust, fumes, chemicals, electrical hazards and noise. Employee will occasionally be required to work indoors in an office setting, work alone and with others. Employee must consistently wear all appropriate personal protective equipment, as required by company safety policies while visiting locations.

We are fully committed to equal opportunities for employment to all individuals regardless of race, national origin, gender, religion, sexual orientation, disability, familial status, and any other classification protected under the law. We are an Equal Opportunity, Affirmative Action employer.

While this job description is intended to be an accurate reflection of the position, management reserves the right to modify, add, or remove duties and to assign other duties as necessary.
