  • American Red Cross First Aid/CPR/AED Instructor Trainer Certification, r.25 — Required﻿ ﻿if you are looking for an instructor trainer role
  • American Red Cross BLS Instructor Trainer Certification — Preferred
  • American Heart Association BLS Instructor Certification — Preferred
  • Other equivalent Instructor Trainer certifications may be considered where an approved bridging pathway is available; we can provide bridging guidance.

Teaching Equipment

The Instructor Trainer must own at least 3 manikin sets.

Key Responsibilities

  • Prepare for American Red Cross First Aid/CPR/AED courses.
  • Deliver instructor-level training sessions to individuals or groups.
  • Demonstrate proper CPR/AED techniques that comply with American Red Cross requirements.
  • Provide feedback to candidates to help them improve their performance.
  • Monitor and evaluate candidate progress to ensure proficiency.
  • Complete and submit course records in accordance with American Red Cross requirements.
  • Ensure training materials are up-to-date and comply with relevant program requirements.
  • Participate in ongoing professional development to stay current with CPR and AED training best practices.

Requirements

  • Excellent communication and interpersonal skills.
  • Ability to prepare and deliver effective training sessions.
  • Attention to detail and the ability to provide constructive feedback to candidates.
  • Strong organizational and time-management skills.
  • High school diploma or equivalent.

  • Must be able to stand for extended periods.

Working Conditions

  • Work may be performed in various settings, including schools, community centers, hospitals, and corporate offices.

title: Intel Analyst
description:
Intel Analyst

Wage: $35.00/ hour

Position Overview

The Intelligence Analyst, Protection Services, supports the Physical Security and Service Continuity organization by identifying, assessing, and communicating risks that may impact employees, travelers, facilities, and business operations. This role is responsible for monitoring a wide range of information sources, producing timely intelligence products, and supporting incident response and crisis management activities. The ideal candidate brings strong analytical discipline, excellent written communication skills, and the ability to operate independently with sound judgment.

Key Responsibilities

Threat and Risk Monitoring

  • Monitor open-source information, global news, government alerts, and industry intelligence feeds to identify events that may affect personnel, travelers, or business operations.
  • Track emerging geopolitical, security, environmental, and operational risks and escalate relevant findings to leadership.
  • Observe publicly available online discussions and digital environments for indicators of reputational or security-related concerns involving the company, its brands, or senior leaders, using approved tools.
  • Receive and assess automated alerts generated by internal monitoring systems, conducting initial review to determine relevance and potential risk.

  • Document findings and escalate alerts that meet defined criteria to the appropriate internal partners.

Intelligence Production & Reporting

  • Produce concise, actionable intelligence summaries, alerts, and situational updates for leadership, including event overviews, assessed business impact, and recommended or completed actions.
  • Develop ad-hoc intelligence products such as risk assessment, travel briefings, and post-incident reports.
  • Maintain accuracy, clarity, and consistency across all written products.

Operational Support

  • Support crisis management teams and business leaders during incidents by providing real-time situational awareness and validated information.
  • Use the organization’s emergency notification system to support employee outreach, awareness messaging, and incident communication workflows.
  • Assist in the configuration, optimization, and maintenance of intelligence platforms, alerting tools, and monitoring systems.

  • Maintain and update operational datasets, including contact lists, asset inventories, and distribution groups to ensure accurate and timely outreach during incidents.

Collaboration and Cross-Functional Engagement

  • Partner with internal Protection Services teams, Physical Security, HR, Legal, Communications, and other stakeholders to ensure intelligence outputs align with organizational needs.
  • Contribute to the development of internal processes, documentation, and standard operating procedures.

Qualifications

Required

  • Bachelor’s degree in a relevant field or equivalent experience demonstrating strong analytical and communication skills.
  • Strong analytical and critical thinking skills, including the capacity to interpret information from multiple sources.
  • Excellent written communication skills, with the ability to produce clear and concise summaries or reports.
  • Ability to work independently, manage time effectively, and maintain consistent productivity.
  • High level of discretion and sound judgment when handling sensitive information.
  • Willingness to learn the tools and techniques used for online research and monitoring.
  • Driver Certification

title: Mobile - American Red Cross First Aid/CPR/AED Instructor/ Instructor Trainer
description:
About Us

At ALLCPR, we are committed to elevating community health and safety standards nationwide. We operate at more than 200 locations across the United States, providing American Heart Association Basic Life Support courses, American Red Cross First Aid/CPR/AED and Basic Life Support courses, and related CPR and life-saving training programs.

With an annual training volume of more than 80,000 participants, ALLCPR stands for the belief that all of us should learn CPR. It is our mission to ensure that everyone has the knowledge and skills to save lives.

Our Work Environment Includes

The Instructor will teach American Red Cross First Aid/CPR/AED courses and train students through the American Red Cross.﻿

The Instructor Trainer will be responsible for teaching American Red Cross First Aid/CPR/AED Instructor courses, training instructor candidates to become certified American Red Cross instructors.

The Instructor Trainer will prepare for training sessions, demonstrate proper techniques, and evaluate candidates' performance to ensure they have achieved proficiency.

The Instructor Trainer will work in various settings, including offices, schools, community centers, hospitals, and other locations.

Note: The Instructor Trainer's teaching methods and content must comply with American Red Cross requirements.

License / Certification

  • American Red Cross First Aid/CPR/AED Instructor Certification, r.25 — Required if you are looking for an instructor role
  • American Red Cross First Aid/CPR/AED Instructor Trainer Certification, r.25 — Required﻿ ﻿if you are looking for an instructor trainer role
  • American Red Cross BLS Instructor Trainer Certification — Preferred
  • American Heart Association BLS Instructor Certification — Preferred
  • Other equivalent Instructor Trainer certifications may be considered where an approved bridging pathway is available; we can provide bridging guidance.

Teaching Equipment

The Instructor Trainer must own at least 3 manikin sets.

Key Responsibilities

  • Prepare for American Red Cross First Aid/CPR/AED courses.
  • Deliver instructor-level training sessions to individuals or groups.
  • Demonstrate proper CPR/AED techniques that comply with American Red Cross requirements.
  • Provide feedback to candidates to help them improve their performance.
  • Monitor and evaluate candidate progress to ensure proficiency.
  • Complete and submit course records in accordance with American Red Cross requirements.
  • Ensure training materials are up-to-date and comply with relevant program requirements.
  • Participate in ongoing professional development to stay current with CPR and AED training best practices.
  • Provide excellent customer service to clients and candidates.

Requirements

  • Current American Red Cross First Aid/CPR/AED Instructor certification.
  • Strong knowledge of CPR and AED techniques and best practices.
  • Excellent communication and interpersonal skills.
  • Ability to prepare and deliver effective training sessions.
  • Attention to detail and the ability to provide constructive feedback to candidates.
  • Strong organizational and time-management skills.
  • High school diploma or equivalent.

Physical Demands

  • Must be able to stand for extended periods.
  • Must be able to lift and carry training equipment, up to 50 pounds.
  • Must be able to demonstrate proper CPR and AED techniques.

Working Conditions

  • Work may be performed in various settings, including schools, community centers, hospitals, and corporate offices.
  • Work may be performed primarily during weekends.

Salary and Benefits

Salary: $30.00 - $40.00 per teaching hour, commensurate with experience and length of working relationship with ALLCPR.

Additional Compensation: $10.00 per enrolled student. (Only for instructor trainer role)

Job Classification: 1099 Contractor or Part-Time Employee (Certain States).

Benefits

  • Flexible schedule.

Schedule

  • Day shift.
  • Weekend/Weekday availability.

Ability to Commute / Relocate

Location: Local area as per job post

Reliably commute or plan to relocate before starting work (Required).

Experience

  • Teaching: 2+ years (Preferred).

Job Type

  • Part-time
  • Contract

Work Location: In person

title: Data Platform Software Engineer
description:
Database Provisioning builds the tools that safely operate and manage the databases running in ServiceNow data centers, including RaptorDB, ServiceNow's PostgreSQL-based database. Internal operations and support teams use the CLI tools we create, and so does every automation running in a ServiceNow data center. Our challenge is to deliver high-quality solutions that run reliably, without interruption, at massive scale. Our work is fundamental to ServiceNow's reliability, reputation, and success.

We believe ease of use, quality, scale, and customer feedback are the pillars of good development. We work in a very collaborative environment with distributed teams in the US and Europe. New team members are mentored in the skills they need to become strong contributors.

What you get to do in this role

  • Build and improve snc-provision, our in-house framework that deploys, configures and operates RaptorDB (PostgreSQL) and MariaDB databases in production, including the snow CLI used by operations teams and automation, and Dojo, our fleet-wide scheduled maintenance and monitoring service.
  • Own well-scoped features from design through implementation, test automation and delivery, with guidance from senior engineers.
  • Write clean, maintainable, well-tested code, and take part in code and design reviews.
  • Automate operational tasks across a large database fleet, from configuration management to monitoring and remediation.
  • Help investigate production issues, including database crashes, backup/restore failures and performance problems, and learn to drive root-cause analysis from logs, stack traces, and system data.
  • Work with operations, support, and partner engineering teams to understand requirements and turn feedback into improvements.
  • Contribute to documentation and runbooks, and share what you learn with the team.

To be successful in this role you have

  • A solid foundation in data structures, algorithms, and object-oriented design.
  • Hands-on experience with Linux, and an interest in learning its internals.
  • Familiarity with relational databases, ideally PostgreSQL, MySQL or MariaDB, and a desire to learn how they run in production.
  • Strong problem-solving skills and curiosity about how systems fail.
  • Clear communication, and comfort working with teammates across time zones (PT, ET, CET).

Qualifications

  • Experience in leveraging or critically thinking about how to integrate AI into work processes, decision-making, or problem-solving. This may include using AI-powered tools, automating workflows, analyzing AI-driven insights, or exploring AI's potential impact on the function or industry.
  • Typically requires a bachelor's degree and a minimum of 2 years of related experience; or an advanced degree without experience; or equivalent work experience.
  • Programming experience in Ruby, Python, Go or a similar language, plus shell scripting. Ruby is preferred but not required; engineers with Python or other scripting experience pick it up quickly.
  • Experience with source control and CI/CD systems such as Git and Jenkins.
  • Nice to have: Puppet or another configuration management tool; database backups, replication or high availability; Kubernetes; AI coding tools such as Claude Code, Windsurf or Cursor.
  • Ability to work (hybrid model) out of either our San Diego, Santa Clara, or Kirkland office. Potential option to be remote.

For positions in this location, we offer a base pay of $139,700 - $216,500, plus equity (when applicable), variable/incentive compensation and benefits. Please note that the base pay shown is a guideline, and individual total compensation will vary based on factors such as qualifications, skill level, competencies, and work location. *AIM HIGH: We embody our collectively audacious goal to courageously make the most complex biologics ever attempted to protect humankind.

Summary:

This role within Technical Operations’ Capabilities & Business Operations function is critical for strengthening how Technical Operations translates strategy into executable work and builds repeatable, scalable ways of working as the organization advances toward commercialization and future growth.

This role partners closely with Technical Operations leaders and cross-functional teams across Vaxcyte to shape strategic priorities into well-defined initiatives, strengthen end-to-end business processes and operating practices, and improve execution readiness through continuous improvement. The Principal also leads select high-priority cross-functional initiatives where additional coordination, specialized expertise, or execution capacity creates the greatest business value.

The successful candidate brings a combination of business process management, operational excellence, strategy realization, and strong cross-functional execution capability. A core expectation of the role is that every initiative strengthens both business outcomes and organizational capability - building better processes, clearer governance, stronger ways of working, and reusable learning through the work itself.

Essential Functions:

Strategy Realization & Execution Readiness:

  • Partner with leaders to translate Technical Operations strategy and priorities into executable initiatives, with clear roadmaps, milestones, ownership, governance, decision rights, and measures of success.
  • Establish and apply project-shaping and execution-readiness practices so high-priority work is well defined, resourced, governed, and ready before execution begins.
  • Support demand intake and prioritization by helping leaders assess business value, readiness, dependencies, risk, resource implications, and sequencing.
  • Connect strategy, priorities, and execution by identifying gaps, interdependencies, and decisions needed to move work forward.

Business Process Management & Operational Excellence:

  • Design, map, optimize, and sustain end-to-end business processes and cross-functional workflows that improve execution, scalability, and clarity across Technical Operations.
  • Establish practical process ownership, governance, operating rhythms, roles, decision rights, and performance measures where they create value.
  • Identify operational friction, duplication, bottlenecks, and handoff gaps, and simplify work across functional boundaries.
  • Lead continuous-improvement efforts using fit-for-purpose problem-solving and process-improvement methods, applying Lean/Six Sigma tools where useful without limiting the role to a single methodology.
  • Capture lessons learned, codify best practices, and build repeatable processes and playbooks that reduce dependence on individual effort or expertise.

Cross-Functional Initiative Leadership:

  • Lead select high-priority cross-functional initiatives that call for neutral leadership, organizational coordination, specialized expertise, or added execution capacity.
  • Facilitate complex cross-functional decisions, working sessions, and problem-solving efforts that build alignment and accelerate action.
  • Strengthen the interfaces between Technical Operations and other functions so interdependent work stays integrated while functional ownership remains clear.
  • Build trusted relationships with leaders and technical experts, bringing an objective, business-minded perspective to execution challenges and tradeoffs.

Organizational Capability:

  • Ensure major initiatives build organizational capability alongside near-term outcomes.
  • Help leaders establish sustainable ways of working that strengthen accountability, decision-making, coordination, and operational performance.
  • Partner with the Principal, Business Operations & Digital Enablement so business processes, portfolio visibility, data, systems, and digital solutions reinforce one another.

Requirements:

  • Bachelor’s degree in Business, Operations, Engineering, Life Sciences, Organizational Development, or a related discipline; advanced degree preferred.
  • 10+ years of progressive experience in business process management, operational excellence, strategy execution, transformation, business operations, program leadership, or related disciplines.
  • Experience in biotechnology, pharmaceutical, biopharmaceutical manufacturing, Technical Operations, or another complex regulated environment strongly preferred.
  • Demonstrated experience designing and improving end-to-end business processes, including process architecture, process ownership, process mapping/redesign, governance, and performance management.
  • Demonstrated ability to translate broad strategy into executable plans and lead complex cross-functional initiatives from ambiguity through execution.
  • Strong understanding of operating models, governance, decision rights, continuous improvement, and organizational change and adoption.
  • Exceptional facilitation, communication, problem-solving, and executive presentation skills, with the ability to influence without direct authority.
  • Ability to operate effectively in a fast-paced, evolving environment and move comfortably between strategic thinking and hands-on execution.
  • Other combinations of education and/or experience may be considered.

title: Roads Supervisor
description:
Live and work in a culture rich location minutes from the Murray River, just a short drive to one of Victoria’s best wine regions and with the ski fields so close you will be zooming down the mountains in under two hours.

Our employee benefits include professional development and flexible working conditions. Our conditions of employment support equal opportunities and an ethical, diverse, and inclusive workplace.

We also recognise and value your priorities beyond work. It’s important to us that you have a sustainable work–life balance, so we offer flexible working arrangements, a nine-day fortnight (full-time staff) and a range of leave options and support programs.

AlburyCity is committed to being a child safe organisation by creating cultures, adopting strategies and taking action to empower children. We work hard to keep them safe from harm because child safety is everyone’s responsibility.

DIRECTORATE:
Infrastructure, Planning & Environment

CLASSIFICATION:
Grade H

SALARY:
A base salary of $101,528 with competency-based increments up to $117,773 pa + 12% employer contribution to superannuation

REPORTING TO:
Team Leader City Works

EMPLOYMENT TYPE:
Permanent Full Time

THE POSITION:
Provide leadership, supervision, and coordination of the Roads Maintenance and Ancillary Works crews to ensure the safe, efficient, and cost-effective delivery of construction and maintenance programs, meeting required quality standards, project timeframes, and budget objectives.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES:

  • Supervise City Works Crews as required. These crews undertake civil construction and maintenance works, including but not limited to roads maintenance and ancillary works.
  • Supervise and lead an effective and efficient team capable of delivering services to agreed levels and standards.
  • Provide effective staff management, including timesheets and rostering, recruitment, performance management and employee development, employee motivation and foster team harmony.
  • Manage, administer, and supervise external contractors, ensuring compliance with contractual obligations, Council standards, and relevant legislation.
  • Implement, monitor, and continuously improve Quality Assurance systems and processes to support the effective delivery of City Works operations.
  • Coordinate works with other work groups and AlburyCity Groups to ensure the most effective outcomes are achieved for the AlburyCity.
  • Execute works in accordance with AlburyCity's WHS Policies and Procedures and safe construction practices, ensuring all WHS requirements are met by employees, contractors, and any other personnel involved in the works.
  • Coordinate and arrange the plant, equipment, materials, and resources required for the efficient delivery of construction and maintenance works.
  • Prepare quotations, cost estimates, and budget submissions relating to City Works activities and projects.
  • Prepare and provide operational, financial, and performance reports on City Works activities as required.
  • Contribute to the development and review of Council's Construction and Maintenance Program.
  • Plan, coordinate, monitor, and deliver capital works and maintenance programs to ensure projects are completed within agreed timeframes, budgets, and quality standards.
  • Monitor plant and equipment utilisation, ensuring scheduled servicing, preventative maintenance, and compliance requirements are effectively managed.
  • Liaise and coordinate with public utility providers to facilitate project planning and delivery.
  • Perform other tasks or duties as directed by the Supervisor which are within the limits of the employee's skill, competence, and training.
  • Observe requirements of the WHS Legislation, relevant to the job and adhere to AlburyCity Policies and Procedures regarding WHS.
  • Observe appropriate AlburyCity Policies and Procedures regarding day-to-day operations including Equal Employment Opportunity policies, AlburyCity's Dress Code and Standards Policy and AlburyCity's Code of Conduct.

KEY RELATIONSHIPS:

Internal

  • Our People

External

  • Our Community
  • Statutory Authorities
  • Businesses
  • Utility Service Organisations
  • Material Suppliers and Contractors

EMPLOYMENT CONDITIONS:

  • Based on a 38-hour week, with actual days and times being Monday to Friday, 7.00am to 4.00pm, with an RDO in accordance with AlburyCity's RDO guidelines. These times may vary due to operational requirements and will be determined by the supervisor.
  • This position may involve work outside normal working hours. Additional hours over the standard 38 hours will attract a time in lieu arrangement or payment of overtime rates as agreed with your supervisor.
  • This position will be provided with vaccination against the following infectious diseases:
    • Hepatitis B
  • This position requires you to wear a compulsory uniform as per AlburyCity’s Our People Dress Code Standards. Our People are required to present a smart and professional image to the public at all times including when in public and when working remotely.
  • This position involves working in a predominantly outdoor environment where a varying range of temperatures, weather conditions and walking surfaces may be experienced. The position requires a moderate level of aerobic and physical fitness to undertake regular physical activities such as walking, lifting, pulling, pushing along with the capacity to maintain normal manual handling tasks across the workday - depending on the nature of the tasks undertaken. The use of relevant work method statements and appropriate WHS standards are an integral part of the role. A full functional and medical assessment is required for this position.
  • This position is delegated with certain powers, authorities, duties, and functions of Council under the AlburyCity Delegations of Authority in accordance with section 378 of the Local Government Act.
  • This position is subject to alcohol and other drug testing
  • This position is location at the Albury Depot, Wodonga Place, Albury, with occasional/frequent visits to external sites/depots, and AlburyCity Administration Building as required.

ESSENTIAL CRITERIA:

  • Qualified Supervisors Certificate and/or Overseer's Certificate NSW or equivalent, and/or Certificate IV in Frontline Management or equivalent relevant experience
  • Construction Induction Certificate
  • Class C (standard) Driver's Licence (compulsory to have & maintain)

DESIRABLE CRITERIA:

  • Certificate III or IV in Construction or relevant demonstrated experience in civil construction, maintenance or infrastructure delivery.

EXPERIENCE:

  • Extensive demonstrated experience in a civil/commercial construction and/or Local Government environment

SPECIALIST KNOWLEDGE AND SKILLS:

  • Complete and comprehensive understanding of all Acts, Regulation, Codes and Construction Practices relating to Civil services maintenance and construction
  • Ability to read and interpret plans and specifications
  • Surveying skills in the use of levels and theodolites
  • Sound knowledge of civil construction best practice

Competence and understanding in the following:

  • Construction planning and contract administration
  • Lifting equipment
  • Maintenance management systems
  • Material properties and application
  • Operation of hydraulic systems
  • Purchasing and procurement
  • Quantity calculations and estimating
  • Record keeping
  • Reticulation systems
  • Traffic control

title: Property Survey Coordinator (Temporary)
description:
Engrain builds map-based tech that’s redefining how real estate works. Our interactive, unit-level maps and powerful data integrations help over 1,000 companies—and 20,000 properties—to make smarter decisions, streamline leasing, and deliver better renter experiences. From prospect to renewal, our products give properties a spatial brain and a visual edge when it comes to property marketing and management.


We’re not your typical proptech company. We move fast, we stay curious, and we don’t do stale or corporate fluff. Backed by successful Seed and Series A rounds, we’re entering a phase of serious scale.


As the Property Survey Coordinator, you will be integral to our on-site video capture process, ensuring seamless coordination and meticulous analysis that directly impact the quality and efficiency of our deliverables. This role bridges property stakeholder coordination with detailed data analysis, giving you a deep understanding of each project and enhancing the overall workflow. Working closely with video creation vendors, on-site property teams, and internal product groups, you will ensure all site requirements are met with precision and timeliness. Your ability to manage multiple projects, analyze property inventory data, and communicate effectively will be crucial in maintaining our high standards and driving client satisfaction. title: Head of Billing and Collections
description:
This is an opportunity to join Ascot Group - one of the world’s preeminent specialty risk underwriting organizations.

Designed as a modern-era company operating through an ecosystem of interconnected global operating platforms, we’re bound by a common mission and purpose: One Ascot. Our greatest strength is a talented team who flourish in a collaborative, inclusive, and entrepreneurial culture, steeped in underwriting excellence, integrity, and a passion to find a better way, The Ascot Way.

The Ascot Way guides our people and our organization. Our underwriting platforms collaborate to find creative ways to deploy our capital in a true cross-product and cross-platform approach. These platforms work as one, deploying our capital creatively through our unique Fusion Model: Client Centric, Risk Centric, Technology Centric.

Built to be resilient, Ascot maximizes client financial security while delivering bespoke products and world class service — both pre- and post-claims. Ascot exists to solve for our clients’ brightest tomorrow, through agility, collaboration, resilience, and discipline.

Ascot is embedding artificial intelligence (AI) and automation across the organisation to enhance decision‑making, efficiency, and quality of outcomes. In this role, you will be expected to work confidently alongside AI‑enabled tools, apply sound judgment when interpreting insights, and adapt as technology continues to evolve. We value curiosity, critical thinking, and a willingness to embrace change as part of how we work.

Job Summary:

Ascot’s Finance Operations team is seeking a strategic, hands-on Head of Billing & Collections to lead billing, cash application, collections, reconciliations, and related receivables operations across the organization. This leader will build disciplined, scalable processes that drive timely invoicing, accurate cash application, effective collections, strong controls, improved working capital, and high-quality service for internal and external stakeholders.

The successful candidate will combine deep operational expertise, sound judgment, and strong people leadership with the ability to influence across Finance, Underwriting, Claims, Operations, Reinsurance, Treasury, Technology, brokers, and other partners. The role will also be a key business leader in the implementation, adoption, and ongoing optimization of Ascot’s new Guidewire billing system—ensuring that requirements, workflows, controls, reporting, data conversion, testing, training, and user readiness are effectively represented. This position follows a hybrid work schedule.

Responsibilities:

  • Lead the end-to-end Billing & Collections function, including invoicing, cash application, payment reconciliation, collections, dispute management, unapplied cash resolution, and related receivables activities.

  • Define and execute the Billing & Collections strategy, operating model—including direct, agency, and deductible billing—and target-state roadmap in support of growth, customer experience, controls, and financial objectives.

  • Establish clear policies, procedures, controls, service standards, and performance metrics that enable timely, accurate, compliant, and scalable execution.

  • Own receivables and working-capital performance, improving collection effectiveness, cash conversion, aging, unapplied cash, and overall cash-flow outcomes.

  • Develop risk-based collection strategies that maximize cash realization while preserving strong relationships with brokers, clients, reinsurers, coverholders, and other partners.

  • Optimize the operating model across automation, outsourced or offshore resources, and internal teams to achieve service, control, quality, and cost objectives.

  • Manage outsourced billing and collections providers, holding them accountable for contractual commitments, service-level agreements, controls, and key performance indicators.

  • Use data, analytics, and predictive monitoring to identify collection risks, prioritize recovery efforts, strengthen cash-flow forecasting, and support proactive decisions.

  • Oversee the analysis and resolution of aged receivables, past-due balances, unapplied cash, payment discrepancies, returned payments, disputes, and other complex account issues.

  • Develop executive reporting and dashboards covering aging, collections effectiveness, cash-application timeliness, dispute trends, working capital, cash flow, operational quality, receivables risk, and service performance.

  • Partner with Underwriting, Claims, Reinsurance, Treasury, Finance, Operations, Technology, Legal, Compliance, and business leaders to resolve systemic issues and improve performance.

  • Serve as the senior escalation point for complex broker, client, reinsurer, and internal stakeholder matters involving billing, collections, payment application, and account status.

  • Drive continuous improvement, automation, and standardization, including active leadership in the Guidewire billing implementation and thoughtful use of data, technology, and AI-enabled tools.

  • Support month-end, quarter-end, and year-end close by ensuring accurate receivables reporting, reconciliations, documentation, controls, and timely issue resolution.

  • Build, lead, coach, and develop a high-performing team with clear expectations, strong capabilities, career development, and accountability.

  • Model The Ascot Way through inclusive collaboration, ownership, and a commitment to an engaged, high-performing culture.

Requirements:

  • Bachelor’s degree in Accounting, Finance, Business Administration, or a related field; equivalent relevant experience may be considered.

  • At least 10 years of progressive experience in accounts receivable, billing, collections, finance operations, insurance accounting, or a related discipline, including people leadership experience.

  • Experience in insurance, reinsurance, financial services, specialty insurance, workers’ compensation, or another complex, transaction-intensive environment is strongly preferred.

  • Deep knowledge of billing operations, collection strategies, receivables management, cash application, internal controls, reconciliations, and financial reporting.

  • Demonstrated ability to analyze complex account issues, identify root causes, and implement practical, well-controlled solutions.

  • Proven success leading process improvement, automation, reporting, and operational transformation initiatives.

  • Strong stakeholder-management skills and the ability to influence effectively across functions and with external partners.

  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to explain complex issues clearly to senior leaders and business partners.

  • Highly organized and detail-oriented, with the ability to manage competing priorities in a fast-paced, collaborative environment.

  • Experience with accounting, billing, collections, ERP, workflow, or reporting platforms; Guidewire BillingCenter or comparable Guidewire experience is strongly preferred.

  • Experience serving as a business subject-matter expert or functional lead on billing-system implementations, including requirements, process design, data conversion, user acceptance testing, training, and adoption.

  • Proven ability to build trusted relationships with Finance, Operations, Underwriting, Claims, Reinsurance, Treasury, Technology, brokers, clients, and external service providers.

  • Demonstrated success building and developing high-performing teams and fostering accountability, collaboration, customer service, and continuous improvement.

  • A positive, self-motivated, customer-centric leadership style and a commitment to developing people and improving outcomes.

This position may be filled at a different level based on the selected candidate’s experience and qualifications.

Compensation:

Actual base pay may vary above or below the stated range based on factors such as experience, subject-matter expertise, and skills. Base pay is one component of Ascot’s total compensation package. Additional rewards may include an annual cash bonus and other discretionary compensation awarded by the Company.

Annualized base pay range: $200,000 - $220,000

Company Benefits:

Ascot offers a competitive benefits package, subject to applicable eligibility requirements, including:

  • Health and welfare benefits: medical (including prescription coverage), dental, vision, health savings account, commuter account, health care and dependent care flexible spending accounts, life insurance, accidental death and dismemberment insurance, work-life resources (including an Employee Assistance Program), and more.
  • Leave benefits: paid holidays; annual paid time off, including state or local paid leave where required; short- and long-term disability; and other leaves, including bereavement, FMLA, adoption, maternity, military, primary caregiver, and non-primary caregiver leave.
  • Retirement benefits: contributory savings plan (401(k)).

title: Kansas City - American Red Cross First Aid/CPR/AED Instructor/ Trainer
description:

We operate at more than 200 locations across the United States, providing American Heart Association Basic Life Support courses, American Red Cross First Aid/CPR/AED and Basic Life Support courses, and related CPR and life-saving training programs.

With an annual training volume of more than 80,000 participants, ALLCPR stands for the belief that all of us should learn CPR. It is our mission to ensure that everyone has the knowledge and skills to save lives.

Our Work Environment Includes

The Instructor will teach American Red Cross First Aid/CPR/AED courses and train students through the American Red Cross.﻿

The Instructor Trainer will be responsible for teaching American Red Cross First Aid/CPR/AED Instructor courses, training instructor candidates to become certified American Red Cross instructors.

The Instructor Trainer will prepare for training sessions, demonstrate proper techniques, and evaluate candidates' performance to ensure they have achieved proficiency.

Schedule

title: Manufacturing Technician ll
description:
Novate Solutions, Inc. a process control engineering firm providing engineering services to a variety of industrial clients with office locations in Livermore, West Sacramento and Merced, is looking for a Manufacturing Technician II assigned to our Merced location. This position can be physically demanding and requires the individual to be a hands-on problem solver and able to work in a fast-paced work environment.


The ideal candidate enjoys a wide variety of projects and is looking to grow his or her skillset through collaboration with engineers, other technicians, and our electrical installation team. Growth opportunities include promotion through production management, or to the field installation and support team.

Responsibilities:

  1. Collect kitted materials from inventory according to Bill of Materials (BOM)

  2. Using hand and power tools, cut steel, aluminum and plastic enclosures and materials per engineering drawings.

  3. Install industrial electrical and automation components per engineering drawings.

  4. Print wire labels per engineering documents.

  5. Wire industrial control equipment per engineering drawings.

  6. Professionally organize wiring in wireway and loom.

  7. Test power equipment under engineering supervision.

  8. Communicate with engineers to document changes required from design.

  9. Redline (correct) drawings for any errors or corrections required via Bluebeam (Windows based software).

  10. Log time and activities in business applications, including work orders, production schedule and traveler documents.

  11. Communicate via Microsoft Outlook (Email) and Microsoft Teams with engineering, field and business management team.

  12. Control panel assembly which includes mounting, labeling, and wiring of custom systems.

  13. Install and repair wiring, electrical fixtures, power equipment, and components of machinery and equipment following UL508 (Industrial Control Panel standards), electrical code, manuals, specifications, schematics, and blueprints.

  14. Diagnose and address problems in electrical circuits, systems, and equipment using testing instruments and equipment.

title: Health Navigator (Bilingual)
description:
Health Navigator Role Description

About Us:

Main Street Health is the nation's largest provider of value-based care exclusively serving rural America. We believe in the old ways of medicine when healthcare was simpler. By partnering with rural primary care doctors, we reinforce the importance of trust and relationship-driven care in rural communities. We provide our partners with the staff, technology, and processes necessary to succeed in a value-based delivery model.

About the Role:
Navigating the changes to our healthcare system can be intimidating and confusing for doctors and patients alike. The Health Navigator’s role is to make it easier. You will start by developing trusted relationships with our patients and providers and will assist with various patient-facing, administrative, and logistical tasks so that doctors can focus on delivering high-quality medical care to their patients. Navigators work for Main Street but go to work every day inside one of our partner clinics alongside clinic staff. They meet with and call patients, enter data into our systems, contact the pharmacy to refill prescriptions, troubleshoot challenges with insurance coverage and more. Main Street’s management and training teams will equip you with the training and tools you need to perform these duties. You will:

  • Develop strong relationships with patients to assist them with their care ​
  • Meet with patients during the check-in process, entering data into the Main Street software platform for reporting and tracking purposes
  • Call patients to schedule an office visit or remind them to pick up their medication
  • Order and schedule various procedures, tests and screenings
  • Identify and track progress on important gaps in patient care
  • Maintain a record of patient interactions and communicate with providers using electronic health records
  • Educate patients on their healthcare options, insurance benefits, and common medical conditions​
  • Help patients access various community resources
  • Help coordinate follow-up care after patients have been discharged from the hospital
  • Demonstrate compassion for patients, adaptability, attention to detail, patience and an eagerness to collaborate with team members​

Requirements for This Role:

  • You are a self-starter who is comfortable working independently
  • You enjoy meeting new people and developing relationships
  • You bring a strong service mentality to your work
  • You love your community and want to see it thrive
  • You can skillfully explain the importance of key activities that makes patients healthier
  • You are flexible and excited to tackle new challenges
  • You love solving problems and will take whatever initiative is required to solve them
  • You are comfortable using data to help inform decisions and activities
  • You are excited by the idea of working in a fast-paced organization where change is the norm
  • You learn and apply new information quickly
  • You are familiar with and comfortable using multiple software platforms
  • Work a full-time 40-hour week; Monday-Friday 8am to 5pm (1 hour lunch)
  • Active unencumbered driver’s license required
  • GED or High School Diploma

We are an equal opportunity employer, indiscriminate of race, religion, ethnicity, national origin, citizenship, gender,
gender identity, sexual orientation, age, veteran status, disability, genetic information, or any other protected
characteristic.

At Main Street, we take your privacy and security seriously. Main Street will never:

  • Contact you via encrypted messaging applications (e.g., Signal, etc.)
  • Send you a check in advance of your employment
  • Request you to wire money anywhere
  • Request detailed personal financial information prior to employment

Candidate must be bilingual Spanish

The Stationary Engineer operates and maintains facility systems that provide heating, air conditioning, refrigeration, steam or high-temperature water, and electricity at Defense Supply Center Columbus. title: Information Security Engineer SOC and Incident Response
description:
About the Team

You will be part of the Enterprise Cyber Security organization responsible for protecting WSI associates, customers, systems, and data. The Security Operations Center (SOC) monitors enterprise security events, investigates suspicious activity, and coordinates response with Incident Response, Threat Intelligence, Detection Engineering, and technology partners.

About the Role

As an Information Security Engineer - SOC / Incident Response, you will provide Level 2 security operations support through alert triage, event investigation, and coordinated incident response. You will participate in a 24x7 SOC rotation, including weekends, holidays, and on-call coverage as assigned, and use established playbooks and escalation procedures to protect enterprise systems.

Responsibilities

  • Triage, investigate, and document security alerts and events from Google SecOps, CrowdStrike, and other security monitoring platforms.

  • Analyze endpoint, network, identity, and application evidence to distinguish malicious activity from benign events.

  • Execute approved investigation and response playbooks through Cortex XSOAR and/or Google SecOps SOAR.

  • Perform authorized containment actions under established procedures and approval requirements; promptly escalate actions outside delegated authority.

  • Support incident investigations, evidence collection, timeline development, remediation coordination, and post-incident follow-up.

  • Use CrowdStrike, Tanium, MISP, and related tools to enrich investigations and coordinate endpoint response.

  • Escalate significant incidents and complex technical issues to senior responders, Incident Response leadership, and designated incident command roles.

  • Partner with Cyber Threat Intelligence and Detection Engineering on threat hunts, detection feedback, and alert-quality improvements.

  • Maintain accurate case notes, handoff documentation, and operational runbooks for continuous coverage.

  • Participate in 24x7 shift operations, including weekends, holidays, and on-call responsibilities, as assigned.

  • Identify opportunities for safe automation and AI-assisted investigative efficiency while validating results and following response controls.

Criteria

  • 3 years of experience in security operations, incident response, IT security, or a related technical field.

  • Bachelor's degree in Computer Science or related field, or equivalent work experience

  • Foundational knowledge of security monitoring, endpoint security, operating systems, networking, and common attack techniques.

  • Experience triaging alerts, investigating security events, and documenting findings.

  • Familiarity with SIEM, EDR, case management, and escalation procedures.

  • Ability to work effectively in a 24x7 operational environment and communicate clearly during time-sensitive events.

  • Experience with Google SecOps, CrowdStrike, Cortex XSOAR, Google SecOps SOAR, Tanium, or MISP preferred.

  • Experience supporting endpoint containment, evidence handling, threat hunting, or response playbooks preferred.

  • Basic scripting, automation, or AI-assisted analysis experience preferred.

  • This role requires being onsite in the Rocklin, CA, San Jose, CA or Brooklyn, NY office Monday through Thursday.

Our Culture & Values

We believe that taking care of our people is vital to our success and we strive to offer equitable and transparent practices for all. We prioritize connection, growth, and wellbeing.

People First

Putting People First means investing in overall well-being and opportunities to grow and advance within the organization. Depending on the position and location, here are a few highlights of what benefits may be available:

Benefits

  • A 401(k) plan and other investment opportunities

  • Paid vacations, holidays, and time off to volunteer

  • Health benefits, dental and vision insurance, including same-sex domestic partner benefits

  • Tax-free commuter benefits

  • In-person and online learning opportunities through WSI University

WSI will not now or in the future commence an immigration case or "sponsor" an individual for this position (for example, H-1B or other employment-based immigration).

This role is not eligible for relocation assistance.

Williams-Sonoma, Inc. is an Equal Opportunity Employer. Williams-Sonoma, Inc. will consider for employment qualified applicants with criminal histories in a manner consistent with the requirements of the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance, or other applicable state or local laws and ordinances.

Actual pay will be determined based on experience and other job-related factors permitted by law. title: Data Analyst – Analytics & Strategy
description:
At cabi, we’re redefining what it means to build a fashion brand—one rooted in connection, confidence, and purpose. As a women’s retail clothing company, we don’t just design beautiful apparel; we create opportunities for women to express themselves, build community, and thrive both personally and professionally. Our culture is collaborative, entrepreneurial, and deeply people-first, and every team member plays a role in creating meaningful experiences for our Stylists and clients. If you’re energized by creativity, inspired by empowering others, and excited to contribute to a brand that blends style with substance, you’ll feel right at home here.

We are looking for a Data Analyst who can own our recurring reporting and also dig into the open-ended questions that come up across the business. About half of the role is keeping our core reporting accurate, reliable, and increasingly automated. The other half is ad hoc analysis and project work, where you'll partner with teams across the company to answer the questions behind their biggest decisions.

This role is a great fit for someone who enjoys both building things that run smoothly and solving new problems. You should be comfortable taking a loosely defined request, figuring out what's really being asked, and turning it into a clear analysis and recommendation. Because our work goes to executives, the board, and external partners, a high attention to detail is essential.

We also use AI tools every day to work faster and smarter, and we're looking for someone who is excited to do the same.

What You'll Do

Reporting, maintenance, and automation

  • • Own and maintain a portfolio of recurring reports and Tableau dashboards used by executives and teams across the company
  • • Monitor data refreshes and pipelines, troubleshoot issues quickly, and keep stakeholders informed when something breaks
  • • Find manual or repetitive reporting work and automate it, using SQL, scripting, and AI tools to make reporting faster and more reliable
  • • Build and maintain data transformation pipelines in our cloud data warehouse (Snowflake) that feed reporting and analysis
  • • Write clear documentation for reports, metric definitions, and data logic so the team can support each other's work
  • • Validate data and check your work so the numbers we publish can be trusted

Ad hoc analysis and projects

  • • Partner with stakeholders across the company to understand the business questions behind their requests
  • • Turn vague or loosely defined asks into specific questions, scoped analyses, and clear timelines
  • • Help develop data products for teams across the organization that keep them informed and guide their decision making
  • • Design and build new Tableau dashboards from the ground up, from gathering requirements and modeling the data to final design
  • • Run analyses that apply statistical techniques to uncover trends, patterns, and correlations, explain performance, and identify opportunities, then present findings in plain language with clear recommendations
  • • Guide stakeholders through what the data means for their decisions, including where it has limits
  • • Use AI tools to speed up analysis, explore new approaches, and prototype solutions, and share what you learn with the team

What You Bring

  • • 2–4 years of experience in data analytics, business intelligence, or a related role
  • • Strong SQL skills and experience working in a cloud data warehouse such as Snowflake
  • • Hands-on experience building Tableau dashboards from scratch, including data modeling, calculations, and thoughtful visual design
  • • Experience building or maintaining data transformation pipelines
  • • Regular, practical use of AI tools in your work, and genuine curiosity about how AI can change the way analytics gets done
  • • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including explaining technical findings to non-technical audiences
  • • Ability to take an ambiguous request, ask the right questions, and turn it into a focused analysis
  • • High attention to detail: you catch errors before anyone else does, sanity-check numbers against what you know about the business, and hold yourself to a standard of accuracy fit for executive and board reporting
  • • Comfort managing several priorities at once and keeping stakeholders updated on progress
  • • Bachelor's degree in a quantitative field such as analytics, statistics, economics, computer science, or business, or equivalent experience
  • • A collaborative mindset and eagerness to work across teams in a fast-moving environment
  • • A strong team player who supports colleagues and takes ownership and accountability for the team's work

Nice to Have

  • • Experience with dbt or a similar transformation tool
  • • Python for data processing, automation, or analysis
  • • Experience in retail, fashion, direct sales, or another consumer business
  • • Familiarity with performance marketing and acquisition platforms such as Google Analytics, Meta, Instagram, and TikTok
  • • Familiarity with Tableau Server or Tableau Cloud administration

What We Offer

At cabi, we believe our people should be recognized for the impact they make. Our compensation philosophy is designed to provide fair and competitive pay based on the value and scope of each role, as well as relevant experience, skills, and the market in which the role is based.

The anticipated salary range for this position is $75,000-$85,000. Actual compensation may vary based on a variety of job-related factors, including relevant experience, knowledge, skills, qualifications, and geographic location.

In addition to base salary, this position may be eligible for up to 10% Bonus.

Benefits & Perks

At cabi, we believe benefits should support the whole person—at work, at home, and for the future. We offer a competitive benefits package designed to support your health and well-being, financial security, time away, personal growth, and connection.

Our benefits include:

  • Competitive medical, dental, and vision coverage
  • Flexible spending account options
  • Company-paid life and AD&D insurance
  • 401(k) retirement plan with a company match
  • Paid time off and paid holidays
  • Employee purchase discounts of up to 85%
  • Additional employee appreciation and clothing perks
  • Opportunities for training and professional development
  • Team celebrations, catered lunches, and other employee appreciation experiences

Benefits eligibility and offerings may vary based on employment status and applicable plan requirements.

Cabi regularly reviews its compensation and benefits programs to promote fair and consistent practices across the organization.

Equal Employment Opportunity

Cabi is an equal opportunity employer. We’re committed to providing equal employment opportunities to all qualified applicants and employees. We don’t discriminate on the basis of race, color, religion, sex, pregnancy, childbirth or related medical conditions, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, national origin, ancestry, age, disability, genetic information, veteran status, or any other status protected by applicable federal, state, or local law.

We’ll consider qualified applicants with criminal histories in a manner consistent with applicable federal, state, and local laws.

Candidate Safety

Your safety matters to us. As you explore career opportunities, be cautious of fraudulent job postings, fake websites, and individuals impersonating recruiters or company representatives.

Cabi recruiters will only contact candidates through @cabiexperience.com or through our official applicant tracking system, Greenhouse.

Joining cabi means more than stepping into a role—it’s stepping into a mission. We’re passionate about uplifting women, supporting growth, and celebrating individuality in everything we do. As you explore this opportunity, imagine the impact you could make as part of a company that values innovation, authenticity, and connection at every level. If you’re ready to bring your talents to a team that’s as driven as it is supportive, we’d love to see what you can do with us.

title: Senior Staff Software Engineer
description:
The team

Build Agent is ServiceNow's AI coding assistant, purpose-built for the platform's metadata-driven substrate - operating natively across ServiceNow's scoped applications, tables, and metadata types. This role leads the team responsible for the Build Agent evaluation framework, model support, and telemetry.

The framework is critical to Build Agent success — it's already driven measurable wins: recovering Build Agent correctness, cutting latency and inference cost ahead of a major release, and catching high-severity defects that manual testing missed before they reached production. The team is 8 engineers and is currently the bottleneck on its own scale — this role exists to convert a high-performing initiative into a durable, scalable function.

Key areas of focus include:

  • Evaluation Infrastructure: Golden prompt sets, Pass@1 and functional scoring, failure categorization (plumbing vs. metadata-creation failures), and coverage across ServiceNow metadata types and UI workflows.
  • Model Support & Benchmarking: Structured evaluation of candidate foundation models against the production default, with failure-consistency analysis to separate scaffold/tuning issues from genuine capability gaps.
  • Telemetry: Token usage, cache efficiency, and inference cost tracked alongside correctness as first-class release signals.
  • Cross-Team Arbitration: Prioritizing eval coverage, defining what "good" means across surfaces owned by different contributing teams, and turning eval signal into committed fixes by the owning teams rather than open-ended findings.

What you get to do in this role

  • Own eval strategy and roadmap: prompt set design, scoring methodology, failure-mode taxonomy, and telemetry instrumentation.
  • Coordinate across the multiple teams contributing to Build Agent to arbitrate quality standards and drive eval findings to committed, owned fixes — not just reports.
  • Lead model benchmarking efforts, making data-backed recommendations on model support decisions (e.g., evaluating frontier coding models against the incumbent default).
  • Solve ambiguous, cross-cutting problems where eval signal, model capability, and platform architecture intersect — and where "correct" isn't obvious until you've defined the bar.
  • Direct experience building or leading evaluation systems for LLM-based products — scoring methodology, benchmark design, and failure analysis, not just prompt engineering.
  • Understanding of coding agent architecture: tool use, agentic loops, context management, and the trade-offs between generic and domain-specific scaffolding.
  • 6+ years of experience with technologies relevant to ServiceNow, including advanced coding skills and fluency in one or more of Java, C++, Ruby, Shell, or JavaScript.
  • Experience critically evaluating foundation models — distinguishing real capability differences from tuning or scaffold artifacts.
  • Ability to execute against ambiguous priorities, weighing context, risk, and desired outcomes — particularly where eval data is incomplete or contested.

For positions in this location, we offer a base pay of $171,900 - $300,800, plus equity (when applicable), variable/incentive compensation and benefits. title: Principal Animation Artist - Unpublished R&D Product
description:
Riot Games was established in 2006 by entrepreneurial gamers who believe that player-focused game development can result in great games. In 2009, Riot released its debut title League of Legends to critical and player acclaim. As the most played video game in the world, over 100 million play every month. Players form the foundation of our community and it’s for them that we continue to evolve and improve the League of Legends experience.

We’re looking for humble but ambitious, razor-sharp professionals who can teach us a thing or two. We promise to return the favor. Like us, you take play seriously; you’re passionate about games. That's where you come in.

As a Principal Animation Artist at Riot you will define craft standards, coach the animation team and influence other disciplines, including VFX artists, character artists, and rigging technical artists. You will help direct the animation experience and communicate that vision to team members. A great reel will showcase a diverse selection of character-driven and interactive animation, and a strong foundation in the principles of animation, including weight, anticipation, and impact. Your craft expertise will breathe life into iconic and beloved characters for players.

As a Principal Animation Artist on the Unpublished R&D Product, you will be responsible for all aspects of player-facing animation systems and character performance, from early ideation through final shipping-quality release. Your critical eye for quality and appeal will help strengthen our animation style. You will report into the Art Director of the team.

Responsibilities:

  • Drive the quality and direction of gameplay animation, ensuring a high bar for responsiveness, clarity, and cohesion
  • Own and evolve multiple player-facing animation systems, ensuring scalability and consistency across features
  • Define and establish animation best practices, workflows, and quality standards for the team
  • Partner with design, engineering, and technical art to shape animation systems and influence gameplay integration
  • Anticipate systemic challenges and lead solutions that improve long-term reliability and performance

title: McCormick House Visitor Engagement Fellow
description:
Foundation Summary

The Robert R. McCormick Foundation is a leading philanthropic institution investing more than $75 million annually in Chicagoland, with a focus on improving economic opportunity on Chicago’s South and West Sides. The Foundation is named for its donor, Colonel Robert R. McCormick. The Foundation’s Board of Directors also oversees Cantigny, Col. McCormick’s estate, which today provides educational and recreational opportunities in Chicago’s western suburbs.


The 500-acre Cantigny estate includes McCormick’s Home and Gardens, which host dozens of programs and events annually for nearly half a million visitors; the First Division Museum, a military history museum that tells the story of the U.S. Army’s 1st Infantry Division, beginning in World War I, in which Col. McCormick served, to present; and Cantigny Golf, a 27-hole public golf course and a 9-hole short course, perfect for children and families.


Position Summary

The McCormick House Fellow is a 1–2 year developmental fellowship at the McCormick House. The role focuses on day-to-day operations, visitor experience, volunteer programming, and historical interpretation. The McCormick House serves as a historic house, public gathering space, and interpretive experience within Cantigny. The Fellow will help ensure visitors experience the House in a welcoming, well-organized, and engaging way by connecting daily operations, storytelling, interpretation, and volunteer leadership.


The fellowship combines meaningful operational responsibility with structured mentorship and professional growth. Working closely with the Director of McCormick House and the Foundation Historian, the Fellow will develop skills in historical research, interpretation, institutional history, operations, and visitor experience. Responsibility for interpretive content, special projects, and cross-departmental initiatives will grow throughout the fellowship. Near the conclusion of the 1–2-year term, Cantigny leadership will evaluate the House’s needs alongside the Fellow’s performance and interests to determine whether a continuing or elevated role is warranted. Continuation beyond the fellowship is not guaranteed.


Essential Functions

Operations

  • Monitor the daily readiness of McCormick House for public visitation.
  • Coordinate with Guest Services and Security on opening, closing, visitor access, building security, and emergency procedures.
  • Identify maintenance, housekeeping, environmental, technology, and facility issues that could affect visitors, and communicate them to the appropriate staff.
  • Develop and maintain operational procedures, checklists, and visitor-service protocols.
  • Ensure public spaces, galleries, interpretive areas, and visitor amenities are ready for daily operation.
  • Plan for periods of high visitation and special events.

Visitor Experience

  • Oversee the day-to-day visitor experience during public hours.
  • Serve as a visible, knowledgeable presence within McCormick House.
  • Respond to visitor questions and concerns with accurate, helpful information.
  • Maintain standards for welcoming, engaging, and accessible visitor interactions.
  • Monitor visitor flow, dwell time, feedback, and other indicators of engagement.
  • Recommend improvements to signage, wayfinding, interpretive materials, and visitor amenities.

History, Interpretation & Tours

  • Research and develop tour narratives, themes, and talking points that connect the McCormick family, architecture, and collection to Cantigny's and Chicago's broader history.
  • Curate and refresh interpretive content to keep tours accurate, current, and engaging for diverse audiences.
  • Deliver tours and public presentations as needed, modeling the storytelling standard expected of docents and volunteers.
  • Train volunteers and tour guides in interpretive techniques and content to ensure consistent, high-quality storytelling across all tours.
  • Evaluate tour quality and visitor engagement, and use feedback to continuously refine content and delivery.

Volunteer Program

  • Coordinate the day-to-day volunteer experience at McCormick House.
  • Support volunteer recruitment, orientation, scheduling, training, and retention.
  • Set clear expectations for volunteer conduct, visitor interaction, building awareness, and communication.
  • Maintain volunteer training and reference materials.
  • Provide regular feedback and coaching to volunteers.
  • Ensure appropriate volunteer coverage during public hours, tours, and special programs.

Programs and Special Experiences

  • Support special tours, open houses, member events, educational programs, revenue-generating experiences, and other activities held at the House.
  • Coordinate onsite logistics for programs and special events as needed.

Cross-Departmental Collaboration

  • Maintain effective working relationships with Guest Services, Public Programs, Food & Beverage, Security, Facilities, Communications, Horticulture, and other Cantigny departments.
  • Communicate upcoming tours, programs, events, and operational needs clearly and on time.

title: Part-Time Truck Washer
description:
Truck Washer and Laborer

Job Type: Part-Time, Hourly
Pay: $20.00–$25.00 per hour DOE
Work Location: Auburn, WA and other company locations as needed

Job Description

A Advanced Septic and Construction Services is hiring a Part-Time Truck Washer Laborer to maintain company vehicles, equipment, yards, and facilities. This position will wash and detail septic trucks, vehicles, excavators, and other equipment; perform general yard and facility upkeep; assist with parts running and shop duties; and support septic field crews as needed.

The employee will travel between company locations, including our Auburn-area location, to wash and maintain vehicles and equipment. The position may also assist septic pumpers with general labor, including exposing septic tank lids, digging, moving equipment, and cleanup.

Requirements

  • Must successfully pass a background check.
  • Must successfully complete a pre-employment drug screening and participate in random drug and alcohol testing in accordance with company policy and applicable law.
  • Must be physically able to safely perform the essential functions of the position, including lifting up to 75+ pounds, standing, walking, bending, kneeling, and working outdoors.
  • Must be dependable, safety-conscious, and able to work independently and as part of a team.
  • Must be willing to travel between company locations and assist with yard, shop, equipment, and septic-related labor as needed.

Responsibilities

  • Wash, clean, dry, and detail company vehicles and equipment, including septic trucks, cars, vans, excavators, flatbed trucks, trailers, and other machinery.
  • Clean and maintain vehicle interiors.
  • Safely operate pressure washers, hoses, brushes, and other cleaning equipment.
  • Inspect vehicles and equipment for visible damage or safety concerns and report issues.
  • Maintain clean and organized yards, shops, work areas, and facilities.
  • Organize hoses, tools, supplies, and yard equipment.
  • Assist with yard maintenance, parts running, general maintenance, warehouse and shop duties.
  • Travel between company locations to wash and maintain vehicles and equipment.
  • Assist septic pumpers and field crews with general labor, including digging to expose septic tank lids, moving materials/equipment, and cleanup.

title: Staff Software Engineer-Voice Connectivity
description:
Overview

The Staff Software Engineer, Voice Connectivity Engineering designs, builds, ships, and operates the connectivity layer between a customer's existing telephony and CCaaS environment and the ServiceNow Voice ecosystem. The engineer works across the full lifecycle: mapping a customer's SIP trunks, CTI integrations, and CCaaS-specific APIs, building and hardening the signaling, media, and event integrations that connect those systems to ServiceNow's Voice/CTI and Native Voice Controls platform, and proving through testing and production monitoring that calls connect, stay connected, and hand off cleanly under real network and carrier conditions. This is not an agent-building role — the engineer is not primarily authoring the prompts or instructions that drive voice AI agent behavior — but it is the foundation those agents run on: without a reliable connectivity layer, no agent, however well designed, can reach a live caller.

Two things follow. First, correctness here is measured in call setup success, audio quality, latency, and failover behavior rather than model output — the engineer's product is a connection that has to hold up under real carrier, network, and vendor conditions, not just in a reference environment. Second, because every customer's telephony and CCaaS setup differs — different SIP providers, media gateways, authentication schemes, and CCaaS vendor quirks — the engineer must design integrations that are resilient and diagnosable, with clear failure signals when a segment of the call path breaks, rather than integrations that only work against the reference stack.

What You Get to Do

  • Build the connectivity layer. Design, build, and operate the SIP trunking, signaling, and media integrations that connect a customer's telephony and CCaaS platform to ServiceNow's Voice/CTI and Native Voice Controls ecosystem.
  • Integrate with CCaaS and telephony platforms. Implement and harden integrations using the common patterns of SIP trunking and signaling, WebSocket and streaming media APIs, and real-time audio and event interfaces — across CCaaS providers such as Genesys, NICE, Five9, Amazon Connect, and Twilio, as well as traditional CTI/PBX and carrier setups.
  • Own call path reliability. Design for call setup success, failover, and graceful degradation across carriers, media gateways, and network conditions; instrument and monitor the connectivity layer for latency, jitter, packet loss, and dropped-call causes.
  • Deliver as a forward deployed engineer, embedded in the customer's environment. Work directly inside a customer's telephony, CTI, and CCaaS environment — mapping their existing architecture, standing up and tuning the connection into ServiceNow's Voice ecosystem, and troubleshooting live issues on their network and vendor stack.
  • Feed the Voice AI agent layer cleanly. Ensure the audio, signaling, and event streams the connectivity layer delivers are clean, well-formed, and low-latency enough for the voice AI agents running on ServiceNow's Voice ecosystem to operate correctly — partnering with agent engineering rather than building the agents yourself.
  • Design for security and compliance on the call path. Implement SIP security, media encryption, authentication, and least-privilege access across the connectivity layer, and account for what regulated or high-security customer environments require.
  • Specify precisely and direct engineering work. Convert customer telephony and CCaaS requirements into testable specifications and integration runbooks with explicit scope, constraints, and acceptance criteria; decompose work into implementable tasks and review the result for correctness and maintainability.
  • Own quality and reliability in production. Monitor connectivity health across live customer deployments, triage call-path incidents, and feed recurring failure patterns back into architecture and runbooks.
  • Collaborate across product, design, and engineering. Partner with product managers, voice AI agent engineers, and platform teams — Voice/CTI, CCaaS, and Native Voice Controls — to define integration requirements, align on tradeoffs, and communicate capability and risk clearly.

To Be Successful in This Role

Experience

A demonstrated track record of building, shipping, and operating production telephony or CCaaS integrations at a Staff Software Engineer level, including hands-on delivery of connectivity between third-party telephony/CCaaS platforms and a hosted or cloud service. Direct, hands-on experience integrating with CCaaS platforms using common patterns — SIP trunking and signaling, WebSocket and streaming media APIs, and real-time audio interfaces — across multiple CCaaS providers, is required. Demonstrated technical leadership is expected at this level: setting architectural direction across teams, mentoring engineers, and driving cross-team integration decisions on voice and telephony systems. Willingness to work directly with customers in a forward deployed capacity, embedded in their telephony and contact center environment, is required; prior forward deployed experience is an advantage. Typically 8+ years of production software experience, with several years focused on telephony, CTI, or real-time communications systems.

Education

Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, or a related technical field, or equivalent practical experience. Advanced degrees or certifications are a plus but are not a substitute for a demonstrated record of shipping reliable, production voice and telephony connectivity.

Key Competencies, Skills, and Experience

  • Software engineering fundamentals. Strong command of data structures, algorithms, system design, APIs, data modeling, and testing.
  • CCaaS and telephony integration patterns. Hands-on experience integrating with CCaaS platforms and telephony infrastructure using SIP trunking and signaling, WebSocket and streaming media APIs, and real-time audio interfaces, across multiple providers such as Genesys, NICE, Five9, Amazon Connect, and Twilio, as well as traditional CTI/PBX systems.
  • Real-time communications and media handling. Practical knowledge of SIP, RTP/SRTP, WebRTC, codecs, media gateways, and the latency, jitter, and packet-loss characteristics of live audio.
  • Call path reliability and observability. Ability to design for failover and graceful degradation across carriers and vendors, and to instrument, monitor, and diagnose connectivity issues in production.
  • Voice platform architecture. Working knowledge of how a hosted voice and agent ecosystem — such as ServiceNow's Voice/CTI and Native Voice Controls — consumes audio, signaling, and event streams, enough to design an integration the platform can reliably use without building the agent logic itself.
  • Specification precision and architectural judgment. Ability to define integration and connectivity problems rigorously enough for another engineer to implement correctly, and sound judgment on build-versus-integrate tradeoffs across vendor ecosystems.
  • Safety, security, and data handling. Working knowledge of risks specific to telephony integrations — SIP security, media encryption, call-recording and PII handling, over-broad access — translated into concrete guardrails and monitoring.
  • Forward deployed delivery and stakeholder communication. Comfort working directly with customers inside their telephony environment under incomplete information and fixed timelines, and credibility communicating capability, limitation, and risk to non-engineers.

Desired Experience

  • Forward deployed or customer-embedded delivery. Prior work as a forward deployed engineer, solution engineer, or in professional services, delivering software inside a customer's environment.
  • Carrier and infrastructure depth. Experience with SIP trunk provisioning, PSTN/carrier relationships, number porting, and codec-level audio handling below the application layer.
  • CCaaS platform specialization. Deep, hands-on experience with one or more major CCaaS platforms — such as Genesys, NICE, Five9, or Amazon Connect — beyond generic integration patterns.
  • Observability tooling. Experience with tracing, monitoring, and analysis tooling for real-time communications systems, and analysis of production call and connectivity data at scale.
  • Enterprise domain depth. Customer service, contact center operations, or enterprise IT/telephony operations, at a depth sufficient to challenge a requirement rather than only implement it.
  • Years of Experience. At least 8 years of experience in software engineering with at least 2 years of experience in deploying contemporary AI solutions at customers.

title: Purchasing Clerk
description:
The Purchasing Clerk is responsible for supporting the day-to-day purchasing activities of Birk Manufacturing for bill of material items used in final product, production and office supplies, as well as any miscellaneous items needed to support the business.
