If your goals and values align with Honda’s, we want you to join our team to Bring the Future!

Job Purpose

The purpose of this position is to plan production requirements, provide forecasts to key suppliers, source parts and services, and purchase parts and materials (both internally, within HRC shops, and externally via outside suppliers) to support production, development, and race component requirements. This position is a key role that manages the supply chain core functions from planning analysis, part review, supplier bids/negotiations, delivery, and quality assurance support that results in best value to meet critical assembly, development testing, and race team activities.

Key Accountabilities

Planning Analysis/Purchasing - Lead production planning analysis and ensure timely release of purchase orders to meet assembly build requirements, based on the certified Bill of Materials (BOM). Provide annual forecasts to long lead and major engine suppliers. Negotiate best price, economic ordering quantities (EOQ), and desired delivery, based on production needs and project milestones. Ensure Purchase Orders are maintained with current information for expected receipt dates and any supplier delay notes. Solicit quotations for current specification production parts with approved suppliers and actively manage the supply chain from order placement to part delivery. Manage project inventory levels to ensure sufficient parts are available for production and development needs, while minimizing excess inventory for cost avoidance. Management of Design Level revisions as they relate to production part supersession. Ensure Vendor Cards are current, with up-to-date contacts, addresses, etc. Ensure Item Cards are kept current, with up-to-date revision levels, pricing, and lead time.
Supplier Management - Manage day to day supplier monitoring for on-time delivery, quality, and cost. Lead and review Production Requisitions and Purchase Orders to ensure expected due dates are current, and any delays are communicated to management. Lead recurring meetings with suppliers to establish purchase requirements and status to stakeholders. Analyze supplier technical capabilities, manufacturing limitations, and facilities/equipment availability and redundancy. Participates in and facilitates meetings and vendors for any part quality issues. Communicate with the approved supplier base and Engineering and Quality Assurance to ensure any delays or quality issues are efficiently resolved for procurement responsibilities. Request HTS codes and understanding of INCOTERMS 2010 for international purchases and customs regulations. Develops solutions to a variety of complex procurement problems, referring to established precedents and policies.
Interdepartmental Coordination and Scheduling - Lead coordination with engineering, manufacturing engineering, production, and supplier quality on component quality/ delivery issues. Lead interdepartmental discussions and direction setting regarding vendor capacity issues, quality inspection/documentation, and shipping and receiving, while maintaining on-time delivery. Provide timely status reporting to stakeholders. Coordinate with procurement peers to assist when workload is high, during the peak purchasing season.
Administrative - Plan weekly/daily schedules to attend required meetings. Ensure required training is completed, prior to expiration. Document status and report to HRC management, as required. Maintenance of Purchase Orders. Complete MRB actions on time.

Qualifications, Experience, and Skills

Minimum Experience of 5 years of manufacturing (Machine Shop experience preferred) and buyer/planner procurement experience. Basic understanding of production/manufacturing machine equipment (Manual, CNC, Welding, Castings, etc.). Working knowledge of supplier management and procurement processes. Ability to develop and integrate requirements, planning analysis, negotiation, documentation, and coordination of supplier activities. Ability to effectively interface with all levels of company associates and outside suppliers and resolve conflicts at appropriate levels. Supplier selection understanding based on QAV, familiar with supplier ranking criteria, monitoring on time delivery, familiar with supplier audit (quality, financial, management and shop floor), and continuous improvement, product quality planning, and production part approval process. Familiarity with various purchasing software modules (Navision, Accellion, etc.). Ability to work in a team environment. Clear and concise verbal communication skills. Ability to work under minimal supervision. Ability to resolve conflict effectively.
BS Degree, preferably in a Business-related field and/or equivalent industry procurement experience.

  1. Attendance and timeliness are required. This is not a job you can do from home.

Supervisory Responsibilities

This job has no supervisory responsibilities.

Qualifications

To perform this job successfully, an individual must be able to perform each essential duty listed above satisfactorily. State law says you must be over the age of 21 to work at Spec's. The requirements listed below are representative of the knowledge, skill, and/or ability required. In other words, here's the technical stuff.

Education or Experience

We'd prefer you to have retail receiving experience, but if youre willing to learn, were willing to teach you. We'd like you to have a high school diploma or a general education degree (GED), but sometimes, experience is the best education.

Language Skills

Mathematical Skills

Reasoning Ability

Certificates, Licenses

Physical Demands

This job also requires physical attendance based on a schedule made by management which may vary week to week based on the needs of the business.

Work Environment and Environmental Conditions

We provide a fun and positive environment in which to serve our guests. You will be exposed to outside weather conditions while youre working in our stores. title: Sr Information Security Engineer - Security Red Team
description:
About the Team

You will be part of the Enterprise Cyber Security organization responsible for evaluating the effectiveness of security controls and identifying opportunities to strengthen enterprise defenses. The Red Team works closely with Security Operations, Detection Engineering, Security Engineering, and business partners to assess realistic attack paths and improve resilience.

About the Role

As a Senior Information Security Engineer - Security Red Team, you will lead authorized offensive security engagements from planning through execution, reporting, and remediation validation. This is a hands-on technical lead role responsible for coordinating internal Red Team resources and external testing partners, translating technical findings into actionable risk reduction, and mentoring other engineers without formal people-management responsibilities.

Responsibilities

  • Plan and lead authorized internal and external penetration tests, adversary simulations, and Red Team engagements across enterprise environments.

  • Define engagement scope, objectives, rules of engagement, written authorization, testing windows, safety controls, and communication plans to minimize production disruption.

  • Coordinate internal Red Team engineers and external penetration-testing vendors, including deliverables and follow-up testing.

  • Conduct or direct assessments of Active Directory and identity attack paths, cloud environments, web applications, APIs, and infrastructure.

  • Lead Purple Team exercises with SOC and Detection Engineering to validate visibility, detection coverage, and response effectiveness.

  • Conduct authorized social engineering assessments in accordance with approved scope and company policy.

  • Apply tools such as Cobalt Strike, BloodHound Enterprise, Burp Suite, Metasploit, and Kali Linux where appropriate to approved engagements.

  • Produce clear technical reports and executive-level summaries that explain exposure, business impact, evidence, and prioritized remediation recommendations.

  • Coordinate remediation follow-up, validation, and retesting with application, infrastructure, and security owners.

  • Mentor team members, develop reusable engagement methodologies, and identify safe opportunities for automation and AI-assisted analysis.

Criteria

  • 5+ years of experience in offensive security, penetration testing, Red Team operations, or related security engineering.

  • Demonstrated experience leading authorized security assessments and communicating findings to varied audiences.

  • Hands-on knowledge of enterprise identity, networking, operating systems, cloud platforms, and web application security.

  • Experience documenting scope, safety controls, evidence, and actionable remediation guidance.

  • Ability to coordinate cross-functional engagements and lead technical work without direct-report authority.

  • Experience with Cobalt Strike, BloodHound Enterprise, Burp Suite, Metasploit, and Kali Linux preferred.

  • Experience conducting Purple Team exercises and mapping observations to MITRE ATT&CK preferred.

  • Relevant offensive security certifications or experience with scripting and assessment automation preferred.

  • This role requires being onsite in the Brooklyn, NY office Monday through Thursday.

  • Climb stairs frequently to inspect all areas thoroughly.

Reporting and Documentation:

Professionalism:

title: Principal AI Strategist
description:
Principal AI Strategists on the PACE team guide customers through their AI transformation by leading business alignment, strategic advisory, and value realization for ServiceNow's AI platform. That platform includes Now Assist, AI Agents, Autonomous Workforce AI specialists, and ServiceNow Otto, the unified AI experience that brings conversational AI, enterprise search, voice, and data exploration into one governed front door.

You will operate independently as the lead strategist on customer engagements. You will drive AI roadmapping, governance advisory, and organizational change management planning so that customers move beyond pilots to sustained, expanding consumption and measurable business outcomes. As customers shift from AI that assists to AI that completes work across systems, you will help executives decide where autonomous execution fits, how to govern it with AI Control Tower, and how to measure what it delivers.

You will partner closely with AI Architects in the PACE pairing model. Strategists own the business strategy workstream ("the why and what"). Architects own technical architecture and implementation ("the how"). Together you deliver integrated service offerings that drive measurable customer outcomes. You will also build trusted relationships with CIOs, department heads, and executive sponsors, and scale your expertise through reusable assets, enablement, and thought leadership.

Responsibilities

  • Operate independently as the lead AI strategist on customer engagements, driving business alignment and value conversations
  • Develop AI roadmaps that move customers from first activation to scaled adoption across Now Assist, AI Agents, AI specialists, and the Otto experience as it rolls out, sequencing quick wins against longer-term transformation milestones
  • Lead AI value discovery and realization conversations, translating usage and adoption data into executive-ready business outcomes and building the case for continued AI investment
  • Build AI business cases and adoption roadmaps with the account team, monitor consumption, and intervene proactively when adoption stalls
  • Advise customers on the Assist consumption model, including how agentic and headless activity affects forecasting and expansion planning
  • Provide AI governance advisory (responsible AI policy frameworks, data classification guidance, executive steering committee charters), including how to govern agents and external AI integrations through AI Control Tower and AI Gateway, aligned to regulatory, privacy, and compliance requirements
  • Lead organizational change management planning for AI initiatives, including stakeholder impact assessments, adoption communications, and role-based training, with attention to how roles change as AI agents take on end-to-end work
  • Partner with AI Architects to shape the joint solution approach, with strategists leading business alignment and architects leading technical implementation
  • Build trusted relationships with senior business executives and own executive stakeholder alignment on AI strategy
  • Support sales activity proactively, including contributing to presales strategy documents and driving Expert Services leads for AI strategy engagements. PACE is a post-sale organization, so this role influences sales rather than owning it
  • Contribute to thought leadership, white papers, knowledge base articles, and strategic advisory frameworks that scale AI strategy expertise
  • Develop and refine techniques, including ROI models, business case frameworks, and outcome dashboards, that demonstrate AI value to business stakeholders
  • Contribute to reusable digital assets, playbooks, and enablement tools for internal teams, partners, and customers

Required

  • 5+ years as a consultant or advisor in software or technology industries
  • 5+ years of experience on the ServiceNow platform, with working knowledge of ServiceNow's AI capabilities (Now Assist, AI Agents, and related offerings)
  • 3+ years of hands-on experience with multiple AI tools and large language models, including evaluating where they create, or fail to create, business value
  • Demonstrated ability to lead executive-level conversations and build business cases, roadmaps, and value realization frameworks for technology adoption
  • Experience advising on AI governance, change management, or adoption in complex enterprises
  • Strong written and verbal communication, with the ability to translate technical usage data into business narratives for CIOs and department heads

Preferred

  • Familiarity with agentic AI concepts, including AI agents, multi-agent orchestration, and open standards such as MCP and A2A
  • Understanding of AI governance and observability approaches for agents, and of how regulatory and compliance requirements shape enterprise AI adoption
  • Familiarity with ServiceNow's AI-native packaging and consumption model
  • Experience with enterprise AI front-door or employee-experience platforms, such as conversational assistants, enterprise search, and voice agents
  • Experience building reusable enablement assets, playbooks, or advisory frameworks
  • Track record of supporting presales or services pipeline within a post-sale or customer success organization

title: Senior Software Engineer
description:
About the Company

At ClaimsHero, we're tackling a fundamental injustice. Companies are often responsible for mass harms, but the system to address them is broken: regulation lags far behind technology, and private litigation can't match the scale of consumer harm global mega-companies create.

ClaimsHero is a licensed law firm with the scale of a technology company. We are building a technology platform to rebalance the scales, making it simple for Americans to assert their rights against the companies that harmed them. Our work centers on the mass lawsuits and arbitrations that could drive real accountability, but pose hard technical challenges in scaling acquisition and operations to tens of thousands of clients/

We are a quickly scaling Series A startup that has already reached over 600,000 users and early profitability. If you're ready to create tremendous impact alongside a team transforming a highly conservative industry, apply today!

About the Role

This is an early hire as we build out operations engineering. You will join a small and mighty engineering team and quickly become a key contributor empowering our legal team to effectively support orders of magnitude more clients than traditional methods would allow. You will build tools, services, agentic workflows, and automations that efficiently carry a client's case from intake to filing. You will work closely with the CTO and CPO to develop roadmaps and establish priorities, owning the process from problem understanding to implementing technical solutions to shipping high quality, reliable systems.

About You

  • 4+ years of software engineering experience in backend, data-intensive, or workflow automation systems.
  • Bachelor's Degree or higher in Computer Science or equivalent discipline.
  • A strong drive for efficiency, translating complex manual processes into scalable, reliable automations.
  • A track record of building tools and systems that operations teams actually use, and comfort sitting with them to find what's worth automating.
  • Shipped production-scale LLM/ML-backed functionality or agentic workflows and owned them afterward: evaluation, failure modes, cost, and where a human still belongs in the loop.
  • Hands-on experience with a managed model platform (Snowflake Cortex, Amazon Bedrock, Google Vertex AI, or similar).
  • Experience handling sensitive data in a regulated or high-trust environment (personal, health, financial, or legal records).
  • Applied models to document-heavy workflows, including retrieval, text extraction, and document understanding.
  • Commitment to technical excellence in your own work and your teammates'. We build for quality and scale, not a perpetual MVP.
  • Scrappy and humble, comfortable working independently in an unstructured environment and diving into any problem the work requires. You can work full-stack when a feature calls for it.
  • Highly collaborative, with the ability to work both async and in person, coordinating projects and resolving blockers across functions.
  • Impact- and prioritization-obsessed. We're a small team and can't do everything at once. What you choose to focus on (and more importantly not focus on) defines our success.

Why You Should Be Excited

  • Early Ownership: You'll have real autonomy to design systems and solve problems that set the standard for how large-scale litigation is handled across the legal industry.
  • Massive Impact: Your work will directly determine how many Americans we can serve and how much of the money they're rightfully owed actually reaches them.
  • Solve Hard Problems: From high-volume data flows to agentic workflows with strong accuracy constraints, you'll be challenged with high-impact technical problems core to our business.

Compensation

At ClaimsHero we aim to have a compensation and benefits plan that supports your well-being and aligns your interests with our success in fulfilling our mission. This includes:

  • Competitive equity and cash compensation
  • Comprehensive medical, dental, and vision benefits
  • 401(k) retirement plan
  • Unlimited PTO and flexible work schedules

The minimum and maximum base salary for the Senior Software Engineer role is $150,000 to $200,000. Title and compensation will be determined by years of relevant experience as defined in the job requirements.

title: Senior Archaeologist
description:
Terracon is seeking an experienced, entrepreneurial, and collaborative professional to help lead our Cultural Resources practice. Cultural Resources is part of our Environmental Planning and Permitting group, which also includes NEPA Planning and full-service Natural Resources capabilities. Our team works collaboratively with these and other Environmental practice areas to support Terracon’s local, state, regional and national client base. We are seeking a candidate who understands and is committed to program growth; is a strong team builder, communicator, and mentor; and who brings technical expertise and depth to our program.

Our Albuquerque office is a multi-disciplined team that works on wetlands delineation and permitting; NEPA documentation; threatened and endangered species (T&E) assessments; wildlife habitat assessments (WHA) and species surveys; archeological studies that include Class I and Class III surveys, site eligibility evaluations, and mitigation planning; environmental site assessments; and environmental compliance work. Our clients include Local Government Agencies (City, County and State), school districts, national and local retailers, private entities, commercial real property developers and managers, telecom companies, energy providers, law and architecture firms, financial institutions, and construction engineers.

As a Cultural Resources Archaeologist Lead, you will work also collaborate with Desert Southwest Region leaders to supervise, mentor, and support the professional growth of our Environmental Planning & Permitting team. This team includes full- and part-time employees at all stages of career development. You will support our team’s continued growth through expanded market share and successful project delivery. You will be a leader in understanding and supporting Terracon’s safety culture and expectations.

You will work with your team to manage projects, prepare and review reports, and coach and mentor staff on quality data generation and reporting. You will play an important role in helping support proposal development and project delivery in our office with opportunities to work in the wider region of the Desert Southwest (which includes Arizona, Nevada, and New Mexico). As a senior practitioner you will participate in business development activities with office and department leadership, and you will work with our regional office leadership as well as key sector leads to help grow our practice.

Essential Roles and Responsibilities May Include:

  • Develop understanding and be aware of project-related risk. Be familiar with what could go wrong on a project and how to protect the Company.
  • Lead safety efforts for team and ensure team follows safety rules and guidelines.
  • Responsible for creating and modeling a safe work environment; demonstrates safety practices.
  • Promote continuous quality monitoring and improvement on all projects. Monitor quality standards and practices.
  • Principal Investigator responsible for leading complex projects requiring innovative investigation techniques, providing guidance and support to projects and people.
  • Manage Cultural Resource projects within Arizona. Work with our regional and statewide teams more broadly to continue to develop Terracon’s Cultural Resources practice.
  • Supervise the analysis and formation of recommendations in written reports and treatment plans.
  • Perform site visits, field observations and field data collection in area of technical expertise.
  • Assist in establishing and updating current policies/ procedures for technical projects in field of expertise, to ensure proper interpretation and implementation by junior staff.
  • Provide technical direction and training to less experienced professional staff.
  • Participate in the development of marketing strategies and presentations of qualifications to clients on projects.
  • Mastery of local, state and federal Cultural Resource Management requirements to ensure requirements of each entity are met.
  • Be capable of serving as an Authorized Project Reviewer.

Requirements:

  • Advanced graduate degree in Anthropology, Archeology, or related discipline and more than 15 years of experience in the practice.
  • Possess strong writing skills and previous experience preparing proposals, building budgets, understanding and managing project finances.
  • Familiarity with the Arizona Antiquities Act, Section 106 of the National Historic Preservation Act, National Environmental Policy Act, and other pertinent legislation .
  • Ability to mentor and supervise junior staff regarding data collection, preparation of figures and maps, and report production.
  • Ability to work on a team and build networks across the division and company.
  • Capability to drive full-sized pickup trucks.
  • Ability to perform physically demanding tasks such as lifting and walking on uneven surfaces carrying at least 20 lbs. of equipment, and ability to work in extreme (hot/cold) weather conditions.
  • This position comes with flexible work arrangements but carries an expectation of three (3) in-office days of a normal five (5) day work week. Ability to travel out of town between 10% and 25% of the normal work week.
  • Flexible work schedule, to ensure project timelines are completed.
  • Ability to pass a drug screen and background check.
  • Eligibility to work in the United States without sponsorship.
  • Valid driver’s license with acceptable violation history.

Preferred:

  • Arizona Antiquities Act Archaeological Principal Investigator (PI).
  • Membership in statewide professional associations and/or other evidence of professional engagement in the larger community
  • GIS capabilities
  • Demonstrable technical proficiency with at least one material culture category

Local travel may be required up to 80% of the time.

About the San Jose Conservation Corps (SJCC+CS):

One of the first urban conservation corps in the country, the San Jose Conservation Corps + Charter School was founded in 1987 to empower young adults aged 18 to 27 ("Corpsmembers") to upskill themselves and advance their career in conservation and green spaces. Today, SJCC+CS continues to operate its 1-year-long paid workforce development program, while also functioning as a WASC-accredited charter high school, allowing those who have aged out of the traditional education system to earn their high school diploma.

SJCC+CS offers an engaging work environment focused on growth, teamwork, and making a positive impact. We value collaboration, respect diverse perspectives, and provide opportunities for employees to contribute their skills to create a hopeful and sustainable community. Whether you're passionate about education and development, environmental conservation, or community engagement, joining our team means embracing a shared commitment to service and the chance to make a meaningful difference. Be a part of our mission to create transformational change and learn more at .

Position Summary:

The Field Site Supervisor implements the mission of SJCC+CS by using their leadership, supervisory and technical skills to develop the educational and work skills of young people while preserving the natural landscape of our community. The crew supervisor is responsible for the oversight of various environmental field projects in city and county parks, which may include trail maintenance, invasive species removal, native habitat restoration, beautification, fire fuel reduction, and more. The supervisor is responsible for a team of 4-9 job training Corpsmembers aged 18 to 27.

Job Duties:

General

  • Transport crew to the job site with equipment trailer in tow
  • Work on projects that include some of the following trades: Landscaping, trail maintenance, new trail construction, in-stream enhancement, eradicating non-native plant species, fire fuel reduction, roadside maintenance and safety.
  • Communicate with the project sponsor, sub-contractor, or contractor
  • Organize, direct, and lead a crew of Corpsmembers to work efficiently to complete projects in the allotted timeframe, ensuring a high quality of work
  • Determine manpower levels, material quantities, and equipment requirements for each project
  • Ensure that SJCC+CS policies are upheld and followed on the job site.
  • Collaborate with program staff
  • Participate in spike, backcountry, and emergency response expeditions as needed.

Administration & Safety

  • Complete and upload Corpsmember disciplinary action as needed, and monthly Corpsmember evaluations
  • Complete and submit daily reports, including attendance, safety tailgates, pre and post trip vehicle inspections, end of day report
  • Oversee maintenance of vehicles, keys, gas cards, and registration papers.
  • Conduct tailgate safety meetings on a daily basis and after all work-related accidents, keeping a written record of each meeting
  • Assure that Corpsmembers wear proper safety gear at all times
  • Take appropriate safety precautions in the performance of job duties
  • Complete paperwork for every accident reported, assure that Corpsmembers work safely at all times
  • Communicate vehicle/work-related injuries to the Project Director
  • Identify common safety hazards
  • Read and understand product labels

Corpsmember Development

  • Be a mentor/role model to Corpsmembers while training them skills in different trades
  • Build a good rapport with each Corpsmember
  • Assist Corpsmembers in defining goals and creating a plan to reach those goals
  • Provide constant feedback on Corpsmembers performance including monthly evaluations
  • Consistently apply discipline and accountability as necessary
  • Train Corpsmembers in proper work ethic, attitude, and personal appearance
  • Implement and monitor the Corpsmember education and training plan related to technical and personal skills needed to complete service assignments, including the required training in CPR/First Aid, communication, and conflict resolution

Benefits of Working at SJCC+CS

  • Health: SJCC+CS offers group health insurance through Kaiser, and Dental / Vision insurance through Principal. The organization covers 100% of the premium for staff member’s dental, vision, Long Term Disability, Life, and AD&D insurance.
  • Financial: Retirement savings plan with up to 3% employer match after 1 year of service, credit union membership and benefits, Tuition Reimbursement program for associate or bachelor’s degree, and a Flexible Spending Account for healthcare or dependent care expenses.
  • Time Off: Paid holidays, Vacation, Sick Leave, Bereavement Leave, and Jury Duty leave. Other unpaid leave of absence options are available, such as Medical, Military, Parental, and Family Care Leave.
  • Other: Employee Assistance Program (EAP), Pet Insurance, and Supplemental insurance plans available (Critical Illness, Hospital Indemnity, Short Term Disability, and more).

​​​​​​​Work Environment & Requirements

Position requires sitting, standing, balancing or walking on uneven and slippery surfaces, reaching, twisting, turning, climbing, kneeling, bending, stooping, squatting, crouching, grasping, reaching overhead and making repetitive hand movement in the performance of daily duties. The position also requires both near and far vision when inspecting work and operating assigned equipment, plus the ability to speak and to hear. The ability to lift, carry, push and pull tools, equipment and supplies weighing up to 50 pounds is required. The incumbent in this position works outdoors in all weather conditions, including wet, hot, and cold. In the course of work the incumbent may be exposed to biologic or infectious agents, unpleasant odors, fumes, smoke, dust and air contaminants, and insects. The nature of the work may also require the incumbent to use power, vibration, and noise-producing tools and equipment, drive motorized vehicles, work near moving equipment, vehicles or machinery, work on ladders or scaffolding or at heights. The incumbent may be required to use protective clothing, equipment, or devices, and may work near hostile or offensive individuals. Some of these requirements may be accommodated for otherwise qualified individuals requiring and requesting such accommodations.

Equipment Used: The incumbent of this position will be utilizing various power tools, equipment, and Company vehicles. Vehicles include mainly passenger vans, and occasionally a pickup truck with a trailer or flat bed with the proper training.

Reasonable Accommodations: The San Jose Conservation Corps + Charter is committed to the full inclusion of all qualified individuals. As part of this commitment, SJCC+CS will ensure that persons with disabilities are provided reasonable accommodations. If reasonable accommodation is needed to participate in the job application or interview process, to perform essential job functions, and/or to receive other benefits and privileges of employment, please contact accommodations@sjcccs.org.

title: Clinical Quality Analyst 2
description:

title: Senior Credit Risk Reporting Analyst

GJA 17

Alongside delivering portfolio-wide credit risk reporting, the squad defines and develops the foundations that enable the Credit Risk Reporting team to report consistently, efficiently, and at scale.

Working closely with the Expert Lead, you will help define and implement the future of Credit Risk Reporting. From data architecture and reporting tooling to governance, controls, and reporting standards, you will help translate strategic ambitions into practical, reusable solutions that improve reporting quality, efficiency, and scalability across the Credit Risk Reporting team.

This role offers a unique combination of delivery, transformation, and influence. You will analyse risk, challenge data, improve reporting capabilities, and help establish the standards and frameworks that support the next steps of Credit Risk Reporting.

Your key responsibilities

Portfolio-Wide Credit Risk Reporting

  • Own and enhance portfolio-wide credit risk reporting across ING Belgium portfolios.
  • Lead key reporting deliverables, including Loan Loss Provisioning (LLP), management reporting, and risk committee reporting.
  • Drive regulatory reporting activities, particularly FINREP and related credit risk deliverables.
  • Lead complex data requests from regulators, auditors, and other stakeholders.

Reporting Foundations, Governance & Transformation

  • Shape the future of Credit Risk Reporting by helping define reporting standards, methodologies, and ways of working across the team.
  • Drive simplification, standardisation, automation, and reuse across reporting processes, data solutions, and reporting capabilities.
  • Establish and promote foundations for data architecture, coding standards, reporting tooling, visualisation, and reporting design.
  • Strengthen reporting governance through robust controls, documentation standards, EUC compliance, and data quality assurance.
  • Translate strategic ambitions into practical, scalable, and plug and play solutions that enable efficient delivery across the Credit Risk Reporting team.

Collaboration & Leadership

  • Act as a trusted expert within the Credit Risk Reporting team.
  • Support colleagues with methodologies, standards, and best practices.
  • Help create reusable solutions that can be easily adopted by other reporting analysts.
  • Foster a culture of collaboration, continuous improvement, and high-quality delivery.

We look for

You are a seasoned reporting professional who combines analytical depth with ownership, pragmatism, and a drive to make things better.

You enjoy solving complex problems, creating structure where needed, and turning ideas into practical solutions. You are comfortable challenging the status quo, influencing stakeholders, and translating complexity into clear and actionable outcomes.

You bring

  • Master's degree in Finance, Economics, Statistics, Mathematics, Information Management, or a related discipline.
  • At least 7 years of experience in credit risk reporting, risk analytics, regulatory reporting, or a similar environment.
  • Strong SQL and SAS skills, complemented by experience with Power BI or similar technologies.
  • Sound knowledge of credit risk reporting, IFRS 9, CRR III, and related regulatory frameworks.
  • Experience with reporting frameworks, reporting architecture, or large scale reporting solutions.
  • Understanding of reporting governance, controls, documentation standards, and data quality management.
  • The ability to translate strategy into practical standards, tools, and ways of working.
  • Experience influencing teams and driving standardisation without direct managerial authority.
  • Strong stakeholder management and communication skills.

We offer you

A clear purpose, a unique offer and a range of flexible compensation and other benefits:

  • Personal growth & challenging work with endless opportunities to realize your ambitions
  • An informal, dynamic environment with innovative colleagues supporting your endeavors
  • A progressive and agile way of working, where new ideas are valued ahead of convention

Furthermore, within the CoE Reporting department, you can count on a range of opportunities to invest in your personal and professional growth with:

  • the opportunity to shape the reporting capabilities of the future
  • the support to challenge the status quo at all times
  • a variety of learning possibilities
  • challenging projects and a steep learning curve
  • the possibility to evolve from one job to another easily within CoE reporting, Finance & Risk, in order to build a full knowledge of the business in a major bank.

We redefine banking. What about you?

This is more than a reporting role. You will be part of the squad responsible not only for understanding portfolio-wide credit risk, but also for shaping how Credit Risk Reporting is performed across the team. If you enjoy combining analytical depth, reporting expertise, and tangible impact, this role offers a unique opportunity to influence both what we report and how we report it.

title: Network Program Manager, Preventative Maintenance
description:
At gFiber, we believe that great internet has the power to drive innovation, strengthen communities, enable the impossible, and do all the everyday things that make all of our world go round. And the job of creating better internet is never done - so we’re growing! Our team is committed to building a place where people who want to make a difference can grow their careers and find their spot to belong.

The application window will be open until at least October 18th, 2026. This opportunity will remain online based on business needs which may be before or after the specified date.

This role is not eligible for immigration sponsorship.

Role Description:

Managing critical physical, electrical, and environmental infrastructure across central offices and fiber huts requires dedicated operational governance, vendor alignment, and rigorous change management. The Network PgM - Preventative Maintenance Manager serves as the primary operational coordinator and Tier-1 escalation lead for national hut facility preventative maintenance programs.


This role bridges high-level facility maintenance strategies with daily field execution—leading vendor partners, enforcing standard Methods of Procedure (MOP), submitting and tracking Change Management tickets, and managing emergency break/fix escalations across multiple regional markets.

In this role, you’ll:

Vendor Management & Operational Coordination
  • Partner Alignment: Lead weekly operational syncs with primary maintenance contractors (e.g., Pearce Services) to review site maintenance progress, pending quotes, and operational blockers.
  • Schedule & Dispatch Coordination: Oversee site dispatching across multiple regional markets (e.g., Austin, Nashville, Charlotte, Raleigh-Durham, San Antonio). Ensure vendor field technicians are properly paired with gFiber site escorts when required.
  • Onboarding & Training: Facilitate system access, onboarding, and workflow training for vendor administrative staff, focusing on work order creation, ticketing and billing compliance.

2. Change Management & MOP Governance

  • Ticket Generation & Workflow Lifecycle: Create, assign, and manage Network Scheduled Maintenance tickets within ServiceNow for all scheduled hut facility maintenance.
  • Lead Time Compliance: Enforce strict adherence to change control policy windows (minimum 72-hour advance lead time prior to work execution).
  • MOP Execution & Approval: Maintain, distribute, and enforce standardized Methods of Procedure (MOP) detailing generator servicing, HVAC filter/coolant maintenance, battery health checks, and ATS inspections. Ensure all MOPs are submitted to gFiber sponsors and shared with NOC () prior to window opening.

3. Tier-1 Incident Escalation & Emergency Dispatch

  • First-Level Escalation POC: Serve as the primary point of contact for vendor technicians and local market teams encountering site deficiencies during PM sweeps.
  • Break/Fix & Remediation Management: Identify site failures (e.g., failed ATS motherboards, faulty breakers, coolant/oxygen sensor failures, degraded battery strings) and initiate reactive break/fix work orders.
  • Emergency Dispatching: Coordinate rapid vendor dispatch for emergency hardware replacements and roll-up generator deployments during commercial power outages or major hardware incidents.

At a minimum we’d like you to have:

  • Bachelor's degree or equivalent practical experience.
  • 3 years of experience in telecommunications infrastructure, central office/fiber hut operations, or critical facility operations management.
  • Proven track record leading external vendor contracts, managing field service operations, and facilitating cross-functional team syncs.
  • Experience with enterprise ticketing and change management platforms (ServiceNow, or equivalent).
  • Functional understanding of critical hut infrastructure:
  • Power Systems: Standby diesel/gas generators, Automatic Transfer Switches (ATS), Manual Transfer Switches (MTS), and -48V DC power plants/battery strings.
  • HVAC & Environmental: Wall-mount shelter HVAC units, lead/lag controllers, MERV filtration, refrigerant/coolant loops, and environmental telemetry/sensors.

It’s preferred if you have:

  • Experience transitioning manual operations to Salesforce Field Service Lightning (FSL) or similar ERP/FSM software.
  • Experience serving in 24/7 on-call rotation management or major incident escalation response teams.
  • Demonstrated ability to draft, refine, and enforce operational MOPs and standard operating procedures (SOPs) across multi-regional deployments.

The US base salary for this full-time position is $84,000 - $122,400 + bonus + benefits. As pay varies by location, your recruiter will share more about the specific salary range for your targeted location during the hiring process.

title: Sr Director, Build Partnerships
description:
Role Overview

As a Sr. Director of Build Partnerships, you will lead a team of Partner Managers who build and execute strategic partnerships with ISVs and OEMs that deliver applications and integrated offerings through the ServiceNow Store. You will set the strategy for the team’s partner portfolio, hold the team accountable for partner GNACV, and develop Partner Managers into trusted advisors who can run complex, multi-stakeholder partnerships on their own.

Your team’s success drives partner revenue and strengthens retention and expansion of ServiceNow’s homegrown solutions. You are measured by your team’s NNACV and by the growth of the people you lead.

Key Responsibilities

Team Revenue and Portfolio Ownership

  • Own quarterly and annual partner GNACV targets for the team, with forecasting that leadership can rely on.

  • Review and approve GTM business plans for each partnership, covering technical innovation, sales, marketing, business goals, and forecasts.

  • Identify where the team should grow existing ISV partnerships and where it should enter new ISV markets.

  • Drive strategic enterprise-wide OEM transactions that require executive sponsorship and cross-functional alignment.

Coaching and Talent Development

  • Coach Partner Managers on partnership strategy, deal strategy, QBR quality, and executive engagement through regular 1:1s and deal reviews.

  • Set clear, measurable goals for each team member, separating the outcomes they control from those they influence, and hold each person to the controllable part.

  • Own hiring, onboarding, performance management, and career development for the team.

  • Identify gaps early and address them directly, with documented expectations and follow-through.

Execution Cadence and Accountability

  • Establish and run the team’s operating cadence, including pipeline reviews, forecast calls, and partner business reviews.

  • Standardize partner planning, enablement, and forecasting practices so the team operates consistently across the portfolio.

  • Escalate and resolve partner issues with BUs, Sales, Marketing, Operations, Legal, Solution Consulting, and Product teams.

Partner Relationships and Program Advocacy

  • Lead partner engagement through QBRs and executive check-ins, and represent the team in senior partner conversations.

  • Evangelize the ServiceNow Technology Partnership Program internally and externally.

  • Build the team’s relationships with partner executives so that partnerships survive changes in individual contacts.

Leadership Expectations

  • Hungry and humble: You push the team to fight for every opportunity and stay curious about the market, the technology, and the customer, including what you don’t yet know.

  • Control the controllables: You separate what a Partner Manager can influence from what they can control, and you measure them on the latter. This keeps accountability fair and performance conversations productive.

  • Carry your own weight: You hold yourself and your team to the same standard. When a gap shows up in a forecast, a deal, or a partner relationship, you name it directly and work with the person to close it.

  • Wow the customer, win as a team: Every partner and account conversation should delight the customer and move the team forward. You remove silos and make it easy for Partner Managers to bring in Sales, Solution Consulting, and Product support.

  • Leadership is developing followership: Your success is measured by how many people on your team grow into strong, independent leaders. You invest time in developing their judgment, not just managing their output.

Qualifications

  • 8+ years of experience managing technology partnerships, OEM/ISV relationships, or enterprise software/SaaS alliances, including at least 2 years leading people or teams

  • Proven track record of meeting or exceeding revenue targets through partner or enterprise sales

  • Experience developing and executing strategic GTM plans with partners, covering sales, marketing, and forecasting

  • Demonstrated ability to sell to and influence C-level executives across Product and IT organizations

  • Experience coaching and developing individual contributors into strong performers

  • Experience with AI in work processes, decision-making, or problem-solving, including using AI-driven insights to inform planning and forecasting

  • Strong technical aptitude and the ability to synthesize complex business and technical issues

  • Excellent interpersonal, communication, and leadership skills

  • Prior experience as a first-line manager of Partner Managers, Alliance Managers, or Account Executives

  • Experience selling both application bundles and platform deployments

  • Experience building partner programs, playbooks, or enablement at scale

  • Track record of building high-performing, diverse teams

For positions in this location, we offer a base pay of $197,220 - $325,440, plus equity (when applicable), variable/incentive compensation and benefits. Sales positions generally offer a competitive On Target Earnings (OTE) incentive compensation structure. Please note that the base pay shown is a guideline, and individual total compensation will vary based on factors such as qualifications, skill level, competencies, and work location. We also offer health plans, including flexible spending accounts, a 401(k) Plan with company match, ESPP, matching donations, a flexible time away plan and family leave programs. Compensation is based on the geographic location in which the role is located and is subject to change based on work location.

Work Personas

We approach our distributed world of work with flexibility and trust. Work personas (flexible, remote, or required in office) are categories that are assigned to ServiceNow employees depending on the nature of their work and their assigned work location. Learn more here. To determine eligibility for a work persona, ServiceNow may confirm the distance between your primary residence and the closest ServiceNow office using a third-party service.

ServiceNow is an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, national origin, age, disability, gender identity, veteran status, or any other category protected by law. In addition, all qualified applicants with arrest or conviction records will be considered for employment in accordance with legal requirements.

Accommodations

We strive to create an accessible and inclusive experience for all candidates. If you require a reasonable accommodation to complete any part of the application process, or are unable to use this online application and need an alternative method to apply, please contact globaltalentss@servicenow.com for assistance.

Export Control Regulations

For positions requiring access to controlled technology subject to export control regulations, including the U.S. Export Administration Regulations (EAR), ServiceNow may be required to obtain export control approval from government authorities for certain individuals. All employment is contingent upon ServiceNow obtaining any export license or other approval that may be required by relevant export control authorities.

title: Software Engineer
description:
RE:LAB is a design and innovation company specialized in shaping the interaction between people and complex technologies.

Since 2004, we have been working on products and systems used daily across the automotive, industrial, and consumer sectors. Our goal is to make advanced technology understandable, safe, and natural to use.

We don’t just design interfaces. We design experiences that bring together design, engineering, human factors, and artificial intelligence. Our multidisciplinary team tackles real-world challenges in highly complex contexts, where quality and reliability are essential.

We partner with global companies when user experience is not a detail, but a critical factor for a product’s success—when adoption, safety, and user trust truly make the difference.

At RE:LAB, we believe technology should feel human. This belief guides the way we work, the design decisions we make, and the relationships we build every day.

Designing human experiences for complex technologies.

Posizione

We are looking for a Software Engineer to join our team and contribute to the design, development, and integration of software solutions for embedded systems, user interfaces, and back-end applications.

The selected candidate will work closely with developers, designers, and system specialists, contributing to all stages of the software development lifecycle, from requirements analysis to validation and maintenance.

Main Activities

  • Design and develop C/C++ software for applications and embedded systems, ensuring performance, reliability, and integration.
  • Develop user interfaces using Qt/QML and JavaScript, focusing on usability and integration with back-end services, REST APIs, and databases.
  • Develop, simulate, and validate signal processing algorithms and digital filters, including through MATLAB/Simulink, and port them to the target platform.
  • Develop and manage back-end components and databases, integrating them with existing systems and applications.
  • Perform software testing, debugging, profiling, and optimization, helping resolve technical issues.
  • Maintain code documentation, version control, and software change management, while contributing to activity planning.

Requisiti

  • Master’s degree in Computer Engineering, Computer Science, Electronic Engineering, or a related field.
  • Advanced C++ skills, including object-oriented programming, multithreading, and synchronization, with experience in embedded C/C++ development.
  • Experience with Qt/QML, JavaScript, UI/UX and usability principles, and REST API integration.
  • Knowledge of Embedded Linux and communication buses and protocols, including Modbus, I2C, UART, and SPI.
  • Skills in algorithm design, signal processing, and digital filters, with proficiency in MATLAB/Simulink for development, simulation, and validation.
  • Experience designing and managing relational and real-time databases; knowledge of SQL, Python, Java, PHP, Node.js, and major back-end frameworks.
  • Proficiency in debugging, profiling, and version control using Git/CVS.
  • Strong teamwork, problem-solving, planning, and technical communication skills, with a results-oriented approach and fluency in technical English.
  • Availability for occasional travel, subject to project needs and prior agreement.

Altre informazioni

Schedule: Full- time, 40 hours per week.

Location: Ancona, on-site.

Our Promise

We build technology for people-and that same principle guides how we work together. At RE:LAB, you’ll find more than a role: a place where ideas are valued, growth is supported, and individual perspectives contribute to meaningful innovation.

Our Values in Action

  • Integrity first: we act with transparency and responsibility in every decision, project, and interaction.
  • Diversity as a strength: different backgrounds and viewpoints help us solve complex problems better.
  • Inclusion by design: we encourage open dialogue and create space for everyone to contribute.
  • Growth mindset: we support continuous learning and professional development through real projects and shared expertise.

Ready to shape the future of human-machine interaction?

Join a team that values both advanced technology and human connection.

description:
BUILD YOUR CAREER WITH SALT RIVER RESTORATION!

Salt River Restoration is growing, and we're looking for an experienced Mitigation Technician who wants more than just a job.

Who We Are

The Trust & Safety Group builds technology that keeps Singapore's online spaces safe. As part of this group, the GovTech Anti-Scam Products (GASP) team develops solutions to detect, disrupt and deter scammers at scale — spanning data infrastructure, AI/ML-powered proactive detection, partner API integrations, and front-end systems for enforcement agencies. Beyond scams, our work extends to tackling terrorism, child sexual exploitation material, youth and family digital wellbeing, and AI safety risks and deepfakes.

Who Are We Looking For

Bring your engineering expertise and problem-solving ability to fighting scams with technology. You will deliver features that span multiple components, make sound trade-offs between speed, quality and maintainability, and take growing ownership of the systems you build.

We use cloud services and open source wherever possible: AWS, React / React Native, and a mix of SQL/NoSQL databases, among others. Knowing what to build versus what to reuse lets us focus on delivering value rather than re-solving solved problems.

As a software engineer, you will:

  • Build POCs and features spanning multiple components to demonstrate technological opportunities.
  • Contribute to system architecture and design decisions, with mentorship on cross-component trade-offs.
  • Write and review production-quality code, and expand test coverage across key workflows.
  • Contribute to CI/CD pipelines, manage cloud deployments, and own observability for what you ship (logging, metrics, SLIs/SLOs).
  • Participate in incident triage and resolution, escalating complex issues appropriately.
  • Use AI-assisted coding tools to accelerate delivery, reviewing AI-generated code to the same bar as human-authored code.

[Requirements]

Must have

  • Python, JavaScript and/or TypeScript
  • Strong knowledge of AWS Cloud
  • Strong knowledge of algorithms and data structures
  • Ability to deliver moderately complex, multi-component features with growing independence
  • Good knowledge of IaC (such as Terraform)
  • Experience with creating GitLab CI/CD templates for different use cases

Preferred

  • Running containers or serverless services
  • Building high-scale, low-latency APIs and deploying scaled AI/ML solutions
  • Data-intensive frameworks and data warehousing (e.g. AWS Glue, Spark); bonus for graph databases (e.g. Neo4j)
  • Event-driven and streaming architectures using SQS/SNS/EventBridge; bonus for Kinesis

We're here to improve how we live as a society through what we can offer as a government. Because our team focuses on pushing new initiatives, you will also:

  • Help identify potential projects that improve the public good
  • Contribute to designing systems that work within real-world constraints
  • Explain technical ideas to teammates and partner agencies

You're not just here to write code, but also to help figure out what we should be building and how we should build it. You will work on meaningful projects to reduce scams and make a big impact on people's lives.

What It Is Like Working Here

  • Rapid Prototyping - Instead of spending too much time debating ideas we prefer testing them. This identifies potential problems quickly, and more importantly, conveys what is possible to others easily.
  • Ownership - In addition to technical responsibilities, this means having opinions on what is being done and ideas on what should be done next. Building something that you believe in is the best way to build something good.
  • Continuous Learning - Working on new ideas often means not fully understanding what you are working on. Taking time to learn new architectures, frameworks, technologies, and even languages is not just encouraged but essential.

description:
Job Description: School Psychologist II

The Opportunity:

Position: Permanent, Full-Time

Hours: 36.25 hours per week, Monday – Friday

Reports to: Director of Education Support Services Location: Moncton Area Schools

Union: New Brunswick Union of Private & Public Employees (NBUPPE) 202-e.pdf

Salary: School Psychologist I ($3667.04 - $4415.76) - School Psychologist II ($3850.35 - $4636.51)

Location: Serving Anglophone East School District

The successful candidate will offer professional psychological services in schools and at the District level, focusing on student learning, behavior, assessment, evaluation, and understanding child and adolescent exceptionalities and psychological adjustment. A District-Based School Psychologist plays a crucial role in supporting students and school teams through a variety of services and interventions. Utilizing the Response to Intervention (RTI) model, they help identify the needs of students and guide the implementation of appropriate interventions at the tier 3 level.

Collaboration is key to their role. District-Based School Psychologists work closely with school-based Education Support Services (ESS) Teams and District ESS (Coordinators, Speech-Language Pathologists, Resource Specialists in Assessment and Intervention (RSAI) and Leads) to ensure a coordinated approach to student support. They also liaise with C&Y Team Psychologists and team members to address academic, behavioral, and mental health needs, ensuring a holistic approach to student well-being.

Through ongoing assessment, consultation, and collaboration, District-Based School Psychologists help create a positive and inclusive school climate, helping to foster the academic, social, and emotional growth of all students.

Must have reliable transportation and be able to travel frequently within the district; this role may require significant travel on a regular basis.


Description:
Under the direction of the Director of Education Support Services, the District based School Psychologist I or ll will be responsible to:

· Respond to DESS Requests for services as directed by the Director of ESS and or their designates.
· Provide a broad range of professional psychological services in the school system in the application of the science of psychology to the areas of student learning and behavior, understanding of child and adolescent exceptionalities and psychological adjustment.
· Consult with teachers, administrators, other school and District personnel, and parents in a collaborative process of defining problems and developing appropriate programs and interventions.
· Conduct and support individual student psychological assessments, in-service education, participation in the development and implementation of preventive and crisis response programs, and program evaluation.
· Other duties as assigned
· Travel within the District is required.

School Psychologist II ($3850.35 - $4636.51)


Definition
The School Psychologist II is responsible for the delivery of professional psychological services within a school district or education center. This will involve, in collaboration with district administrators, the responsibility for the planning, organization, and evaluation of psychological services within the district. It may involve the direct clinical and administrative supervision of Psychologists, Residents in Psychology and Psychometrists within the school district and/or education center. In addition to the functions of the School Psychologist I, this classification maintains appropriate professional relationships with various community agencies in order to coordinate professional psychological services within the school system.

Qualifications
A Master’s or Doctoral degree in Psychology with course work and experience to meet the requirements for licensed membership in the College of Psychologists of New Brunswick and considerable (3 to 6 years) related experience in school psychology. Successful completions of course work in child and adolescent development as well as child and adolescent exceptionalities are required. Experience in school psychology is desirable.

Necessary Special Requirements
Licensed membership in the College of Psychologists of New Brunswick.

Where skill, qualifications and ability are relatively equal amongst union applicants, the vacancy will be filled on the basis of seniority within the bargaining unit. title: Scientist I, Medicinal Chemistry
description:
Revolution Medicines is a global, commercial-state oncology company dedicated to discovering, developing and delivering innovative medicines for patients with RAS-addicted cancers. Leveraging its differentiated RAS(ON) tri-complex inhibitor platform, the company is advancing a broad, integrated portfolio of oral RAS(ON) inhibitors designed to directly target the active, cancer-driving state of RAS. Founded on rigorous scientific inquiry and a willingness to challenge long-held assumptions, Revolution Medicines is committed to changing the trajectory of disease for patients with RAS-addicted cancers worldwide.

Our people are united by a shared way of working: follow the science, challenge assumptions, act with urgency and hold ourselves to a high standard of rigor—all in service of patients.

The Opportunity:

Revolution Medicines is seeking a scientifically talented individual to join our world-class Discovery Research organization as a Scientist I, Medicinal Chemistry.   • Strong written and verbal communication skills to work with interdepartmental teams.

title: Durable Medical Equipment Fitter
description:
Park Nicollet welcomes applications for a Durable Medical Equipment Fitter at our TRIA Orthopedics location in Woodbury. Come join us as a Partner for Good and help us make an impact on the care and experience that our patients and their families receive every day.

The Durable Medical Equipment (DME) Fitter places and fits physician-recommended durable medical soft goods on patients. This role is responsible for product knowledge and complex billing rules surrounding a variety of medical equipment and supplies, maintaining inventory, and maintaining and cleaning department equipment. With a focus on patient experience, the DME Fitter asks clarifying questions to identify patient needs and effectively promote our products and service, ensuring that the patient is trained in the use and care of the product.

Additionally, the DME Fitter gathers documentation required for billing, contacts insurance for prior authorization, schedules appointments for patient product pickup, and maintains documentation and patient files. This position reviews the daily OR schedule, provides training on DME products to clinic staff, and maintains the DME schedule.

Work Schedule:

  • Day shift, varied schedule.

Required Qualifications:

  • One year of sales or customer service experience in a DME or business environment with high service standards.

  • Certified Fitter required after 1000 hours DME experience.

  • BOC certification required within 8 months of hire.

  • COF certification required within 8 months of hire.

  • State of Minnesota licensure required within 8 months of hire.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Sales and customer service training.

  • Basic PC knowledge including Windows and Microsoft Outlook.

  • Experience with inventory management, electronic healthcare management software, merchandising, and performing retail transactions.

  • Knowledge of home medical supplies and equipment, product lines, and insurance guidelines for reimbursement.

Additional Information:

This is a non-union 1.0 FTE (80 hours per pay period) day shift position, working in Woodbury, MN. The full salary range for this position is $22.66-$34.00 per hour, based on experience and internal equity. This position is non-exempt under the Fair Labor Standards Act, and is eligible for benefits. Park Nicollet offers a competitive benefits package that includes medical and dental insurance (which begin on the first day of the month following start), 401(k) with match, time away from work, disability insurance, fertility benefits, tuition reimbursement, an employee assistance program, and much more! Park Nicollet is also a qualified nonprofit employer under the federal Public Service Loan Forgiveness program.

title: Document Compliance Coordinator - Active Security Clearance Required
description:
We have an opening for a Document Compliance Coordinator to navigate a complex matrix of federal, institutional and organizational requirements. You will collaborate with engineers and subject matter experts to initiate, develop, document and evaluate comprehensive technical procedures, documents and safety plans. This position will support the Superblock (SBK) facility within the Strategic Deterrence Directorate.

This position may offer a hybrid schedule, which includes the flexibility to work from home one or more days per week, after a probationary period. The specifics of the hybrid schedule, including the exact number of days required in the office and virtual work options, may vary based on the needs of the team and the organization.

You will

  • Analyze, develop, and implement documentation processes, procedures, and practices to ensure activities within the facility are performed in compliance with requirements in federal regulations, institutional procedures, and the facility safety bases.
  • Independently evaluate complex procedures and process documents to resolve implementation gaps and verify facility requirements are adequately implemented, safety-basis controls are maintained, and required technical and management reviews are conducted.
  • Serve as subject matter expert on technical document control; interpret and analyze data to provide recommendations to senior management.
  • Collaborate with subject matter experts, facility management, training, and SBK staff to lead the review, revision, and release of operational procedures through established change control processes affecting facility operations, systems, and LLNL programs.
  • Monitor and oversee document tracking and routing, and ensure revision control using electronic applications (e.g., Enterprise Lifecycle Management-Unclassified [ELM-U]/Windchill) for configuration management of documents.
  • Identify, establish, monitor, and analyze internal performance metrics; provide reports and recommendations to the SBK Document Compliance Manager.
  • Develop, lead, and implement strategies for addressing process improvement initiatives that impact major mission areas.
  • Lead and coordinate complex special projects supporting document management; represent the facility on related programmatic, directorate, and Laboratory-wide initiatives.
  • Perform other duties as assigned.
  • This position requires an active Department of Energy (DOE) Q-level clearance or active Top-Secret clearance issued by another U.S. government agency at the time of hire.
  • Bachelor’s degree in communications, English or a related field, or equivalent combination of education and relevant experience.
  • Advanced technical composition, writing and editing skills and experience effectively composing professional documentation.
  • Experience interpreting, reviewing, and analyzing procedures to determine if the activities they address are performed in compliance with complex regulations and requirements.
  • Demonstrated ability to manage cross-functional work, influence stakeholders, and resolve sensitive issues with tact and judgment.
  • Strong collaboration and communication skills with the ability to work effectively across multidisciplinary teams.
  • Ability to manage multiple competing priorities, and to apply project management principles to organize, coordinate, sequence, and accomplish work.
  • Experience applying advanced organizational skills, demonstrating attention to detail, accuracy, and follow through.
  • Strong proficiency in Microsoft Word and a solid working knowledge of Excel, FileMaker Pro, Adobe Acrobat, and EDMS (such as SharePoint or Windchill) with the ability to learn new software quickly.

Qualifications We Desire

  • Procedure Writer Certification (Professional Procedure Association).
  • Experience with Superblock policies, procedures, and operating practices.

Pay Range

$136,020 - $166,584 Annually

This is the lowest to highest salary we in good faith believe we would pay for this role at the time of this posting. An employee’s position within the salary range will be based on several factors including, but not limited to, specific competencies, relevant education, qualifications, certifications, experience, skills, seniority, geographic location, performance, and business or organizational needs.
