title: Associate Director, Biotherapeutic Production and Characterization
description:
The Role:

The Associate Director will lead a talented scientific team working at the intersection of biological engineering, protein science, automation, and data-enabled discovery. You will help define how difficult and diverse protein targets are designed, produced, characterized, and delivered to project teams with greater speed, scale, quality, and scientific insight, working at the intersection of biological engineering, protein science, automation, and data-enabled discovery. Your leadership will directly influence critical program decisions, the success of novel protein modalities in discovery, the technologies and capabilities we build, and the inclusive, high-performance culture we create.

At Generate:Biomedicines, this is an opportunity to combine deep experimental science with agentic design, automation, and high-throughput experimentation to tackle some of the most complex challenges in protein design and production. You will develop novel solutions for difficult-to-express antigens, membrane proteins, and other complex modalities, building workflows that connect sequence and structure to construct design, production, characterization, and scientific learning at scale.

As Associate Director, Biotherapeutic Production & Characterization, you will lead protein production, purification, and fit-for-purpose characterization in support of discovery and early development. You will be accountable for delivering high-quality, assay-ready protein reagents and actionable data that support critical program decisions, while advancing the technologies, data practices, and team capabilities needed to expand what we can design and produce.

Here's how you will contribute:

  • Oversee production across mammalian, bacterial, and cell-free systems, including end-to-end workflows for construct design, expression, purification, characterization, quality control, normalization, and assay-ready handoff.
  • Drive innovation for difficult antigens and complex proteins through construct and boundary optimization, tag and format selection, alternate expression systems, site-specific labeling, automation, and other enabling technologies.
  • Establish fit-for-purpose production, purification, and characterization standards for attributes including yield, purity, aggregation, concentration, identity, oligomeric state, stability, and biotinylation.
  • Lead portfolio planning, prioritization, and resource allocation for the team across internal and outsourced production and characterization activities, balancing program delivery, platform advancement, capacity, timelines, and external spend.
  • Manage relationships with CROs, technology providers, and other external partners, and communicate progress, risks, resource needs, and tradeoffs to senior stakeholders.
  • Represent Biotherapeutic Production & Characterization on cross-functional program and platform teams, translating scientific objectives into actionable strategies and recommendations.
  • Lead adoption of automation, structured data practices, AI/ML-enabled tools, and agentic workflows while driving operational excellence through prioritization, resource planning, metrics, risk management, and continuous improvement.

Leadership Responsibilities:

  • Lead, coach, and develop a high-performing team spanning protein construct design, molecular biology, expression, purification, characterization, and protein reagent operations.
  • Establish clear expectations for scientific quality, delivery, collaboration, and accountability.
  • Ensure team members understand how their work contributes to program, functional, and organizational priorities.
  • Provide timely, constructive feedback and create equitable opportunities for technical development, leadership growth, increased responsibility, and career progression.
  • Build a culture in which technical excellence, inclusion, integrity, urgency, and collaboration are expected and reinforced.

The Ideal Candidate will have:

  • PhD in biochemistry, molecular biology, chemical engineering, bioengineering, protein sciences, or a related discipline, with 8 years of relevant industry experience; or an M.S. in a related discipline with 10 years of relevant industry experience.
  • Demonstrated success leading and developing scientific teams within a biotechnology or pharmaceutical environment.
  • Experience producing or characterizing complex biologics, including multispecific antibodies.
  • Expert technical knowledge across protein expression, purification, and characterization, with the judgment to guide complex scientific decisions and resolve cross-workflow challenges.
  • Strong experience with construct design and optimization, protein formats, boundary engineering, affinity tags, or site-specific labeling strategies.
  • Strong experience with mammalian expression systems; experience with cell-free or other specialized systems is valuable.
  • Strong expertise in protein-purification methods, including affinity capture, size-exclusion chromatography, and other methods used to generate high-quality research or assay-enabling material.
  • Strong understanding of fit-for-purpose analytical and biochemical characterization methods used to evaluate protein purity, aggregation, concentration, identity, stability, oligomeric state, and related quality attributes.
  • Experience establishing and managing productive relationships with CROs, vendors, or other external technology partners.
  • A track record of improving workflows, implementing new technologies, and increasing throughput, reproducibility, material quality, or operational efficiency.
  • Strong resource-planning and prioritization skills, including the ability to manage competing program needs, internal capacity, timelines, external partnerships, and approved spending plans.
  • Demonstrated ability to apply advanced judgment to highly complex scientific and operational problems, assess incomplete or conflicting information, and make sound decisions with meaningful program impact.

About Generate:Biomedicines

We are a clinical-stage generative biology company pioneering the AI revolution in drug design and development. We are advancing a new approach to drug creation—one grounded in the ability to design proteins with defined biological intent. By integrating machine learning with large-scale experimentation, this approach aims to reduce the uncertainty, time, and cost associated with developing protein-based medicines.

Founded in 2018, we are advancing a growing pipeline of clinical and preclinical programs across multiple disease areas and protein modalities. By unifying computational design and clinical development within a single operating model, we translate this approach into clinical-stage programs and are leading a shift from traditional drug discovery toward systematic drug generation.

At Generate:Biomedicines, we collaborate across disciplines in new ways to invent and innovate. We bring diverse perspectives to a shared goal of delivering better medicines to patients in need, faster, guided by our values and leadership behaviors.

title: Vil du være med til at udvikle både partiorganisationen og sekretariatet i et ungt politisk parti?
description:
Moderaterne søger en stærk leder, der vil være med til at udvikle både partiorganisationen og sekretariatet – og skabe gode rammer for medlemmer, frivillige, tillidsvalgte, ledere og medarbejdere.

Vi er et ungt parti, der på få år har bygget en landsdækkende organisation, gennemført valg og fået en central rolle i dansk politik. Nu skal vi tage næste skridt: Organisationen skal stå stærkere lokalt, vores frivillige skal have bedre rammer for at lykkes, og vi skal fortsat udvikle måden, man bygger og driver et moderne politisk parti på.

Derfor søger vi en chef for Parti og Organisation, som får ansvaret for et team med opgaver inden for organisationsudvikling, lokal partiorganisation, økonomi, HR, IT og digitalisering samt internationale relationer.

Du refererer til partisekretæren og bliver en del af sekretariatets ledelse.

Din vigtigste opgave er at udvikle partiorganisationen

Du skal først og fremmest have lyst til at arbejde med mennesker og organisation. Moderaternes organisation består ikke kun af medarbejdere på Christiansborg. Den består også af medlemmer, frivillige, lokalforeninger, kandidater, folkevalgte og tillidsvalgte over hele landet. De har forskellige roller og behov – og organisationen fungerer kun, hvis samspillet mellem dem gør.

Du får en central rolle i arbejdet med at gøre det lettere og mere meningsfuldt at engagere sig i Moderaterne og i at skabe stærkere rammer for den lokale organisation.

Det indebærer blandt andet, at du skal:

  • udvikle og styrke Moderaternes lokale organisation og samarbejdet med frivillige og tillidsvalgte

  • skabe struktur og fremdrift i organisatoriske udviklingsprojekter

  • sikre gode processer omkring blandt andet medlemsorganisation, valgopstillinger og organisatoriske fora

  • understøtte samspillet mellem den landsdækkende organisation, den politiske ledelse og sekretariatet

  • være med til at omsætte partiets strategiske prioriteter til konkret organisatorisk udvikling

Du skal også være med til at udvikle sekretariatet

Rollen handler ikke kun om organisationen uden for Christiansborg. Du får også en vigtig opgave i at skabe bedre rammer for ledere og medarbejdere i sekretariatet og sikre, at organisation, drift og udvikling hænger bedre sammen.

Det betyder blandt andet, at du skal være med til at:

  • skabe tydelige og velfungerende processer på tværs af sekretariatet

  • styrke samspillet og udnytte synergierne mellem sekretariatet og den øvrige partiorganisation

  • identificere områder, hvor vi kan arbejde smartere, mere sammenhængende og med mindre unødig administration

  • sikre, at udviklingsinitiativer bliver forankret i den daglige organisation og kommer ud at leve

Du skal være leder

Du får personaleansvar for et team med forskellige fagligheder og skal skabe tydelig retning, prioritering og arbejdsdeling.

Vi leder derfor efter en person, der trives med ledelse i praksis: at sætte mål, følge op, udvikle medarbejdere og tage ansvar, når noget skal prioriteres eller besluttes.

Du behøver ikke selv være specialist på alle teamets fagområder. Til gengæld skal du kunne samle dem, stille de rigtige spørgsmål og sikre, at tingene bliver gennemført.

Du skal være med til at udvikle fremtidens partiorganisation

Hos Moderaterne er vi nysgerrige på nye måder at udvikle og drive et politisk parti på. Det kan være gennem bedre brug af data og teknologi, nye måder at engagere medlemmer og frivillige på, smartere processer eller ved at bruge AI til at løse opgaver hurtigere og bedre.

Du behøver ikke selv være teknologispecialist. Men du skal være nysgerrig på mulighederne og have lyst til at omsætte nye værktøjer og idéer til noget, der rent faktisk virker i hverdagen.

Økonomi og governance

Teamet har også ansvar for en række af partiets centrale drifts- og governancefunktioner. Det gælder blandt andet økonomi og HR. Du skal derfor have en solid økonomisk forståelse og være i stand til at tage ansvar for budgetter, økonomiopfølgning, leverandører og beslutningsgrundlag, mens den daglige drift på økonomiområdet varetages eksternt.

Du kommer også til at arbejde tæt med partiets organisatoriske og politiske ledelse og skal være tryg ved formelle beslutningsprocesser og governance. Erfaring med eksempelvis hovedbestyrelser, forretningsudvalg, bestyrelser, medlemsorganisationer eller lignende vil derfor være en klar fordel.

Vi forestiller os, at du

  • har solid erfaring fra en medlemsorganisation, politisk organisation, NGO, interesseorganisation eller en anden organisation, hvor frivillige spiller en væsentlig rolle

  • både forstår og holder af arbejdet med frivillige, medlemmer og tillidsvalgte

  • har ledelseserfaring og kan skabe tydelighed, motivation og fremdrift i et team

  • har erfaring med governance, bestyrelser eller andre formelle beslutningsprocesser

  • har god økonomiforståelse og kan tage ansvar for budgetter og økonomiopfølgning

  • er nysgerrig på teknologi, AI og nye organisatoriske arbejdsformer

  • har blik for, hvordan nye idéer kan omsættes til konkret praksis

  • kan bevæge dig sikkert mellem strategi og konkret eksekvering

  • er en stærk relationsbygger og kan samarbejde med mennesker med meget forskellige roller og perspektiver

  • arbejder struktureret og får processer helt i mål

  • trives i en politisk organisation, hvor tempoet til tider er højt, og virkeligheden kan ændre sig hurtigt

Det er en fordel, hvis du har erfaring fra politik eller en politisk organisation, men det vigtigste er, at du forstår dynamikken i en organisation, hvor både ansatte, frivillige og valgte skal lykkes sammen.

Vi tilbyder

En central lederrolle i et parti, der fortsat er under opbygning – og hvor der derfor er reel mulighed for at præge både organisationen og måden, vi arbejder på.

Du bliver en del af et engageret sekretariat på Christiansborg og får et tæt samarbejde med både partiets ledelse, folketingsgruppen og organisationen rundt om i landet.

Vi har høje ambitioner, korte beslutningsveje og en uformel hverdag. Og vi leder efter en kollega, der både har lyst til at skabe resultater nu og være med til at bygge en stærkere og mere moderne organisation for de kommende år.

Ansøgning og kontakt

Ansøg via nedenstående link senest 26. oktober 2026. Løn gives efter kvalifikationer.

Hvis du har spørgsmål til stillingen, er du velkommen til at kontakte Partisekretær, Katrine DiBona på mail katrine.dibona@ft.dk.

Vi glæder os til at modtage din ansøgning.

title: Ophthalmic Technician, Full Time, Ophthalmology
description:
Adventist Health Ukiah Valley has been deeply connected to the community we serve since 1956. We are comprised of a 50-bed acute care medical center, level IV trauma center, level II intensive care nursery services, extensive physical rehabilitation program, outpatient surgery and diagnostic center and advanced wound care center. Ukiah is a unique small town that charms you with its rich character, arts, vineyards and natural surroundings. Ukiah beckons you to explore all that the valley has to offer amidst our 300 days of sunshine each year. We are also conveniently located just two hours north of San Francisco and 45 minutes from the Pacific Coast.

Job Summary:

Assists ophthalmologist and other technical support personnel to perform diagnostic tests necessary for evaluation of patient eye problems. Assists ophthalmologists in identifying, diagnosing, and treating illnesses, diseases and conditions of the eye.

Job Requirements:

Education and Work Experience:

  • High School Education/GED or equivalent: Required
  • Associate’s/Technical Degree or equivalent combination of education/related experience: Preferred
  • Ophthalmic Technician or Medical Assistant experience: Preferred

Licenses/Certifications:

  • Ophthalmic Technician certification: Preferred

Facility Specific License/Certifications:

  • Basic Life Support (BLS) certification from approved vendor per AH policy: Required

Essential Functions:

  • Screens walk-in patients, emergency patients and telephone calls from patients and referring physicians to determine appropriate physician and priority of appointments. Administers Electro-retinogram, Electro-oculogram tests and specular microscopy examinations to patients.
  • Performs preliminary screening examinations for physician review including, but not limited to, central and peripheral visual field tests; ocular motility tests; color vision tests; pharmacological pupil tests; tests to determine intraocular pressure and pupil testing for size, equality and reaction prior to dilation. Examines the cornea, lens and anterior chamber of the eye using a slit lamp and note variations from normal. Assists physician in preparation of routine microbiological specimens and in various research studies.
  • Measures acuity of patient, with and without glasses, for distance and near vision. Obtains optical and lensometry measurements to determine lens prescription and correct acuity problems. Records findings on patient chart. Obtains topographical measurements of the eye to include corneal diameter and curvature; assist physician to fit patients with contact lenses and to evaluate lens fit with a bio-microscope. Instructs patients on the proper techniques used in caring for, inserting and wearing contact lenses.
  • Directs the flow of patients. Obtains medical and personal data for patient charts. Screens patients for conditions excluding ocular examination. Arranges for laboratory and other tests, ophthalmic photography, outpatient studies and patient admissions and surgery as requested by physician. Alleviates patient and family concerns by explaining diagnostic procedures and method of treatment.
  • Calibrates and maintains all instruments; clean and stock consultation rooms and microbiology laboratory with drugs and other supplies as needed. Sterilizes and sets up instruments for ophthalmic surgical procedures. Assists with minor office surgery, laser treatments and operating room surgery as required.
  • Performs other job-related duties as assigned.

Adventist Health participates in E-Verify. Visit https://adventisthealth.org/careers/everify/ for more information about E-Verify. By choosing to apply, you acknowledge that you have accessed and read the E-Verify Participation and Right to Work notices and understand the contents therein.

title: MEDICATION SPECIALIST
description:
JOB SUMMARY

The Medication Specialist supports the safe, accurate, and timely administration or observation, documentation, monitoring, storage, and disposal of resident medications during assigned shifts, within the authorized scope of the position. Working collaboratively with the Nurse Practitioner (NP), Clinical Coordinator, and clinical team, this position maintains medication records, supports resident access to healthcare services, and follows agency policy and applicable medication-management requirements.

ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES:

  • Respond promptly to resident medication needs and concerns during assigned shifts and obtain clinical, medical, supervisory, or emergency assistance when a concern exceeds the position’s authority or training.

  • Maintain and update Medication Administration Records (MAR) for assigned residents, ensuring documentation is complete, accurate, timely, and compliant with agency requirements.

  • Conduct weekly reviews of medication records, resident medication needs, medical appointments, documentation gaps, and significant medication-related concerns.

  • Assist with internal and external audit processes and correction of identified medication-documentation deficiencies in accordance with agency policy and applicable requirements.

  • Complete incident reports for medication errors, missed medication activities, documentation concerns, adverse events, or other reportable issues, documenting the concern, actions taken, notifications, follow-up, and known outcome.

  • Coordinate and schedule medical appointments for residents with the Nurse Practitioner (NP), ensuring efficient access to care.

  • Monitor and document resident adherence to medication schedules and promptly notify appropriate clinical or medical staff of missed doses, refusals, non-adherence, or other concerns.

  • Administer, observe, or support medication activities only within the employee’s authorized scope and ensure required documentation is completed during the assigned shift.

  • Perform other job-related duties within the authorized scope of the position as assigned by management or requested by supervisors.

  • Consistently uphold the Hope Haven Code of Ethics and Client Rights, demonstrating professionalism and commitment to resident care.

  • Maintain compliance with agency policies, procedures, standards, and applicable medication-management requirements while upholding organizational values and resident rights.

  • Seek direction when a requested duty exceeds the position’s training, certification, competency, supervision, delegation, or authorized scope.

  • Complete or support medication disposal only within the authorized scope of the position and in accordance with established procedures; accurately document disposal and promptly report expired, discontinued, damaged, missing, or unaccounted-for medications.

title: Information Security Engineer - DevSecOps
description:
About the Team

You will be part of the Enterprise Cyber Security organization responsible for protecting Williams-Sonoma, Inc. through reliable, scalable security platforms and automation. The Security DevSecOps function partners with Security Operations, Incident Response, Threat Intelligence, Security Engineering, Identity & Access Management, and Infrastructure to build software and integrations that improve the effectiveness of enterprise security operations.

The team’s mission is to reduce repetitive manual work, strengthen response capabilities, and deliver secure, maintainable software and automation that support our associates, customers, and business.

About the Role

As an Information Security Engineer - DevSecOps, you will design, develop, deploy, and support SOAR playbooks, workflow automations, platform integrations, and custom applications used by the Enterprise Cyber Security team. This is a hands-on engineering role with end-to-end responsibility for solution design, coding, testing, deployment, documentation, and production support. You will balance SOAR development, security automation, and custom software development while working closely with operational teams to translate security requirements into dependable technical solutions.

Responsibilities

  • Design, develop, test, deploy, and maintain SOAR playbooks and response workflows in Google SecOps SOAR and Palo Alto Cortex XSOAR.

  • Build custom security applications, reusable services, scripts, and workflow automations that improve investigation, enrichment, triage, and response processes.

  • Develop and maintain secure integrations using REST APIs, JSON, webhooks, and platform SDKs across Google SecOps SIEM, CrowdStrike, Tanium, Ping Identity, Delinea, MISP, and other enterprise systems.

  • Own the full software development lifecycle, including requirements analysis, solution design, source control, testing, release management, documentation, and ongoing production maintenance.

  • Apply Python and PowerShell to automate repeatable security operations tasks; use Git and CI/CD practices to manage versioning, code review, and controlled releases.

  • Use Docker and container-based development practices, and Terraform or other infrastructure-as-code approaches where appropriate for repeatable deployments.

  • Partner with SOC, Incident Response, Threat Intelligence, Security Engineering, IAM, and Infrastructure teams to identify automation opportunities and translate operational needs into technical requirements.

  • Troubleshoot failed playbooks, API integrations, custom applications, and production workflows; conduct root-cause analysis and implement durable fixes.

  • Build appropriate safeguards into automations, including least-privilege access, credential protection, audit logging, error handling, testing, approval gates, and rollback procedures for disruptive actions.

  • Participate in an on-call rotation supporting production SOAR automations, integrations, and custom security applications.

  • Evaluate AI-assisted development and agentic automation opportunities, applying human review, security controls, and validation before production adoption.

  • Maintain clear technical documentation, runbooks, and knowledge transfer materials to support reliable operations and cross-team collaboration.

Criteria

  • 3+ years of experience in information security engineering, software development, DevSecOps, security automation, or a related technical discipline.

  • Bachelor's degree in Computer Science or related field, or equivalent work experience.

  • Hands-on software development and scripting experience using Python and PowerShell, with working knowledge of REST APIs and JSON.

  • Experience building, testing, and maintaining automation workflows, platform integrations, or custom applications in production environments.

  • Working knowledge of SIEM, SOAR, endpoint security, identity, and threat intelligence concepts and operational workflows.

  • Experience with Git-based source control, CI/CD practices, software testing, and secure development principles.

  • Familiarity with Docker or containers and infrastructure-as-code tools such as Terraform.

  • Strong analytical, troubleshooting, documentation, and communication skills; ability to work effectively across security and infrastructure teams.

  • Willingness to participate in an on-call rotation for supported production services.

  • Experience developing playbooks and integrations in Google SecOps SOAR or Palo Alto Cortex XSOAR preferred.

  • Hands-on experience integrating Google SecOps SIEM, CrowdStrike, Tanium, Ping Identity, Delinea, or MISP preferred.

  • Experience designing reusable automation frameworks, custom APIs, or internal security applications preferred.

  • Familiarity with incident response processes, detection engineering, and threat intelligence enrichment workflows preferred.

  • Experience with AI-assisted software development or agentic AI workflows, including appropriate testing, oversight, and security controls preferred.

  • Experience supporting hybrid on-premises and cloud infrastructure in a large enterprise environment preferred.

  • This role requires being onsite in the Rocklin, CA office Monday through Thursday.

Our Culture & Values

We believe that taking care of our people is vital to our success and we strive to offer equitable and transparent practices for all. We prioritize connection, growth, and wellbeing.

People First

Putting People First means investing in overall well-being and opportunities to grow and advance within the organization. Depending on the position and location, here are a few highlights of what benefits may be available:

Benefits

  • A generous discount on all WSI brands

  • A 401(k) plan and other investment opportunities

  • Paid vacations, holidays, and time off to volunteer

  • Health benefits, dental and vision insurance, including same-sex domestic partner benefits

  • Tax-free commuter benefits

  • A wellness program that supports your physical, financial and emotional health

Continued Learning

  • In-person and online learning opportunities through WSI University

  • Cross-brand and cross-function career opportunities

  • Resources for self-development

  • Advisor (Mentor) program

  • Career development workshops, learning programs, and speaker series

WSI will not now or in the future commence an immigration case or "sponsor" an individual for this position (for example, H-1B or other employment-based immigration).

This role is not eligible for relocation assistance.

Williams-Sonoma, Inc. is an Equal Opportunity Employer. Williams-Sonoma, Inc. will consider for employment qualified applicants with criminal histories in a manner consistent with the requirements of the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance, or other applicable state or local laws and ordinances.

The expected starting pay range for this position is $90,000 - $110,000. Applicable pay ranges may differ across markets. Actual pay will be determined based on experience and other job-related factors permitted by law. title: Senior Information Security Engineer - Security Firewall Policy
description:
About the Team

You will be part of the Enterprise Cyber Security organization responsible for protecting WSI systems, applications, and information assets. The Firewall Policy team governs enterprise firewall access and network segmentation, partnering with Security Engineering, Network Infrastructure, application owners, and business teams to enable secure connectivity.

About the Role

As a Senior Information Security Engineer - Security Firewall Policy, you will serve as the hands-on technical lead for a team of approximately 3-5 engineers and analysts. You will coordinate project intake, prioritize firewall policy work, and guide secure, consistent implementation of Palo Alto Networks firewall policies. This is an individual contributor role with technical leadership responsibilities and no formal supervisory duties.

Responsibilities

  • Coordinate the day-to-day technical work of the Firewall Policy team, providing guidance, mentoring, and escalation support without formal people-management responsibilities.

  • Own firewall policy project intake, assess requirements and dependencies, prioritize the backlog, coordinate delivery, and communicate status to stakeholders.

  • Lead review, approval coordination, implementation planning, validation, and lifecycle management of Palo Alto Networks firewall rules and access requests.

  • Drive policy optimization, rule recertification, cleanup of unused or overly permissive access, and continuous improvement of firewall governance.

  • Partner with Network Engineering and application owners to define application flows, troubleshoot connectivity, and implement least-privilege access.

  • Lead firewall policy work supporting network segmentation, PCI compliance, and secure separation of critical environments.

  • Coordinate production changes, risk reviews, maintenance windows, rollback plans, and incident-related firewall requests.

  • Develop repeatable processes, documentation, and automation to improve policy review, request handling, and audit readiness.

  • Collaborate with Security Architecture, Infrastructure, IAM, and project teams to align firewall policies with enterprise security standards.

  • Provide technical knowledge transfer and help develop team capabilities.

Criteria

  • 5+ years of experience in network security, firewall engineering, or related information security roles.

  • Hands-on expertise with Palo Alto Networks firewall policies, rule lifecycle management, and troubleshooting.

  • Strong knowledge of TCP/IP, routing, DNS, NAT, segmentation, and enterprise application connectivity.

  • Experience coordinating technical workstreams, project intake, and cross-functional change activities.

  • Ability to lead technical decisions, resolve competing priorities, and communicate with technical and business partners.

  • Experience with PCI-related network segmentation and evidence collection preferred.

  • Experience automating firewall policy workflows with APIs, Python, PowerShell, or similar tools preferred.

  • Exposure to policy governance platforms, configuration analysis, and AI-assisted operational workflows preferred.

  • This role requires being onsite in the Rocklin, CA office Monday through Thursday.

We believe that taking care of our people is vital to our success and we strive to offer equitable and transparent practices for all. We prioritize connection, growth, and wellbeing.

People First

Putting People First means investing in overall well-being and opportunities to grow and advance within the organization. Depending on the position and location, here are a few highlights of what benefits may be available:

Gordian (www.gordian.com), an international company, is the leader in facility and construction cost data, software and services for all phases of the building lifecycle. A pioneer of Job Order Contracting, Gordian’s solutions also include proprietary RSMeans data and Facility Intelligence and Asset Management Solutions. The Gordian Planning Services team is a group of dynamic, diverse, hardworking individuals focused on delivering valuable data and insights to help our customers ensure their facilities are mission ready. As a trusted advisor in the industry, we provide facilities condition assessments, capital planning and asset management software, and consulting services to our clients in Higher Education, K-12, Healthcare, Government, Corporate and FM Providers. We train and develop our teams to be successful in their roles and prepared for new opportunities as they become available. If this sounds like a team you want to be on, we have an opportunity for you to join us. With our rapid growth, we need additional talent and are seeking motivated professionals to conduct Facility Assessments in the mechanical discipline.

As a facilities assessor, you will get the opportunity to travel with a collective team of assessment professionals to perform condition assessments of mechanical systems in facilities and supporting site infrastructure for asset types that range from zoos to airports, hospitals to schools, historic government buildings to advanced lab facilities.

Responsibilities:
  • Independently review client documentation in preparation and during inspection process (drawings, studies, maintenance logs, etc.).
  • Perform visual inspections of building systems using professional expertise and judgment to verify physical condition of heating, cooling, ventilation, distribution, fire protection, controls, and plumbing. Inspections may include conformance review to client standards and compliance to accessibility, fire and life safety, code, energy and or sustainability evaluations.
  • Interact and collaborate with client facilities management staff to learn key information related to facilities operations, investments, and functional needs.
  • Use computer tablets with built-in cameras and mobile collection software to document system findings while on-site, providing justification for determination of the physical condition.
  • Develop cost estimates for facilities replacement costs and/or corrective measures, using existing data libraries appropriately and at times researching costs with vendors.
  • Document findings within Gordian’s asset management and capital planning software in collaboration with other assessment team members.
  • Responsible for individual quality assurance including completeness and accuracy of findings aligned with project scope in prep for findings reports and presentation.
  • Support client’s inquiries by providing additional clarification and guidance in support of your assessment findings.

Essential Job Functions:

  • Fortive/Gordian requires new employees to be fully vaccinated for COVID-19 as defined by federal and state/provincial laws and mandates, subject to applicable, verified accommodation requests.
  • While on-site, physical ability to walk and inspect large complexes, to climb ladders and stairs to assess the various building systems (including roofing systems).
  • This position requires upwards of 40% to 50% travel – on a national and occasionally an international basis.

Qualifications:

  • Associates or bachelor’s degree in Architectural Engineering, Mechanical Engineering or Facility/Construction management degree or a combination of equivalent experience.
  • Minimum of 5 years of experience in one or more of the following: facility assessment or inspection, facility operations, design, construction, facility/property management experience.
  • Knowledge with researching and applying relevant building codes and standards for existing buildings.
  • Experience conducting quantity surveys and estimating replacement values using RS Means or other construction cost data sets.
  • Have evaluated facility/system conditions and conducted lifecycle analysis to identify deficiencies with corrective cost estimates.

  • An eye for accuracy and attention to detail.
  • *Technical Certifications, Professional registrations, and government clearance a plus.
  • *Multi-discipline knowledge including architectural, structural, mechanical (HVAC and Plumbing), electrical and/or site utilities a plus.

title: Senior Staff Software Engineer_Voice AI Agent Prompting
description:
The Forward Deployed Engineer, Voice AI Agent Engineering designs, builds, ships, and operates voice AI agents whose core behavior is model-driven rather than explicitly authored — conversational and agentic experiences that interpret caller intent over a live audio channel, reason over context, invoke tools, and act on the caller's behalf. The engineer works across the full lifecycle: shaping ambiguous call flows and telephony requirements into precise specifications, authoring the instructions and prompts that govern voice agent behavior, proving through automated evaluation that the result behaves correctly on real calls. This is not a machine learning or AI research role — the engineer does not train foundation or speech models — but it is distinct from traditional software engineering, where systems follow deterministic call-flow logic rather than selecting execution paths at runtime.

Two things follow, and voice makes both harder. First, the agent's most important logic often lives in natural language — instructions, prompts, tool descriptions, and guardrails — which must be engineered, versioned, and reviewed with the same discipline as code, while also holding up under what a spoken channel adds: turn-taking, barge-in, and disambiguating what speech recognition got wrong. Second, because behavior is probabilistic and happens live on a call, correctness is established by measuring behavior at scale — including latency, containment, and transcription accuracy — rather than by asserting fixed outputs, making automated evaluation a first-class engineering activity rather than a quality-assurance afterthought. The engineer owns the correctness of what ships to a live caller, whether a human or an agent produced it.

What You Get to Do in this role:

  • Build voice AI agents. Design and ship agentic voice applications — intent interpretation, multi-step reasoning, tool invocation, and action on the caller's behalf — together with the CTI, CCaaS, and telephony integrations that make them usable in production.

  • Design AI-driven autonomous voice workflows. Decompose call flows and business processes into the steps and decision points a voice agent can execute — determining where autonomy is appropriate, where a live-agent handoff is required, and how misrecognition, retries, and escalation are handled.

  • Engineer for what voice demands. Build experiences that hold context across turns, manage barge-in and interruption, recover gracefully from speech-recognition error, disambiguate caller intent, and confirm before consequential actions — all within the latency budget a live call imposes.

  • Author and maintain voice agent instructions. Write, structure, and version the system instructions, role definitions, tool descriptions, guardrails, and escalation rules that govern voice agent behavior — as engineering artifacts under review and regression coverage, not configuration text.

  • Engineer prompts for reliability rather than demo quality. Iterate prompts against measured call outcomes: task decomposition, golden call transcripts, structured output schemas, grounding and citation, graceful hand-back to a human agent, and the token and latency cost that directly shapes caller experience.

  • Build automated evaluation and test non-deterministic voice behavior. Design and operate the evaluation that makes change safe on a live channel — golden call datasets, multi-turn conversation suites, model-as-judge scoring calibrated to human QA review, CI gates, and drift detection — plus adversarial, jailbreak, grounding, and tool-selection testing specific to voice.

  • Specify precisely and direct AI coding agents. Convert customer call-flow and telephony requirements into testable specifications with explicit scope, constraints, and acceptance criteria; decompose work into agent-sized tasks; and review agent output for correctness and maintainability. You own the result regardless of what produced it.

  • Deliver as a forward deployed engineer, embedded in the voice stack. Work directly inside a customer's telephony, CTI, and CCaaS environment — building against their call data, integrations, and channels, tuning instructions and evaluation sets against live traffic, and returning with evidence that improves the product.

  • Own quality, safety, and reliability on live calls. Monitor call containment, hallucination, unsafe actions, and transcription accuracy; defend against prompt injection and data leakage on live calls; and feed production call failures back into specifications and evaluation sets.

  • Collaborate across product, design, and engineering. Partner with product managers, designers and platform teams to define success criteria, align on tradeoffs, and communicate capability and risk clearly.

To Be Successful in This Role:

A demonstrated track record of building, shipping, and operating production voice applications, including hands-on delivery of AI-native voice agent features that real callers depend on rather than demos. Direct experience authoring agentic instructions and prompts for voice, designing AI-driven autonomous call workflows, and building the evaluation and testing that verifies them against live call traffic, is required. Willingness to work directly with customers in a forward deployed capacity, embedded in their voice and contact center environment, is required. At least 10 years of experience in software engineering with at least 2 years of experience in deploying contemporary AI solutions at customers.

Education:Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, or a related technical field, or equivalent practical experience. Advanced degrees or certifications are a plus but are not a substitute for a demonstrated record of shipping reliable, production voice AI agents.

Key Competencies, Skills, and Experience

  • Software engineering fundamentals. Strong command of data structures, algorithms, system design, APIs, data modeling, and testing.

  • AI native voice application development. Hands-on experience building applications where model-driven behavior is central — agent orchestration at the application layer, tool and function calling, context assembly, grounding against enterprise data, and handling the latency, cost, and failure modes unique to a live audio channel.

  • AI-driven autonomous workflow design. Demonstrated experience designing workflows in which voice agents carry out multi-step call processes with limited supervision: call-flow decomposition, decision points and autonomy boundaries, human-in-the-loop checkpoints, exception and retry handling, and observability over what the agent did and why.

  • Voice and telephony platform expertise. Practical experience with telephony integration, speech recognition and synthesis, and streaming audio — including the barge-in, turn-taking, and confirmation patterns a live call requires.

  • Agentic instruction authoring. Demonstrated skill writing and maintaining the natural-language logic that governs voice agent behavior — instructions, role definitions, tool descriptions, guardrails, and refusal and escalation rules — with versioning, review, and regression coverage applied as they would be to code.

  • Prompt engineering. Intent-driven prompt design tuned for voice: decomposition, golden and few-shot examples, structured output and schema enforcement, grounding and citation, and disciplined iteration against call-level evaluation results rather than impressions.

  • Evaluation and testing of non-deterministic voice systems. Ability to build measurable frameworks assessing call quality, agent behavior, tool-selection accuracy, and regression risk — golden call datasets, scenario suites, model-as-judge scoring with human QA calibration, continuous evaluation pipelines, and drift detection — plus adversarial, jailbreak, and grounding testing.

  • Specification precision and architectural judgment. Ability to define call-flow problems rigorously enough that another engineer or an AI agent implements them correctly, and to decide soundly when to solve a problem in code, in instructions, or by delegating to an agent.

  • Safety, security, and data handling. Working knowledge of risks specific to AI-integrated voice applications — prompt injection, sensitive-data and call-recording leakage, over-broad tool access, unsafe autonomous action — translated into concrete guardrails, least-privilege controls, and monitoring.

  • Forward deployed delivery and stakeholder communication. Comfort working directly with customers inside their telephony environment under incomplete information and fixed timelines, judgment about when a fast local solution is right and when to hold out for the durable one, and credibility communicating capability, limitation, and risk to non-engineers.

Desired Experience

  • Forward deployed or customer-embedded delivery. Prior work as a forward deployed engineer, solution engineer, or in professional services, delivering software inside a customer's environment.

  • Voice and contact center technology. Telephony and contact center platforms, IVR, speech recognition and synthesis, streaming audio, and real-time latency optimization.

  • Conversation design partnership. Experience working alongside conversation or content designers, contributing to dialogue flow, tone, and error-recovery design.

  • Evaluation and observability tooling. Evaluation frameworks, prompt and instruction management tooling, tracing for LLM applications, and analysis of production call transcripts at scale.

  • Enterprise domain depth. Customer service, contact center operations, sales, or enterprise workflow, at a depth sufficient to challenge a requirement rather than only implement it.

  • Years of Experience. At least 10 years of experience in software engineering with at least 2 years of experience in deploying contemporary AI solutions at customers

I denne stilling får du det primære ansvar for den daglige lønhåndtering hos Børsen. Du bliver den centrale drivkraft på området, hvor du tilrettelægger din egen arbejdsdag, træffer de faglige beslutninger og driver opgaverne selvstændigt. Du står dog aldrig alene – du bliver en integreret del af vores HR-team, som altid er tilgængeligt for tæt samarbejde, faglig sparring og gensidig støtte i hverdagen.

Om dig

Med din erfaring inden for lønområdet navigerer du sikkert i lønprocessen på egen hånd. Du arbejder struktureret og grundigt, så deadlines altid overholdes.

Vi forestiller os, at du:

title: Supply Chain Assistant (National Position)
description:
Under the overall supervision of the Procurement and Logistics Officer in Pohnpei, Federated States of Micronesia and direct supervision of the Associate Procurement Officer and in collaboration with relevant units at Headquarters and the Administrative Centres, the supply chain assistant will be responsible and accountable for managing the resources management functions in Sub-Office in Koror, Palau.

  1. Receive and consolidate all procurement requisition forms; verify they have all the required information and comply with the Purchase Authorization Matrix and other office instructions and obtain any necessary additional information.

  2. Prepare tender documents, solicit bids and quotations as applicable; prepare bid analysis summary and share it with the requesting unit.

  3. Once the purchase is approved, confirm terms of agreement with selected suppliers, prepare the relevant documentation (purchase order, contract, etc.) and coordinate the required authorizations.

  4. Monitor status of open requisitions and follow up on the timely delivery of goods and services; upon delivery, coordinate with the receiving unit to obtain satisfactory delivery notes.

  5. Review vendor invoices, prepare payment requests and coordinate with Finance the timely payment to suppliers/service providers.

  6. Maintain physical and electronic records of all documentation through the procurement cycle in accordance with IOM instructions and procedures; retrieve and present information from the system and support preparation of periodic reports.

  7. Conduct market surveys to identify potential new suppliers/service providers; participate in their evaluation regarding quality, prices and services in line with the organization’s best interests.

  8. Keep track of any contractual agreements and inform concerned parties for timely renewal; monitor office supplies and service and prepare requisitions when required and coordinate with Finance Unit the payment of utilities invoices.

  9. Provide technical information to all staff in the office on procurement related instructions and procedures.

  10. Perform supply chain tasks related to property and asset management, warehousing, insurance coverage, maintenance, and transportation.

  11. Support the coordination of transportation needs and drivers’ movements; verify all logbooks are properly maintained and monitor fuel consumption and vehicle’ maintenance records.

  12. Monitor activities of contractors working on the office premises.

  13. Support the organization of meetings, workshops and trainings.

Perform other duties as may be assigned.

EDUCATION

  • University degree in Business Administration, Accounting, Logistics, Supply Chain Management or a related field from an accredited academic institution with two years of relevant professional experience; or

  • High school diploma with four years of relevant professional experience

Certification in Procurement, Logistics or Supply Chain Management is an advantage

EXPERIENCE

  • Experience in procurement and logistics and working with vendors and service providers;

  • Experience with asset management process;

  • Experience working with IOM/UN Procurement and Logistics Rules and Procedures is an advantage;

  • Experience working in an international organisation an advantage.

SKILLS

  • High level of computer literacy;

  • Ability to work with national and international institutions;

  • Ability to prepare clear and concise report;

  • Excellent communication and negotiation skills;

  • Ability to establish realistic resource requirements to meet IOM needs.

Languages[1]
IOM’s official languages are English, French, and Spanish.

REQUIRED

For this position, fluency in English is required (oral and written).

DESIRABLE

Palauan

Competencies[2]

The incumbent is expected to demonstrate the following values and competencies:

VALUES - All IOM staff members must abide by and demonstrate these five values:

Inclusion and respect for diversity: Respects and promotes individual and cultural differences. Encourages diversity and inclusion.

Integrity and transparency: Maintains high ethical standards and acts in a manner consistent with organizational principles/rules and standards of conduct.

Professionalism: Demonstrates ability to work in a composed, competent and committed manner and exercises careful judgment in meeting day-to-day challenges.

Courage: Demonstrates willingness to take a stand on issues of importance.

Empathy: Shows compassion for others, makes people feel safe, respected and fairly treated.

CORE COMPETENCIES - Behavioural indicators – Level 1

Teamwork: Develops and promotes effective collaboration within and across units to achieve shared goals and optimize results.

Delivering results: Produces and delivers quality results in a service-oriented and timely manner. Is action oriented and committed to achieving agreed outcomes.

Managing and sharing knowledge: Continuously seeks to learn, share knowledge and innovate.

Accountability: Takes ownership for achieving the Organization’s priorities and assumes responsibility for own actions and delegated work.

Communication: Encourages and contributes to clear and open communication. Explains complex matters in an informative, inspiring and motivational way.

title: Staff Research Scientist
description:
Description de poste

En tant que chercheur principal, vous travaillerez sur des questions de recherche auxquelles la plupart des laboratoires d’IA n’ont tout simplement pas accès. La recherche en IA de ServiceNow a pour mission de bâtir l’avenir de l’IA agentique en entreprise, avec un point de vue privilégié : nous observons le comportement réel des agents, au sein d’environnements d’entreprise complexes et à grande échelle.

Vous contribuerez à des initiatives de recherche portant sur la manière dont les agents accumulent et réutilisent les connaissances tacites, sur leur capacité d’apprentissage et d’amélioration continue, ainsi que sur leur résilience, leur sécurité et la confidentialité des données qu’ils traitent. Ce sont les véritables obstacles au déploiement de l’IA agentique en entreprise aujourd’hui, et ils apparaissent dans la réalité opérationnelle bien avant d’être documentés dans la littérature scientifique.

Alors que la majeure partie de la communauté IA et TAL se concentre sur les capacités fondamentales des agents, notre équipe explore les dimensions qui déterminent l’adoption réelle : mécanismes de sécurité, détection des menaces, garanties de confidentialité et pratiques d’IA responsable. Vous aurez la liberté de publier et de faire progresser l’état de l’art, avec l’avantage rare de tester vos hypothèses sur de véritables déploiements plutôt que sur des bancs d’essai.

#######

As a Staff Researcher, you will work on research questions that most AI labs simply do not have access to. ServiceNow AI Research is chartered to build the future of enterprise agentic AI, from a rare vantage point: we see how agents actually behave, inside complex enterprise environments, at scale.

You will contribute to research initiatives on how agents accumulate and reuse tacit knowledge, learn and improve continuously, and on their resilience, their safety, and the privacy of the data they handle. These are the real obstacles to enterprise agentic deployment today, and they surface in operational reality well before they appear in the literature.

While much of the AI and NLP community concentrates on core agent capabilities, our team explores the dimensions that determine real adoption: safety mechanisms, threat detection, privacy guarantees, and responsible AI practices. You will have the freedom to publish and advance the state of the art, with the rare advantage of testing your hypotheses against real deployments rather than against benchmarks.

Qualifications

  • Doctorat en informatique, en apprentissage automatique ou dans un domaine connexe, ou expérience de recherche équivalente
  • Au moins deux ans d’expérience de recherche après le doctorat, dont une part importante en milieu industriel ou au contact direct de systèmes déployés
  • Historique de publications dans des conférences de premier plan (NeurIPS, ICML, ICLR, ACL, EMNLP ou équivalents), avec des contributions reconnues comme influentes dans votre domaine
  • Expérience avérée de définition et d’exécution d’un programme de recherche, et pas seulement d’exécution : vous avez choisi des problèmes avant que la communauté ne s’y intéresse, et vous pouvez expliquer pourquoi
  • Expérience de travail au sein d’équipes ou de projets interdisciplinaires, en collaboration avec des chercheurs et des ingénieurs
  • Solides compétences en développement logiciel : vous écrivez, maintenez et optimisez du code de recherche de haute qualité, et vous savez ce qu’il faut pour qu’un résultat survive le passage en production
  • Utilisation avancée des outils agentiques dans votre propre pratique de recherche, et volonté de faire progresser les pratiques de l’équipe dans ce domaine
  • Capacité démontrée d’influencer des décisions techniques au-delà de votre propre équipe, notamment auprès des équipes produit et ingénierie
  • Excellentes aptitudes de communication, incluant la capacité d’expliquer des travaux techniques complexes à des publics non spécialisés et à des dirigeants

Atouts

  • Expertise dans un ou plusieurs des domaines suivants : mémoire des agents et connaissances tacites, apprentissage continu, sécurité et alignement, sécurité informatique et détection des menaces, confidentialité, évaluation des agents
  • Expérience de systèmes d’IA opérant dans de véritables environnements d’entreprise, avec les contraintes de conformité, de gouvernance et d’échelle que cela implique
  • Contributions à des logiciels libres, jeux de données ou bancs d’essai d’évaluation utilisés par la communauté
  • Rôles de service scientifique : comités de programme, travail éditorial, organisation d’ateliers
  • Collaborations académiques ou encadrement de doctorants
  • Maîtrise du français, ou intérêt à l’apprendre, dans un environnement de travail bilingue à Montréal

Requirements

  • PhD in computer science, machine learning, or a related field, or equivalent research experience
  • 2 or more years of research experience post-PhD, a significant portion of it in an industrial setting or in direct contact with deployed systems
  • Established publication record at top-tier venues (NeurIPS, ICML, ICLR, ACL, EMNLP, or equivalents), with contributions recognized as influential in your field
  • Demonstrated track record of setting/executing research agenda, not only executing one: you have chosen problems before the community turned to them, and you can explain why
  • Experience working on cross-disciplinary teams or projects collaborating with researchers and engineers
  • Strong software development skills: you write, maintain, and optimize high-quality research code, and you know what it takes for a result to survive the move into production
  • Advanced use of agentic tools in your own research practice, and a willingness to advance the team's practices in this area
  • Demonstrated ability to influence technical decisions beyond your own team, particularly with product and engineering teams
  • Excellent communication skills, including the ability to explain complex technical work to non-specialist audiences and to executives

Nice to have

  • Expertise in one or more of the following areas: agent memory and tacit knowledge, continual learning, safety and alignment, security and threat detection, privacy, agent evaluation
  • Experience with AI systems operating in real enterprise environments, with the compliance, governance, and scale constraints that entails
  • Contributions to open source software, datasets, or evaluation benchmarks used by the community
  • Scientific service roles: program committees, editorial work, workshop organization
  • Academic collaborations or supervision of doctoral students
  • Fluency in French, or interest in learning it, in a bilingual Montreal work environment

Work Personas

Nous abordons notre monde du travail distribué avec flexibilité et confiance. Les profils de travail (flexible, à distance ou requis au bureau) sont des catégories attribuées aux employés de ServiceNow en fonction de la nature de leur travail et de leur lieu de travail assigné. Pour en savoir plus, cliquez ici. Equal Opportunity Employer

ServiceNow est un employeur qui souscrit au principe de l'égalité d’accès à l’emploi. Tous les candidats qualifiés recevront une considération pour l’emploi sans égard à la race, la couleur, la croyance, la religion, le sexe, l’orientation sexuelle, l’origine nationale ou la nationalité, l’ascendance, l’âge, le handicap, l’identité ou l’expression de genre, l’état matrimonial, le statut d’ancien combattant ou toute autre catégorie protégée par la loi. De plus, tous les candidats qualifiés ayant des antécédents d’arrestation ou de condamnation seront pris en considération pour un emploi conformément aux exigences légales.

Accommodations

Nous mettons tout en œuvre offrir une expérience accessible et inclusive pour tous les candidats. title: Omaha - American Red Cross First Aid/CPR/AED Instructor/ Instructor Trainer
description:
About Us

At ALLCPR, we are committed to elevating community health and safety standards nationwide. We operate at more than 200 locations across the United States, providing American Heart Association Basic Life Support courses, American Red Cross First Aid/CPR/AED and Basic Life Support courses, and related CPR and life-saving training programs.

With an annual training volume of more than 80,000 participants, ALLCPR stands for the belief that all of us should learn CPR. It is our mission to ensure that everyone has the knowledge and skills to save lives.

Our Work Environment Includes

The Instructor will teach American Red Cross First Aid/CPR/AED courses and train students through the American Red Cross.﻿

The Instructor Trainer will be responsible for teaching American Red Cross First Aid/CPR/AED Instructor courses, training instructor candidates to become certified American Red Cross instructors.

The Instructor Trainer will prepare for training sessions, demonstrate proper techniques, and evaluate candidates' performance to ensure they have achieved proficiency.

The Instructor Trainer will work in various settings, including offices, schools, community centers, hospitals, and other locations.

Note: The Instructor Trainer's teaching methods and content must comply with American Red Cross requirements.

License / Certification

  • American Red Cross First Aid/CPR/AED Instructor Certification, r.25 — Required if you are looking for an instructor role
  • American Red Cross First Aid/CPR/AED Instructor Trainer Certification, r.25 — Required﻿ ﻿if you are looking for an instructor trainer role
  • American Red Cross BLS Instructor Trainer Certification — Preferred
  • American Heart Association BLS Instructor Certification — Preferred
  • Other equivalent Instructor Trainer certifications may be considered where an approved bridging pathway is available; we can provide bridging guidance.

Teaching Equipment

The Instructor Trainer must own at least 3 manikin sets.

Key Responsibilities

  • Prepare for American Red Cross First Aid/CPR/AED courses.
  • Deliver instructor-level training sessions to individuals or groups.
  • Demonstrate proper CPR/AED techniques that comply with American Red Cross requirements.
  • Provide feedback to candidates to help them improve their performance.
  • Monitor and evaluate candidate progress to ensure proficiency.
  • Complete and submit course records in accordance with American Red Cross requirements.
  • Ensure training materials are up-to-date and comply with relevant program requirements.
  • Participate in ongoing professional development to stay current with CPR and AED training best practices.
  • Provide excellent customer service to clients and candidates.

Requirements

  • Current American Red Cross First Aid/CPR/AED Instructor certification.
  • Strong knowledge of CPR and AED techniques and best practices.
  • Excellent communication and interpersonal skills.
  • Ability to prepare and deliver effective training sessions.
  • Attention to detail and the ability to provide constructive feedback to candidates.
  • Strong organizational and time-management skills.
  • High school diploma or equivalent.

Physical Demands

  • Must be able to stand for extended periods.
  • Must be able to lift and carry training equipment, up to 50 pounds.

Working Conditions

  • Work may be performed in various settings, including schools, community centers, hospitals, and corporate offices.

Salary and Benefits

Salary: $30.00 - $40.00 per teaching hour, commensurate with experience and length of working relationship with ALLCPR.

Schedule

Ability to Commute / Relocate

Location: Local area as per job post

Experience

  • Teaching: 2+ years (Preferred).

  • Part-time
  • Contract

title: Fiscal & Business Analyst II
description:
The Fiscal Business Analyst II supports the financial operations of the Department of Emergency Medicine within USF Health. The incumbent provides financial analysis, budget projections, account reconciliation, and fiscal resource management, and serves as a key point of contact for faculty and staff on budget-related matters. This position reports to the Associate Director of Fiscal and Business Management.

Budget Management & Financial Analysis 25%

  • Develop and monitor the annual operating budget for the Department of Emergency Medicine, including funds tied to the TeamHealth/USF agreement.

  • Prepare financial projections, variance analyses, and cash-flow forecasts to support planning for a growing faculty complement.

  • Identify spending trends and advise the Associate Director and department leadership on over/under allocations, recommending budget or expenditure transfers as needed.

TeamHealth Agreement & Contract Compliance 20%

  • Monitor expenditures and funding allocations under the executed TeamHealth/USF agreement to ensure compliance with contract terms, University policy, and applicable state/federal regulations.

  • Track faculty and staff positions funded under the agreement, reconciles agreement-related accounts, and supports periodic reporting to TeamHealth and University stakeholders.

Account Reconciliation & Financial Reporting 18%

  • Reconciles multiple account types (E&G, Auxiliary, UMSA/USFF convenience accounts, Carryforward, and related funds) on a monthly basis.

  • Prepare financial statements, cash-balance reports, and management-ready reporting packages.

  • Resolve discrepancies and maintain accurate, audit-ready financial records.

Faculty Growth & Workforce Financial Support 15%

  • Provide fiscal support for the onboarding and ongoing compensation administration of newly recruited faculty, including the 15-faculty hired effective July 1, 2026.

  • Perform payroll and salary-funding analysis, advise on chartfields/combo codes, and coordinate with HR and Payroll to ensure faculty funding is accurately established and maintained.

Purchasing, Travel & Expenditure Oversight 12%

  • Review and process purchasing, travel, and accounts payable/receivable transactions for the department.

  • Recommend and implement procedural and internal-control enhancements to ensure compliance with USF purchasing and travel policy.

Liaison & Advisory Support 5%

  • Serve as the department point of contact for faculty, staff, and central offices (Budget Office, Research Financial Management, Human Resources, USF Health Business Office) on fiscal and budget-related inquiries.

  • Advise faculty and staff on applicable USF policies, procedures, and funding requirements.

Other Duties as Assigned 5%

  • Perform other duties as assigned by the Associate Director of Fiscal and Business Management or department leadership. This allowance is included to provide flexibility for responsibilities that arise during the course of departmental operations and are not fully captured by the categories above.

Minimum Qualifications:

  • This position requires a Bachelor's degree in Accounting, Finance, or Business Administration or other field directly related to the position's specific responsibilities and 2-4 years of fiscal related work experience; or a bachelor's degree in no specific required field and three years of fiscal related work experience; or five years fiscal related work experience.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Demonstrated experience with budget development, account reconciliation, and financial reporting.
  • Experience in a higher education or academic medicine fiscal environment, including grant, contract, or agreement-based funding (e.g., clinical services or academic practice agreements such as the TeamHealth agreement).
  • Experience with USF financial systems (e.g., FAST, GEMS/PeopleSoft, Finance Mart, Power BI, Archivum, Bull Marketplace).
  • Experience supporting a growing department or faculty group, including payroll/salary-funding analysis and onboarding-related fiscal setup.

Is proactive in solving problems and resolving issues with support from district leaders. Leads efforts to leverage satisfied residents and families to grow community occupancy. Becomes active in social and civic affairs of the local community that align with the Company’s mission. Represents the community and the Company to governmental agencies (as appropriate), professional organizations, community groups, and other appropriate agencies and groups.

title: Information Security Engineer
description:
About the Team
You will be part of the Cyber Security organization responsible for protecting the company’s information assets and supporting critical security infrastructure. The Security Operations team ensures the stability, performance, and ongoing support of enterprise security tools and services used across the organization.

Our mission is to reduce risk and protect the confidentiality, integrity, and availability of company systems and data through effective operational support, continuous improvement, and strong cross-functional collaboration.

About the Role
As an Information Security Engineer – Security Operations, you will provide Level 2 operational support for enterprise security tools and platforms. You will play a key role in maintaining, monitoring, and improving the health of security systems while partnering with engineering and IT teams to resolve issues and enhance security posture.

Responsibilities

  • Provide Level 2 support for security tools including Google SecOps, Tanium, CrowdStrike, Ping Identity, and Delinea
  • Monitor, triage, and resolve operational issues, escalating complex problems to engineering (L3) as needed
  • Perform system maintenance activities including patching, upgrades, and configuration updates
  • Support vulnerability scanning processes and track remediation efforts with technology teams
  • Assist in troubleshooting system alerts, integration issues, and performance concerns
  • Partner with DevOps, IT, and Security Engineering teams to ensure secure configurations and best practices
  • Document procedures, configurations, and operational runbooks
  • Identify opportunities for process improvement and contribute to operational efficiency initiatives

Criteria

  • 3 years of experience in information security, IT operations, or related field

  • Bachelor's degree in Computer Science or related field, or equivalent work experience

  • Foundational understanding of security principles and practices
  • Experience supporting security tools such as EDR, IAM, SIEM, or vulnerability management platforms
  • Working knowledge of Windows and Linux systems
  • Basic understanding of networking concepts (DNS, DHCP, TCP/IP, SSL/TLS)
  • Strong troubleshooting and problem-solving skills
  • Ability to work collaboratively in a cross-functional environment
  • Exposure to tools such as Google SecOps, CrowdStrike, Tanium, Ping, or Delinea preferred
  • Experience with scripting (Python, PowerShell, or similar) preferred
  • Familiarity with incident response or security operations workflows preferred

  • This role requires being onsite in the Rocklin, CA or San Francisco, CA office Monday through Thursday


Our Culture & Values

title: Clinical Quality Analyst 2
description:
The Clinical Quality Analyst 2 will play a crucial role in supporting the health system's mission to provide high-quality care through data analysis and reporting. This position involves analyzing clinical and operational data to identify trends, improve patient outcomes, and support strategic decision-making. The Clinical Quality Analyst 2 collaborates with multidisciplinary teams to ensure compliance with regulatory standards and drives initiatives that enhance overall healthcare quality.

Data Analysis: Collect, analyze, and interpret clinical and operational data to identify trends, areas for improvement, and opportunities for enhancing patient outcomes.

Reporting: Develop, maintain, and distribute regular and ad-hoc reports on key quality indicators and performance metrics to stakeholders.

Quality Improvement Initiatives: Collaborate with clinical and administrative teams to design, implement, and evaluate quality improvement projects.

Regulatory Compliance: Ensure adherence to local, state, and federal regulations, as well as accreditation standards, by maintaining accurate and up-to-date documentation and reporting.

Performance Monitoring: Continuously monitor and assess the effectiveness of quality initiatives using data-driven approaches and recommend adjustments as necessary.

Stakeholder Engagement: Work closely with healthcare providers, administrators, and other stakeholders to communicate findings, share best practices, and promote a culture of continuous improvement.

Education and Training: Provide training and support to staff on quality improvement methodologies, data interpretation, and the use of reporting tools.

Education: Bachelor’s degree in Nursing or Allied Health.

Experience: Minimum of 3 years related experience in healthcare setting, preferably in a role related to quality improvement, data analysis, or a related field.

Technical Skills: Proficiency in data analysis software (e.g., SAS, SPSS, SQL) and advanced Excel skills. Experience with electronic health records (EHR) systems is a plus.

Analytical Skills: Strong analytical and problem-solving skills with the ability to interpret complex data and present actionable insights.

Communication Skills: Excellent verbal and written communication skills, with the ability to effectively convey information to diverse audiences.

Attention to Detail: High level of accuracy and attention to detail in data analysis and reporting.

Team Collaboration: Demonstrated ability to work collaboratively in a multidisciplinary team environment.

Knowledge: Familiarity with healthcare quality standards, regulatory requirements, and accreditation processes.
