title: Senior Director, Revenue Cycle Self Pay and Cash Mgmt
description:
This is a hybrid position and must be located within 100 miles of a Mayo Clinic campus for occasional on-site expectations based on business needs.

The Senior Director of Self-Pay and Cash Management provides strategic and operational leadership for key Revenue Cycle functions that support the financial health of the organization and optimize the patient financial experience. This leader is responsible for the oversight of Cash Management operations, including payment posting, remittance processing, reconciliation activities, credit balance management, and regulatory compliance related to patient and payer payments.

In addition, the Senior Director oversees the Self-Pay portfolio, including Patient Account Services, Financial Assistance, self-pay collections, and agency and vendor partnerships. This role is responsible for developing and executing strategies that improve patient engagement, financial access, customer service, and account resolution while ensuring compliance with organizational policies and regulatory requirements. The position provides leadership for back-end customer service operations, ensuring patients receive accurate, timely, and compassionate support throughout their financial journey.

The Senior Director collaborates closely with Revenue Cycle, Finance, Compliance, and Operational leaders to drive performance, implement process improvements, leverage technology solutions, and achieve organizational goals related to cash performance, patient satisfaction, financial assistance programs, bad debt mitigation, and revenue cycle excellence. Through effective leadership and strategic planning, this role fosters a high-performing culture focused on operational efficiency, service excellence, and continuous improvement.

Contributes significantly to the Revenue Cycle initiatives of Mayo Clinic and Mayo Clinic Health System. Develops and participates in short-term tactics and long-range planning that result in optimal Revenue Cycle operations and performance. Takes an active Enterprise and site-based leadership role with physician and executive leadership on proactive revenue cycle strategies and addressing daily Revenue Cycle operations including customer relationship management, process and project management. Functions as a mentor and facilitator of professional development opportunities in order to keep the team optimally refined and aligned with the changing healthcare landscape. Manages institutional and system-wide initiatives and responsibilities associated with the revenue cycle, including personnel. Serves as the primary interface on all revenue cycle related issues including: department oversight, CPR Liaison, technical and governmental issues, billing and collection remediation. Interface with other finance departments including FAS, CPR and Treasury. Responsible for actively advancing strategies and implementation of strategic priorities, standardization/value analysis process, servicing key stakeholders and providing customer service and appropriate staffing support. Responsible for an operating budget associated with area of accountability, its management and adherence to operating expense targets and plans. Understands and contributes to the adherence to the overall Revenue Cycle budget targets and plans. Maintains appropriate compliance for Federal, State, local regulatory agencies and oversight bodies.

Bachelor's degree in business or a related field and a minimum of 10 years of related experience in a hospital or health-care related environment, which includes at least 8 years' experience in major healthcare system or healthcare consulting firm required. Preference will be given to individuals with prior experience as a Director, Revenue Cycle. A Master's degree is strongly preferred. Advanced certification in healthcare is desirable.

Broad expertise in healthcare management, healthcare operations, change management and systems preferred. Experience on non-clinical operational efficiency improvements, care process/procedural standardization improvements, and/or improved patient outcome activities are preferred. Well-disciplined in quality improvement methodology. Demonstrated ability to relate to, gain support of, and drive consensus with clinicians and administrators for the purpose of operational efficiency improvements related to patient experience, financial results and care process improvement. Must have significant facilitation skills and persistence in gaining physician leadership and clinical/technical support for the implementation of organizational strategies. Demonstrated knowledge of revenue cycle accounting processes, cost/benefit analysis and strategic planning. Must be capable of independent work, with little to no guidance provided exercising good judgment, creating an environment in which people communicate with each other respectfully, solving problems, and growing personally and professionally. Must be an advocate of change management, effectively communicating and implementing change and managing it proactively in order to minimize disruption to the Practice, patients and revenue cycle operations. Must be an individual of high integrity, comfortable working in a team environment, possessing vision, solving problems through effective planning and management. Experience in making and implementing decisions in a complex, consensus-oriented environment required. Must have excellent negotiation skills with external and internal constituencies and a thorough knowledge of industry best practices to continually enhance and improve revenue cycle processes. Promotes teamwork and seeks to maximize the potential of all employees. Demonstrated oral and written communication, interpersonal and customer service skills are essential. Able to effectively communicate Revenue Cycle strategies and initiatives to internal management groups and business partners, including MC executive leadership and industry and Fortune 100 company leaders. Must be proficient with software programs (Excel, Word, etc.). Healthcare Financial Management Association (HFMA) Certification Preferred.

Authorization to work and remain in the United States, without necessity for Mayo Clinic sponsorships now, or in the future (for example, be a U.S. Citizen, national, or permanent resident, refugee, or asylee). Mayo Clinic does not participate in the F-1 STEM OPT extension program.

During the selection process you may participate in an OnDemand (pre-recorded) interview that you can complete at your convenience. During the OnDemand interview, a question will appear on your screen, and you will have time to consider each question before responding. You will have the opportunity to re-record your answer to each question - Mayo Clinic will only see the final recording. The complete interview will be reviewed by a Mayo Clinic staff member and you will be notified of next steps.

title: Licensed Therapist (Alaska Licensure)
description:
Help Shape the Future of Behavioral Addiction Treatment

As online gambling and gaming continue to expand, so does the need for specialized behavioral health care. At Kindbridge Behavioral Health, a Joint Commission-accredited telehealth organization, we help individuals and families affected by gambling, gaming, and related challenges while providing therapists the opportunity to build expertise in this growing field.

We're seeking part-time Therapists licensed to practice in Alaska (residency in AK not required) who are interested in expanding their clinical skill set, working with a unique client population, and making a meaningful impact through flexible, remote work.

Why Choose Kindbridge:

Develop a Specialized Clinical Skill Set — Gain hands-on experience treating gambling, gaming, and other behavioral addictions while building expertise in one of behavioral health's fastest-growing specialties

Receive Clinical Training & Mentorship — We provide ongoing education, clinical consultation, and support pursuing the International Certified Gambling Counselor (ICGC-I) credential through mentorship from a nationally recognized, Ph.D.-trained, ICGC-II-certified gambling addiction clinician

Join an Accredited Behavioral Health Organization — Work with a Joint Commission-accredited organization committed to the highest standards of quality, safety and patient care

Focus on Clinical Work — We handle credentialing, billing, insurance claims, collections, and other administrative tasks so you can focus on providing care

Build a Flexible Remote Practice — Set your own schedule and maintain a caseload that aligns with your availability and professional goals

Work Alongside Experts in the Field — Join a collaborative team of clinicians who are passionate about advancing care for individuals and families seeking support for compulsive or overuse behaviors, or emotional dysregulation struggles through compassionate, evidence-based treatment

What We Provide:

  • ICGC-I certification support
  • Ongoing training and professional development
  • Clinical consultation and peer support
  • Insurance credentialing support
  • Assistance with and funding for additional state licensure
  • Administrative and billing support
  • Flexible scheduling and remote work
  • W-2 employment
  • 401(k) with employer match

Who We're Looking For:

  • Active clinical licensure in the state of Alaska: LPC, LPCC, LCSW, LMFT, or equivalent license
  • Interest in gambling disorder, gaming disorder, and other behavioral challenges
  • Desire to pursue ICGC-I certification with company support
  • Commitment to evidence-based, client-centered care
  • Interest in collaborating with a team that’s driving innovation in teletherapy
  • Spanish fluency is a plus

Join Our Mission:

At Kindbridge, you'll have the opportunity to expand your expertise into a highly specialized area of behavioral health while helping individuals and families affected by gambling, gaming, and related behavioral challenges.

If you're looking for meaningful clinical work, ongoing mentorship, and the opportunity to become a leader in an emerging field, we'd love to hear from you.

title: Client Partner
description:
ustwo is looking for an exceptional, high-impact Principal-level Client Partner to grow a portfolio of client relationships, each valued multiple millions. You'll own the commercial growth, strategic direction and overall health of your accounts, serving as a trusted advisor to senior client stakeholders.

The core mandate is horizontal growth. You'll take our product design, technology and strategy services into new business units, divisions and geographies within existing clients.

This is a hands-on growth role. Alongside leading established relationships, you'll network into assigned target accounts and run outbound activity into cold accounts, turning first conversations into long-term partnerships. You'll work closely with the Exec Director of Client Services & Growth, Growth, Marketing and our global Client Partner community.

Responsibilities

Account Leadership & Horizontal Growth
  • Horizontal account growth: Proactively identify, shape and close new workstreams by extending ustwo's services across divisions, business units, regions and brands within existing clients.
  • Portfolio & P&L ownership: Be accountable for revenue, profitability and forecasting across accounts valued at multiple millions with a clear plan to grow each one.
  • Account planning: Build and maintain account plans that map the client organisation, its decision-makers and budget holders, and the whitespace where ustwo can add value.
  • Executive relationships: Act as the primary strategic partner for VP to Director-level stakeholders, and build new relationships with adjacent leaders beyond your day-to-day contacts.
  • Strategic leadership & value delivery: Partner with leads across Strategy, Technology, Product, Delivery and Design to deliver high-quality work with commercial rigour.
  • Global Collaboration: Collaborate with ustwo’s global leadership and Client Partner community to leverage global studio talent, share best practices, and drive continuous improvement.

New Business & Outbound Growth
  • Networking into target accounts: Use your network, referrals, events and warm introductions to open new doors within assigned target accounts across our five verticals.
  • Outbound into cold accounts: Run consistent, targeted outbound activity (research, personalised outreach, follow-up sequences) to engage cold accounts where ustwo has no existing relationship.
  • Pipeline building: Build and manage a pipeline of new opportunities aligned with ustwo's commercial priorities and your assigned verticals.
  • Early-stage conversations: Lead first meetings and discovery with senior decision-makers, qualify opportunities, and bring in studio leadership and specialists at the right moment.
  • Account-based marketing: Partner with Marketing on campaigns, events, thought leadership and account-based initiatives that warm up target accounts.
  • Market insight: Develop a point of view on your verticals' challenges and industry trends, and use it to shape outreach and proposals.
  • Tools & reporting: Keep CRM data, pipeline forecasting and commercial reporting accurate, and use AI-enabled tools to sharpen research and prospecting.

Requirements

  • 10+ years in client services, account leadership or business development within a digital agency, consultancy or design and technology environment.
  • A track record of managing and growing client accounts valued at multiple millions annually, including growing accounts from the lower end of that range to the upper end.
  • Demonstrated success expanding services horizontally into new business units, divisions or geographies, within existing clients and in newly won organisations.
  • Proven experience networking into target accounts and turning introductions into qualified opportunities with senior decision-makers.
  • Hands-on experience running outbound activity into cold accounts, and comfort owning that activity yourself rather than handing it off.
  • Strong commercial judgement across revenue forecasting, margin, risk, pipeline management and opportunity qualification, using CRM tools such as Pipedrive or Salesforce.
  • Solid understanding of digital product development, human-centred design and technology transformation.
  • A skilled communicator, facilitator and negotiator who builds trust quickly and collaborates well with multidisciplinary teams.
  • Inspiring, inclusive team lead who thrives on collaborating with multidisciplinary digital specialists to deliver tangible business outcomes.
  • Able to rapidly understand client contexts, build relationships quickly, and deliver impact with minimal onboarding.
  • Curious, proactive and self-directed, with a hands-on approach to execution.

Benefits

Why ustwo?
We’re a design and technology studio that believes thoughtful design creates better outcomes for people and businesses. You’ll join a collaborative team that values curiosity, generosity and craft, with the opportunity to shape one of the industry’s most respected design brands.

Details and benefits
Our full benefits package is available to all permanent and fixed term contract employment, please see further details here. We will also be able to share a benefits deck to showcase local benefits.

Location
This is a hybrid role based out of our Malmö studio or remote from a major Northern European city with regular travel to the Malmö studio. Given our global studio model, regular international travel across Europe may be required to build deep relationships, oversee key strategic initiatives and collaborate with colleagues in person when required.

We encourage applications from people with different backgrounds and experiences. If this role excites you, we’d love to hear from you, even if you don’t meet every requirement.

title: Commercial Operations Lead Leasing Documentation Coordinator
description:
Citizens Asset Finance (CAF) is headquartered in Johnston, RI and provides secured finance transactions for commercial clients. Products include loans, capital leases, synthetic leases, leveraged leases, direct finance leases and operating leases. CAF operates on a national business platform providing coverage to the equipment financing industry throughout North America.

The Lead Documentation Coordinator is a critical member of the CAF documentation team, who is responsible for determining the appropriate financing documents; ensuring documents have been properly prepared, authorized and executed; confirming that all conditions precedent to closing have been met; and completing due diligence to perfect CAF’s security interest in the collateral. This role also ensures that all terms and conditions prescribed by the credit approval have been satisfied and transactions are consistent with product guidelines and regulatory requirements. Because the Lead Documentation Coordinator brings experience and a thorough understanding of financing documentation to the role, this individual is expected to handle basic document negotiations and will maintain their own portfolio of complex transactions and portfolio of CAF customers as well as reviewing documentation packages of other team members.

In connection with these responsibilities, the Senior Documentation Coordinator will have the following additional duties:

  • Review documentation packages prepared by Documentation Coordinators and outside legal counsel including documentation and collateral (invoice/asset) review, outgoing wire validation and approval and pre-bookings entered into system.

  • Independently prepare and validate all legal documentation on complex loan and lease transactions to ensure documents accurately reflect the approved structure and comply with company policies and procedures.

  • Provide initial drafts of document revisions based on negotiations or specific requirements outlined in the credit approval.

  • Demonstrate knowledge of various types of equipment being financed to ensure appropriate documents are utilized and lien perfection in collateral occurs properly.

  • Analyze and understand transactions, including pricing, deal structure, collateral evaluation, credit, and tax components (including sales/use taxes and property taxes).

  • Manage the closing process with all parties, including customers, vendors, and internal and external counsel; authorize closings and instruct operations to disburse funds.

  • Independently book transactions using the CAF front-end system (Rapport) and ensure all transactions are booked accurately and in a timely manner.

  • Perform appropriate due diligence to ensure all conditions precedent are met prior to closing / funding a transaction
  • Research and resolve complex operational issues
  • Must be well versed in UCC requirements to review UCC searches, UCC1, UCC3
  • Be able to review documents that CAF purchases and facilitate funding and pre-booking in system of record
  • Support the Documentation Manager in establishing and maintaining appropriate procedures, training materials, control environment, metrics and reporting
  • Act as an informal resource for colleagues on the team

Qualifications

  • Requires 5+ years of related experience in financial services

  • Prefer advance knowledge of post-approval to loan closing process for equipment finance transactions. Prefer strong knowledge of lease accounting system

  • Prefer knowledge of specialty collateral including aircraft, marine, and rail transactions

  • Strong understanding of lease and loan documentation requirements

  • Self-motivated with an ability to adapt and adjust to changing conditions and priorities

  • Have a collaborative style, be flexible, and have an ability to partner with other team members across global time zones

  • An evidenced and accomplished history of independent problem solving

  • Established track record of delivery results in a complex environment

  • Ability to effectively manage multiple priorities through planning and time management

  • Demonstrated motivation to assist with team goals

  • Bachelor’s Degree required, Paralegal preferred

  • This position is available in Johnston, RI; Chicago, IL; Columbus, OH; Charlotte, NC. Qualified candidates may be considered for remote status.

  • Work Schedule:

    • 40 hours per week

    • Monday – Friday, 8:00am – 5:00pm

Pay Transparency

The salary range for this position is $98,000 - $142,000 per year, plus an opportunity to earn an annual discretionary bonus. Actual pay is based on various factors including but not limited to the budget, work location, and relevant skills and experience.

We offer competitive pay, comprehensive medical, dental and vision coverage, retirement benefits, maternity/paternity leave, flexible work arrangements, education reimbursement, wellness programs and more. Note, Citizens’ paid time off policy exceeds the mandatory, paid sick or paid time-away policy of every local and state jurisdiction in the United States. For an overview of our benefits, visit .

title: Housing Navigator (7176)
description:
Mission Statement: "To be a leader in ending homelessness by providing a unique system of dignified housing opportunities, programs, and supportive services."

Job Summary: The Housing Navigator is responsible for supporting individuals in the shelter system through ongoing needs assessments, housing plans, referrals, and advocacy for individuals at our Mercy House shelters to help them achieve housing stability. The role requires creating individualized service plans, coordinating with external agencies, and using trauma-informed care and harm reduction strategies. This position involves managing a caseload, keeping clear and accurate files, and providing crisis intervention and housing support services.

Essential Duties and Responsibilities:
Client/Service Delivery

  • Maintain a caseload of 22-30 individuals
  • Meet with the participants as needed or instructed by your supervisor
  • Conduct Navigation assessment for client within seven days of entering shelter
  • Determine eligibility and enter assessment into Central Entry System (CES) for prioritization and linkage to housing provider
  • Assist client obtaining required documents to secure housing (e.g., valid identification card, birth certificate, income verification, assistance with Social Security Benefits, etc.)
  • Provide information referrals, crisis intervention, and assistance with permanent housing placement for participants
  • Conduct comprehensive screenings and assessments to collect functional, environmental, financial, employment, housing, educational, and health information, as appropriate, to develop an Individual Service Plan with short-term and long-term goals
  • Participate in all stages of client service: assessment, service planning, engagement, and delivery
  • Provide employment linkage, benefits establishment, linkage to community providers for substance abuse, primary and mental health care, and all other services needed to assist clients in reaching their individual housing goals
  • Utilize harm reduction interventions and methodologies to provide client-centered services

title: Senior Staff Software Engineer-Voice AI Agent Prompting
description:
The Forward Deployed Engineer, Voice AI Agent Engineering designs, builds, ships, and operates voice AI agents whose core behavior is model-driven rather than explicitly authored — conversational and agentic experiences that interpret caller intent over a live audio channel, reason over context, invoke tools, and act on the caller's behalf. The engineer works across the full lifecycle: shaping ambiguous call flows and telephony requirements into precise specifications, authoring the instructions and prompts that govern voice agent behavior, proving through automated evaluation that the result behaves correctly on real calls. This is not a machine learning or AI research role — the engineer does not train foundation or speech models — but it is distinct from traditional software engineering, where systems follow deterministic call-flow logic rather than selecting execution paths at runtime.

Two things follow, and voice makes both harder. First, the agent's most important logic often lives in natural language — instructions, prompts, tool descriptions, and guardrails — which must be engineered, versioned, and reviewed with the same discipline as code, while also holding up under what a spoken channel adds: turn-taking, barge-in, and disambiguating what speech recognition got wrong. Second, because behavior is probabilistic and happens live on a call, correctness is established by measuring behavior at scale — including latency, containment, and transcription accuracy — rather than by asserting fixed outputs, making automated evaluation a first-class engineering activity rather than a quality-assurance afterthought. The engineer owns the correctness of what ships to a live caller, whether a human or an agent produced it.

What You Get to Do in This Role:

  • Build voice AI agents. Design and ship agentic voice applications — intent interpretation, multi-step reasoning, tool invocation, and action on the caller's behalf — together with the CTI, CCaaS, and telephony integrations that make them usable in production.

  • Design AI-driven autonomous voice workflows. Decompose call flows and business processes into the steps and decision points a voice agent can execute — determining where autonomy is appropriate, where a live-agent handoff is required, and how misrecognition, retries, and escalation are handled.

  • Engineer for what voice demands. Build experiences that hold context across turns, manage barge-in and interruption, recover gracefully from speech-recognition error, disambiguate caller intent, and confirm before consequential actions — all within the latency budget a live call imposes.

  • Author and maintain voice agent instructions. Write, structure, and version the system instructions, role definitions, tool descriptions, guardrails, and escalation rules that govern voice agent behavior — as engineering artifacts under review and regression coverage, not configuration text.

  • Engineer prompts for reliability rather than demo quality. Iterate prompts against measured call outcomes: task decomposition, golden call transcripts, structured output schemas, grounding and citation, graceful hand-back to a human agent, and the token and latency cost that directly shapes caller experience.

  • Build automated evaluation and test non-deterministic voice behavior. Design and operate the evaluation that makes change safe on a live channel — golden call datasets, multi-turn conversation suites, model-as-judge scoring calibrated to human QA review, CI gates, and drift detection — plus adversarial, jailbreak, grounding, and tool-selection testing specific to voice.

  • Specify precisely and direct AI coding agents. Convert customer call-flow and telephony requirements into testable specifications with explicit scope, constraints, and acceptance criteria; decompose work into agent-sized tasks; and review agent output for correctness and maintainability. You own the result regardless of what produced it.

  • Deliver as a forward deployed engineer, embedded in the voice stack. Work directly inside a customer's telephony, CTI, and CCaaS environment — building against their call data, integrations, and channels, tuning instructions and evaluation sets against live traffic, and returning with evidence that improves the product.

  • Own quality, safety, and reliability on live calls. Monitor call containment, hallucination, unsafe actions, and transcription accuracy; defend against prompt injection and data leakage on live calls; and feed production call failures back into specifications and evaluation sets.

  • Collaborate across product, design, and engineering. Partner with product managers, designers and platform teams to define success criteria, align on tradeoffs, and communicate capability and risk clearly

To Be Successful in This Role:

A demonstrated track record of building, shipping, and operating production voice applications, including hands-on delivery of AI-native voice agent features that real callers depend on rather than demos. Direct experience authoring agentic instructions and prompts for voice, designing AI-driven autonomous call workflows, and building the evaluation and testing that verifies them against live call traffic, is required. Willingness to work directly with customers in a forward deployed capacity, embedded in their voice and contact center environment, is required. At least 10 years of experience in software engineering with at least 2 years of experience in deploying contemporary AI solutions at customers.

Education:Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, or a related technical field, or equivalent practical experience. Advanced degrees or certifications are a plus but are not a substitute for a demonstrated record of shipping reliable, production voice AI agents.

Key Competencies, Skills, and Experience

  • Software engineering fundamentals. Strong command of data structures, algorithms, system design, APIs, data modeling, and testing.

  • AI native voice application development. Hands-on experience building applications where model-driven behavior is central — agent orchestration at the application layer, tool and function calling, context assembly, grounding against enterprise data, and handling the latency, cost, and failure modes unique to a live audio channel.

  • AI-driven autonomous workflow design. Demonstrated experience designing workflows in which voice agents carry out multi-step call processes with limited supervision: call-flow decomposition, decision points and autonomy boundaries, human-in-the-loop checkpoints, exception and retry handling, and observability over what the agent did and why.

  • Voice and telephony platform expertise. Practical experience with telephony integration, speech recognition and synthesis, and streaming audio — including the barge-in, turn-taking, and confirmation patterns a live call requires.

  • Agentic instruction authoring. Demonstrated skill writing and maintaining the natural-language logic that governs voice agent behavior — instructions, role definitions, tool descriptions, guardrails, and refusal and escalation rules — with versioning, review, and regression coverage applied as they would be to code.

  • Prompt engineering. Intent-driven prompt design tuned for voice: decomposition, golden and few-shot examples, structured output and schema enforcement, grounding and citation, and disciplined iteration against call-level evaluation results rather than impressions.

  • Evaluation and testing of non-deterministic voice systems. Ability to build measurable frameworks assessing call quality, agent behavior, tool-selection accuracy, and regression risk — golden call datasets, scenario suites, model-as-judge scoring with human QA calibration, continuous evaluation pipelines, and drift detection — plus adversarial, jailbreak, and grounding testing.

  • Specification precision and architectural judgment. Ability to define call-flow problems rigorously enough that another engineer or an AI agent implements them correctly, and to decide soundly when to solve a problem in code, in instructions, or by delegating to an agent.

  • Safety, security, and data handling. Working knowledge of risks specific to AI-integrated voice applications — prompt injection, sensitive-data and call-recording leakage, over-broad tool access, unsafe autonomous action — translated into concrete guardrails, least-privilege controls, and monitoring.

  • Forward deployed delivery and stakeholder communication. Comfort working directly with customers inside their telephony environment under incomplete information and fixed timelines, judgment about when a fast local solution is right and when to hold out for the durable one, and credibility communicating capability, limitation, and risk to non-engineers.

Desired Experience:

  • Forward deployed or customer-embedded delivery. Prior work as a forward deployed engineer, solution engineer, or in professional services, delivering software inside a customer's environment.

  • Voice and contact center technology. Telephony and contact center platforms, IVR, speech recognition and synthesis, streaming audio, and real-time latency optimization.

  • Conversation design partnership. Experience working alongside conversation or content designers, contributing to dialogue flow, tone, and error-recovery design.

  • Evaluation and observability tooling. Evaluation frameworks, prompt and instruction management tooling, tracing for LLM applications, and analysis of production call transcripts at scale.

  • Enterprise domain depth. Customer service, contact center operations, sales, or enterprise workflow, at a depth sufficient to challenge a requirement rather than only implement it.

  • Years of Experience. At least 10 years of experience in software engineering with at least 2 years of experience in deploying contemporary AI solutions at customers

title: Manufacturing Engineering Technician
description:
Position Summary
The Manufacturing Engineering Technician provides hands-on production support to Manufacturing Engineers and production associates. This role helps keep manufacturing operations running by ensuring tooling readiness, maintaining clear manufacturing instructions, training operators, collecting process data, and supporting continuous improvement. The technician performs work under the direction of Manufacturing Engineering and communicates production issues and improvement recommendations to engineers.
The initial primary assignment is Building 24 at the Chandler site. The technician must also support Manufacturing Engineers and production teams in other Chandler buildings as business needs require. This individual contributor reports to Phil Kelman and receives daily functional direction from the Manufacturing Engineer supporting the assigned production area.


Responsibilities
• Verify that production tooling is available, correct for the operation, in usable condition, and within its approved calibration status. Identify tooling shortages, damage, or upcoming calibration needs and coordinate timely resolution.
• Coordinate tooling inventory, purchase and fabrication requests, repairs, replacements, and calibration activities with the appropriate teams. Ensure tools are ready for production in accordance with approved requirements.
• Assist Manufacturing Engineers with tooling and fixture design and implementation. Handle routine tooling support within established procedures; escalate new designs and engineering decisions for Manufacturing Engineer review and approval.
• Work with production associates to identify and correct issues in manufacturing procedures and visual work instructions. Modify and update documentation through the established document-change process.
• Review approved manufacturing instructions with operators, demonstrate process steps and proper equipment/tool use, and help train new or developing associates. Reinforce process adherence and promptly address or escalate incorrect practices and production concerns.
• Support and help lead smaller process-improvement activities under Manufacturing Engineering direction. Gather shop-floor ideas and assist with Lean, Kaizen, standard work, and other continuous-improvement initiatives.
• Collect, report, and perform initial analysis of production and process data. Summarize findings and communicate recommendations to Manufacturing Engineers to support equipment evaluation, process performance, and defect reduction.
• Generate engineering work orders and support production-readiness reviews, project kickoff actions, engineering studies/experiments, and engineering or pre-production builds.
• Assist Manufacturing Engineers with process failure mode and effects analysis, process hazard analysis, and statistical process control activities as trained.
• Support welding-related tooling, operator training, and weld sectioning/evaluation activities as qualified and directed, helping identify and reduce production defects.
• Collaborate with production supervisors/leads, operators, Manufacturing Engineers, and integrated product teams. Provide support across Chandler buildings and perform other related duties as assigned.


Required Qualifications
• High school diploma or equivalent.
• At least two years of related manufacturing, production, or technical experience.
• Hands-on knowledge of production equipment, tooling, manufacturing procedures, and work instructions, with the ability to recognize process problems and resolve or appropriately escalate them.
• For the initial Building 24 assignment, demonstrated capability to perform the area’s manufacturing processes and explain proper process and equipment use to others.
• Computer competency with Microsoft Office applications.
• Ability to communicate respectfully, train and work effectively with production associates, follow engineering direction, and contribute to shared production and quality goals.
• Ability to work fully on site in Chandler, support multiple production buildings, and provide overtime or weekend coverage as needed.


Preferred Qualifications
• Five or more years of relevant experience, including established knowledge of PacSci EMC manufacturing processes and experience across multiple production buildings.
• Laser or TIG welding, soldering, and weld sectioning/evaluation experience.
• Experience with powder measurement and pressing, pre-weld cleaning, assembly, inspection, and electrical testing in energetic-device manufacturing.
• Experience with tooling readiness, engineering/document changes, engineering work orders, prototype or pre-production builds, and production-readiness activities.
• Aegis electronic manufacturing instructions experience and exposure to Lean, continuous improvement, Kaizen, or the Ralliant Business System.
• Experience with process-data analysis, PFMEA, process hazard analysis, or SPC. Further training may be provided in data analysis, PFMEA, SPC, and Aegis.


Work Environment and Schedule
This is a hands-on, hourly position supporting shop-floor manufacturing in Chandler. Daytime coverage is anticipated, with flexibility for earlier starts, later finishes, and Friday, Saturday, or other weekend overtime as needed. The standard weekly schedule will be confirmed during the selection process. Routine travel is not anticipated, although occasional travel may be required.


Development Opportunities
The role offers opportunities to broaden technical capability, contribute to tooling and process improvements, and develop operator-training skills. Progression depends on demonstrated capability and applicable role requirements. Engineering education may support a future Manufacturing Engineer career path. No promotion or advancement timeframe is guaranteed.


Employment Eligibility
Due to U.S. Government contract requirements applicable to this position, only U.S. citizens are eligible for employment in this role.

title: Court Operations Associate, Hennepin County, Family Court
description:

Below are the past experiences that will lead to success in the role. For education requirements listed, the equivalent number of years of related experience may serve as a substitute.

  • High school diploma or equivalent

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Associate, paralegal, or bachelor’s degree
  • Experience with high-volume data entry
  • Experience providing exceptional customer service in a high-volume, fast-paced environment
  • Experience working in a courtroom setting, preparing court orders, and generating court forms
  • Experience scheduling multiple appointments/hearings
  • Knowledge and working experience with a case processing system such as MNCIS (Minnesota Court Information System) and EFS (Electronic File and Serve

Supplemental Information:

The expected starting salary for external candidates is $23.50 - $28.45 per hour, $49,068 - $57,403.60 annually. The offer will take into consideration other equivalent qualifications. The full classification earning potential is $21.45 - $35.44 per hour, $44,787.60 - $73,998.72 annually, with the top end of the range being what someone could be making after years of service in the role of Court Operations Associate.

title: Co-Responder Therapist-Licensed (S0318)
description:
Co-Responder Therapist – Licensed- Full Time – La Plata County, CO

Position Summary:

The role of the Co-Responder Therapist is to work in collaboration with a law enforcement officer or emergency medical technician to respond to community members whose need for urgent intervention was reported through the Emergency Communication Center (911). The team(s) specialize in de-escalation, problem-solving, risk assessment, and community resource linkage. Co-responder teams have demonstrated improved interactions between law enforcement, first responders, and the people they serve. Communities have also recognized savings by connecting people to appropriate services and resources, rather than using more costly, higher-level interventions.

It is the role of the Co-Responder Therapist to act as a first responder to issues related to behavioral health crises which may include mental illness, substance use, and social determinants of health. The Co-Responder Therapist will utilize a working knowledge of crisis intervention approaches to provide intervention, support, risk evaluation and triage services for all populations utilizing the 911 system within the jurisdictional limits of the partner agency and program specifications. They will actively participate in patient continuity of care, brief counseling, referral, and prompt documentation. This includes an intense focus on community resourcing and linkage, requiring strong interpersonal skills and collaboration.

Qualifications: Candidate should hold a Bachelor's degree in one of the recognized mental health professions, and have a minimum of (2) two years’ experience in mental health field. They will also have experience in an emergency service setting or demonstrated competency. Preferred experience: Master's degree in one of the recognized mental health professions and be Colorado License Eligible/Licensed LPC, LMFT, LCSW or PsyD in the State of Colorado. Crisis intervention experience preferred.

Driver’s License:Must have current driver’s license and ability to be commercially insured and maintain a driving record that allows insurability with Axis Health System commercial insurance agency.

They must also be able to complete and apply training with law enforcement agency including basic tactical intervention, scene safety, basic firearm safety, defensive driving, use of CAD and radio systems.

title: Marathi Data Labeling Associate
location: New York, New York, United States
description:
Overview

Welo Data is looking for sharp, curious, and detail-oriented individuals to join our team as Data Labeling Associate.

This is not a traditional annotation role.

You'll be working directly with cutting-edge AI systems — evaluating outputs, identifying gaps, and helping improve how these systems behave in real-world scenarios. The work sits at the intersection of data quality, model evaluation, and human judgment, where your ability to think critically matters just as much as following guidelines.

We're looking for people who are naturally curious about AI, comfortable forming opinions, and confident in contributing to conversations with teammates, leads, and stakeholders.

Project Details

  • Job Title: Project Perseus | Data Labeling Associate – Marathi Speakers (Human-in-the-Loop AI)
  • Hiring in: NYC, Seattle, Bellevue, Redmond, San Francisco, Sunnyvale, Burlingame, Los Angeles, Washington DC, Boston

  • Employment Type: W2 Full-Time Employee
  • Work Authorization: Must be authorized to work in the U.S. (no visa sponsorship)

Important: This is a 100% onsite position — remote work is not available for this role. To be considered, candidates must be located in or able to commute to one of the following cities: New York City, Seattle, Bellevue, Redmond, San Francisco, Sunnyvale, Burlingame, Los Angeles, Washington DC, Boston. Please only apply if you meet this location requirement.

What You'll Do

  • Evaluate AI model outputs and provide structured, high-quality feedback
  • Perform audit-based reviews of data and model behavior — identifying patterns, edge cases, and failure modes
  • Apply guidelines thoughtfully — and flag when they don't reflect real-world scenarios

  • Participate in team discussions, calibrations, and stakeholder syncs
  • Partner with leads and cross-functional teams to refine quality standards
  • Document findings in a clear, concise, and actionable way

  • Native-level proficiency in Marathi and a university degree (Bachelor's or higher).

  • Ability to apply complex writing rules and guidelines consistently

  • Strong critical thinking and attention to detail
  • Ability to make sound judgment calls in ambiguous situations
  • Naturally curious about AI, technology, and how systems behave
  • Comfortable speaking up, asking questions, and contributing ideas
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills
  • Ability to stay consistent while working with evolving guidelines
  • Experience in data quality, QA, annotation, or analysis is helpful — but not required

title: CED Faculty Scholar
description:
We have an opening in the Computational Engineering Division within the Engineering (ENG) Principal Associate Directorate (PAD) for a faculty member to engage in a 6-month collaborative research assignment of mutual interest to further their research goals. Opportunities include providing research in optimization methods for simulation of electricity markets in the medium and long term. The Faculty Scholar will be selected based upon their outstanding scholarship and research expertise and overlap with the Lab's mission. Please include a cover letter and your CV.

Essential Duties

  • Provide expertise in one or more of the following areas: short-term power system scheduling (e.g., unit commitment and optimal power flow), risk quantification and modeling in power systems, pricing mechanisms in electricity markets, ancillary services modeling, and capacity expansion planning.
  • Collaborate with technical area leaders, project leaders, and program management in a multidisciplinary team environment to achieve research objectives.
  • Perform theoretical and simulation studies of wholesale pricing impacts and mechanisms to capture impact of beyond-horizon constraints (e.g., large thermal commitment, storage and hydro management) in short-term electricity markets.
  • Author complex scientific reports and deliver presentations to both internal and external scientific audiences.
  • Participate in laboratory activities to both provide and gain exposure to ongoing research.
  • Perform other duties as assigned.
  • Must be available to start March 2027 - August 2027.
  • Must be a faculty or scientist affiliated at an accredited institution with a Ph.D. in Electrical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Industrial Engineering, Operations Research, Applied Mathematics, or equivalent level of demonstrated knowledge.
  • Significant experience modeling risk and risk averse behavior in electricity markets and power systems.
  • Analytical skills necessary to solve complex research problems and make decisions independently.
  • Advanced communication skills to author technical and scientific reports, publications, and invited papers and to deliver scientific presentations.
  • Experience working effectively independently, as well as in a team, with minimal supervision in a goal-oriented environment.

All your information will be kept confidential according to EEO guidelines.

Position Information

This is a Temporary Faculty Scholar appointment.

Why Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory?

  • Included in 2026 Best Places to Work by Glassdoor!
  • Holiday Pay
  • Sick leave accrual
  • Individual 401(k) contributions

National Defense Authorization Act (NDAA)

The 2025 National Defense Authorization Act (NDAA), Section 3112, generally prohibits citizens of China, Russia, Iran and North Korea without dual US citizenship or legal permanent residence from accessing specific non-public areas of national security or nuclear weapons facilities. The restrictions of NDAA Section 3112 apply to this position. To be qualified for this position, Candidates must be eligible to access the Laboratory in compliance with Section 3112.

Pre-Employment Drug Test

External applicant(s) selected for this position must pass a post-offer, pre-employment drug test. This includes testing for use of marijuana as Federal Law applies to us as a Federal Contractor.

Wireless and Medical Devices

Per the Department of Energy (DOE), Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory must meet certain restrictions with the use and/or possession of mobile devices in Limited Areas. Depending on your job duties, you may be required to work in a Limited Area where you are not permitted to have a personal and/or laboratory mobile device in your possession. This includes, but not limited to cell phones, tablets, fitness devices, wireless headphones, and other Bluetooth/wireless enabled devices.

If you use a medical device, which pairs with a mobile device, you must still follow the rules concerning the mobile device in individual sections within Limited Areas. Sensitive Compartmented Information Facilities require separate approval. Hearing aids without wireless capabilities or wireless that has been disabled are allowed in Limited Areas, Secure Space and Transit/Buffer Space within buildings.

If you have encountered a job posting or have been approached with a job offer that you suspect may be fraudulent, we strongly recommend you do not respond.

title: Director, Clinical Monitoring Oversight
description:
Olema Oncology is a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company committed to transforming the standard of care and improving outcomes for patients living with breast cancer and beyond. With our transformation into a fully integrated oncology company well underway, it’s an exciting time to be part of Team Olema.

Our lead product candidate, palazestrant, is a novel, orally available complete estrogen receptor antagonist (CERAN) and selective estrogen receptor degrader (SERD) currently in two pivotal Phase 3 clinical trials. We expect top-line data from OPERA-01, our ongoing Phase 3 trial of palazestrant as a monotherapy in patients with second- or third-line ER+/HER2- metastatic breast cancer (MBC), in Q1 2027 which, if positive, could lead to our first potential approval and commercial launch in 2028. OPERA-02, our Phase 3 trial of palazestrant in combination with ribociblib in patients with frontline ER+/HER2- MBC, is enrolling patients. Together with its mechanism of action, pharmacokinetic properties, and the potential to demonstrate activity in both ESR1 wild-type and mutant tumors, palazestrant could transform the metastatic breast cancer treatment paradigm and provide access to a $15 billion global market opportunity.

Our follow-on product candidate, OP-3136, is a potent KAT6 inhibitor with the potential to generate further value and meaningfully impact the metastatic breast cancer treatment landscape – particularly in combination with palazestrant. We recently presented encouraging Phase 1 monotherapy data from this program across multiple solid tumor types, are advancing patient enrollment in the ongoing combination arms in MBC, and expect to initiate a Phase 1 study of OP-3136 in combination with Bayer’s darolutamide in metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer by the end of this year.

Aspiring to transform the metastatic treatment paradigm is an ambitious endeavor that requires a resolute approach to developing better therapies and passionate colleagues dedicated to helping the patients we serve feel better, longer. Team Olema possesses a deep commitment to a shared purpose, the sustained pursuit of excellence, cultivating the courage required to advance our programs, the drive to succeed, and a collective capacity for adaptability through learning, growth, and evolution. We are a small group of nimble self-starters who bring consistency in our quest for the extraordinary every single day.

If you’re ready to be part of a tenacious, courageous, agile, and growing team, join us in making a profound impact, together – for our patients, for your career, and for what’s beyond.

About the Role >>> Director, Clinical Monitoring Oversight

As the Director, Clinical Monitoring Oversight reporting to the Vice President, Clinical Operations you will provide strategic and operational leadership for global clinical monitoring oversight across Olema’s clinical programs. This role ensures that clinical monitoring, whether by internal teams, through Functional Service Providers (FSPs), or outsourced to Clinical Research Organizations (CROs), is executed with high standards of quality and consistency while maintaining compliance with GCP regulations. The Director oversees Olema’s Clinical Monitoring Oversight Leads, regional monitoring and oversight teams, clinical service provider/FSP provider, and site performance. This role will develop and implement global monitoring oversight strategies and standards for Olema’s clinical monitoring execution, driving operational excellence, data integrity, and inspection readiness across all trials with an emphasis on risk-based, data driven processes. The role will adapt to evolving organizational structures, monitoring delivery models, and clinical development needs as Olema's portfolio and operational requirements change.

This role is based out of either our San Francisco or Cambridge office and will require 10-20% travel.

Your work will primarily encompass:

  • Provide strategic direction and operational oversight of all global monitoring activities across Olema’s clinical programs
  • Oversee internal clinical monitoring and/or oversight team and FSP vendor responsible for providing Clinical Oversight Monitors (COMs) and/or Clinical Research Associates, ensuring alignment, consistency, and accountability across global regions
  • Adapt clinical monitoring and oversight strategies, organizational structures, resource allocation, and operating models to meet evolving clinical development and business needs
  • Oversee clinical monitoring and/or monitoring oversight resource planning, utilization, and related budgets and forecasts, ensuring alignment with study priorities, risk, workload, and portfolio needs
  • Establish and maintain effective governance with the FSP partner, including performance management, risk mitigation, and continuous improvement in monitoring quality and efficiency
  • In collaboration with assigned Clinical Trial Leads, define and implement Olema’s clinical monitoring and oversight strategy, including risk-based and centralized monitoring approaches in alignment with ICH-GCP and regulatory expectations
  • Ensure global harmonization of clinical monitoring and oversight processes, training, and documentation across programs and regions
  • Develop and monitor key performance indicators (KPIs) and quality metrics to evaluate site performance, FSP delivery, and regional oversight effectiveness
  • Collaborate with Clinical Operations, Data Management, Clinical Compliance, Clinical Quality, Pharmacovigilance, Clinical Science, and Clinical Development to ensure monitoring activities are aligned with program objectives and timelines
  • Contribute to the development and review of key operational documents, including Monitoring Plans, Oversight Plans, Risk Management Plans, and audit/inspection responses
  • Proactively assess monitoring risks and implement mitigation strategies to maintain inspection readiness
  • Lead, manage, and mentor internal monitoring and oversight staff, fostering collaboration, accountability, and continuous improvement
  • Support organizational capability development, succession planning, and evolving staffing needs to ensure effective monitoring and oversight as the clinical portfolio changes
  • Serve as the Monitoring Oversight representative on cross-functional and governance teams, presenting program updates, risks, and mitigation strategies to senior management
  • Drive innovation and process optimization in monitoring oversight practices, including leveraging technology and data analytics to enhance quality and efficiency
  • Establish and implement monitoring oversight reporting processes, tools, and communication pathways to ensure COMLs provide timely, consistent, and actionable updates to Clinical Trial Leads (CTLs), enabling effective collaboration, risk escalation, and CTL accountability for monitoring quality and performance within their assigned trials
  • May perform the full scope of Clinical Oversight Monitor Lead (COML) responsibilities, including direct oversight of assigned COMs, sites and CRAs, as needed based on study requirements, resource availability, and/or organizational priorities

Ideal Candidate Profile >>>

A love of challenging, important work. We are a pragmatic team, driven to imagine and develop meaningful therapies for improving lives. All employees within our company play a unique and crucial role in our success, both in accomplishing our mission and building a positive company culture. As such, we are looking for someone with the right combination of knowledge, experience, and attributes for this role.

Knowledge:

  • Bachelors/Masters in a scientific discipline
  • Expert knowledge of global clinical monitoring oversight strategies and execution
  • Deep understanding of ICH-GCP, global regulatory requirements, and inspection readiness expectations
  • Strong knowledge of vendor governance models, KPI frameworks, and quality management systems
  • Broad understanding of clinical development and cross-functional clinical operations

Experience:

  • 12+ years of clinical operations experience
  • Minimum 5 years direct site monitoring experience preferred
  • Minimum 5 years in a role providing oversight of global monitoring activities and FSP/CRO management preferred
  • 3+ years of demonstrated direct people management experience, including performance management, coaching, and staff development
  • Oncology experience required
  • Significant experience leading global monitoring oversight activities across programs
  • Experience managing FSP/CRO partnerships, including governance frameworks and performance management
  • Proven track record of driving monitoring quality, operational efficiency, and performance improvement initiatives
  • Experience leading teams and developing monitoring oversight capabilities
  • Experience with monitoring resource planning, vendor budgets, and resource utilization preferred

Attributes:

  • Strong strategic thinking and leadership capability
  • Excellent communication, influencing, and negotiation skills
  • Ability to lead cross-functional initiatives and align stakeholders
  • Strong analytical and decision-making ability
  • Results-oriented with high accountability
  • Ability to drive consistency and quality across complex global programs

The base pay range for this position is expected to be $235,000 - $250,000 annually, however the base pay offered may vary depending on location, market, job related knowledge, skills and capabilities, and experience. The total compensation package for this position also includes equity, bonus, and benefits.

title: Fire Alarm Designer
description:
JOB SUMMARY:

The Fire Alarm Designer position is responsible for operating with minimal supervision while completing project designs and submittals. Expected to be very familiar with SFP’s quality documents, procedures, and work instructions as they related to the design function.

ESSENTIAL JOB DUTIES:

  • Design fire detection/alarm, clean agent fire suppression, pre-engineered fire suppression, non-water-based fire protection, low voltage/security, etc. using working knowledge of fire alarm codes.
  • Adept with battery and voltage drop calculations.
  • Prepare submittal packages to send to (AHJ) Authority Having Jurisdiction and subsequent correspondence to achieve design approval.
  • Participate in coordination meetings with contractor.
  • Participate in design kick off meetings.
  • With assistance from the Design Manager, a Senior Sprinkler Designer, or others, prepare project package submittals including voltage calculation drops, materials and equipment required for installation and requisition materials for job.
  • With assistance from the Design Manager, a Senior Sprinkler Designer, or others, perform field surveys to ensure design is appropriate for structure.
  • Assist field personnel with design related installation issues.
  • Prepare and submit final job close-out documents after final acceptance testing.
  • Understand and follow SFP’s Safety program, SDS book, Hazardous communication program, policies and procedures.
  • Employee must know where all related safety documentation is at all times on each project.
  • Periodically attend seminars or similar education/training sessions to stay abreast of latest technology, codes, and standards changes.
  • Communicate with internal and external customers in a professional manner.
  • Other duties may be assigned.

QUALIFICATIONS

The qualifications listed below are representative of the elements required to perform the job successfully, however in some cases, an equivalent combination of Education, Training, Certifications and Experience may meet the job qualifications.

Education, Training, Certifications:

  • HS Diploma or equivalent required.
  • NICET II or NICET III and/or state required certification required. Equivalent experience will be considered assuming individual pursues NICET education.

Experience, Knowledge, Skill Requirements:

  • 1-2 years’ experience as alarm designer, strongly preferred.
  • Construction experience, Mechanical aptitude, basic and advanced math skills, required.

Communication Skills:

  • Must have the ability to effectively read, write and communicate in English with employees and customers.

Systems and Software Skills:

  • Ability to operate a computer, use Microsoft Office required.
  • Familiarity with AlarmCAD, AutoCAD and/or other CAD software, preferred.

Other Qualifications:

  • Valid driver’s license with acceptable driving record required.
  • Must be able to comply with SFP’s Drug and Alcohol policy and Background screening requirements, which may also include customer specific requirements based on contractual agreement.

PHYSICAL & WORK ENVIRONMENT REQUIREMENTS

Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform Essential Job Duties.

Physical Requirements:

While performing the duties of this job, the employee is required to sit for long periods. Employee will occasionally be required to bend, kneel, balance, lift <20lb, walk, stand, ascend/descend stairs, drive, twist, and reach above and below shoulders. Employee will frequently be required to drive and walk for periods.

Work Environment:

Employee will consistently be required to work indoors in an office setting, work alone and with other. Employees will occasionally be required to work outside, and be exposed to hot/cold temperatures, dust, fumes, chemicals, electrical hazards and noise. Employee will be occasionally required to wear all appropriate personal protective equipment, as required by company safety policies while visiting locations.

title: Crew Supervisor I
location: North East Los Angeles Site - Los Angeles, CA 90012
description:
Position Summary

Reporting to the Program Coordinator [Manager or Director], the Crew Supervisor I implements the mission of the LA Conservation Corps by using his/her leadership, supervisory and technical skills to develop the educational and work skills of young people enabling them to advance their own educational, personal and career opportunities.

The Crew Supervisor I is responsible for the supervision, work project coordination, recruitment, education support, and other leadership responsibilities for a team of 3-14 program participants aged 18-26 years old. The Crew Supervisor I provides the closest personal contact with corpsmembers in the work environment. It is their ability to relate, train and motivate that enables the corpsmembers to create stronger ties to their communities through community involvement and service, explore avenues for personal growth and development in a respectful and nurturing environment, and develop leadership skills to contribute to the advancement of all people.

Essential Duties and Responsibilities

Leadership & Mentorship

  • Manage, supervise, and participate in all aspects of crew work.
  • Crew Supervisor I’s work cooperatively with their crew and delegate responsibilities to crew members, maintain crew discipline, resolve conflicts, and establish/maintain crew morale.
  • Crew Supervisor I’s provide formal and informal feedback to Corpsmembers with specific attention to work productivity and quality, teamwork, and leadership. Crew Supervisor I’s receive feedback on their performance and are challenged to develop their own leadership skills within this program.

Conservation

  • Crew Supervisor I’s effectively learn and apply new environmental conservation skills.
  • Crew Supervisor I’s lead, train, and supervise a team during conservation based work projects, which may include but are not limited to: general maintenance, community beautification (e.g. recycling, litter abatement), food rescue, composting, graffiti removal, constructing and maintaining trails, constructing and maintaining fences and outdoor facilities, restoring wildlife habitat, maintaining public parks, campgrounds, and recreation areas, planting trees, conducting native plant revegetation, eradicating exotic/invasive plant species, surveying, conducting ecological testing and monitoring, mapping and monitoring using GPS technology, wildfire restoration, and restoring forest health and reducing wildfire risk through tree thinning using powered equipment.
  • The Crew Supervisor I supports environmental education activities and opportunities and helps inspire the next generation of conservation and public lands stewards.

Safety & Risk Management (Workplace Safety)

  • Oversee the physical and emotional safety of Corpsmembers at all times. Safety is the number one priority in everything we do, including work, education, and recreation. This includes not only the physical safety of participants but their mental and emotional safety as well. Crew Supervisor I’swill be responsible for transporting the crew and equipment, to and from the worksite daily, safely in Corps fleet vehicles.

Project Management & Implementation

  • Crew Supervisor I’s are responsible for safely completing conservation projects to high standards by training, working with, and supervising crews of 3-14 participants 28-40 hours/week. They will serve as the principal liaison with project sponsors and members of the local community.
  • The Crew Supervisor I’s principal role will be to manage and motivate their crew of young adults. In the field, they will provide direction to their crew with specific attention to safe work practices, proper tool use, work quality, and productivity.
  • Crew Supervisor I’s are mentors and role models and set the pace and tone of the project site. This position is physically, emotionally, and mentally demanding. Leaders will lift heavy loads, walk long distances, and should expect to find each project physically challenging.
  • Crew Supervisor I’s are expected to participate in as-needed overnight work projects (spikes)

Education (Coaching & Developing)

  • Crew Supervisor I’s are required to lead a variety of field trainings that support the conservation-based projects they are assigned to. Examples include but are not limited to: general hand tool use and maintenance, chainsaw use and maintenance, brush cutter use, trail building and maintenance, invasive plant removal, tree planting standards, and in-the-field studies on project topics related to the environment. Crew Supervisor I’s will also provide ongoing support and feedback for program participants.
  • Crew Supervisor I’s are also required to complete at least 10 hours of professional development trainings every year in the areas of tool operation, conflict resolution, leadership, driving, sexual harassment prevention and conflict resolution, to name a few.
  • Other duties may be assigned, as needed.

Please note that this job description is not designed to cover or contact a comprehensive listing of activities, duties and/or responsibilities that may be required of the employee for this job. Duties responsibilities and activities may change at any time and without notice.

Due to the organization’s response to the COVID-19 pandemic, your essential functions and responsibilities may change to accommodate the needs of the program and to stay in compliance with CDC and County of LA Public Health Department requirements.

title: Professional Services Technician
description:

QUALIFICATIONS

title: Sr. Solution Architect |Wisconsin, Minnesota, or Illinois

description:

We have been delivering digital infrastructure solutions since 2001. We are not a startup finding our footing. We have the network, cloud, cybersecurity, data protection, and managed services capabilities that allow our customers to consolidate vendors and simplify complexity. title: Inventory Specialist
description:
ASAHI BEER USA | OCTOPI BREWING


INVENTORY SPECIALIST

If It's on the Shelf, You Know It's in the System

1st Shift | Full-Time


ABOUT ASAHI BEER USA / OCTOPI BREWING

Founded in 2014 as a Wisconsin contract brewery, Octopi Brewing has spent over a decade brewing and packaging beer, seltzers, RTDs, and sodas for clients nationwide. In 2024, Asahi — brewers of Asahi Super Dry — acquired Octopi, making us the U.S. production home of Super Dry. Today, our 250+ person team of beverage industry pros keeps that same local, quality-first spirit alive at a state-of-the-art facility. Our Inventory team keeps raw materials, packaging, and finished goods accurately counted and tracked, so production and customer orders never miss a beat.


THE OPPORTUNITY

We're looking for an Inventory Specialist to support our Inventory Manager in keeping stock accurate across our brewery and warehouse locations. You'll run cycle counts, chase down variances, keep product rotating first-in, first-out, and work with teams across the building to make sure what's in our system matches what's on the floor.


WHAT MAKES THIS ROLE GREAT

  • A detail-driven role with real impact — accurate inventory keeps production running and finance numbers right
  • Variety every day — counting, investigating, reporting, and partnering with Brewing, Packaging, Quality, Logistics, and Finance
  • Room to improve how we work — you'll help shape SOPs and process improvements that cut waste and discrepancies

WHAT YOU'LL DO

  • Complete scheduled cycle counts, stock checks, and reconciliations for finished goods, raw materials, packaging, and staging stock
  • Enter inventory transactions, transfers, receipts, and adjustments accurately and on time in SAP and our warehouse management system
  • Investigate variances and stock losses, find the root cause, and recommend corrective action
  • Keep FIFO on track and flag slow-moving, aging, or at-risk stock before it becomes a write-off
  • Reconcile materials and finished goods after production runs so records match what's physically on hand
  • Track inventory on quality or operational hold, coordinating with Quality and Warehouse teams
  • Support month-end close with stock valuation checks and audit-ready documentation
  • Build reports on stock accuracy, cycle count completion, variances, and write-offs
  • Follow safe material handling practices during all counting and inventory activities

WHAT YOU BRING

Must-haves:

  • Practical understanding of inventory management, stock control, and warehouse operations
  • Knowledge of cycle counting, reconciliation, variance investigation, and FIFO
  • Experience with ERP, warehouse management, or inventory systems, with a strong focus on data accuracy
  • High attention to detail, and strong organization and time management
  • Clear written and verbal communication skills

Nice-to-haves:

  • Education in Supply Chain, Logistics, Operations, Business, or a related field
  • Experience with inventory in manufacturing, food and beverage, FMCG, or brewery operations
  • Prior warehouse, inventory, logistics, or supply chain support experience

BENEFITS & PERKS

  • Medical, dental, and vision coverage — effective the 1st of the month after 30 days
  • Company-paid life, short-term, and long-term disability insurance
  • 401(k) eligible after 3 months, with company match — 100% up to 3%, 50% on the next 2%
  • 120 hours of PTO annually, with accrual that grows the longer you're here
  • 9 paid holidays (if they fall on your scheduled workday)
  • A free beer after shift, because you earned it

PAY & SCHEDULE

  • Pay: $24.50/hr
  • Schedule: Monday – Friday 8am-5pm

Full-time, non-exempt

title: Clinical Laboratory Scientist, Full Time, Evening Shift
description:
Adventist Health Ukiah Valley has been deeply connected to the community we serve since 1956. We are comprised of a 50-bed acute care medical center, level IV trauma center, level II intensive care nursery services, extensive physical rehabilitation program, outpatient surgery and diagnostic center and advanced wound care center. Ukiah is a unique small town that charms you with its rich character, arts, vineyards and natural surroundings. Ukiah beckons you to explore all that the valley has to offer amidst our 300 days of sunshine each year. We are also conveniently located just two hours north of San Francisco and 45 minutes from the Pacific Coast.

Job Summary:

Prioritizes and performs a wide variety of clinical laboratory tests on various biological specimens. Reviews, evaluates, documents and reports results. Preserves confidentiality of patients and follows lab safety and maintenance protocols. Trains and supervises trainees, laboratory assistants and clerks as needed.

Job Requirements:

Education and Work Experience:

  • Bachelor’s Degree in medical technology, clinical laboratory science, biological sciences, chemical sciences or allied health technologies or equivalent: Required
  • Clinical laboratory experience: Preferred

Licenses/Certifications:

  • Valid Clinical Laboratory Scientist (CLS) license in state of employment: Required in CA
  • Current certification from American Society for Clinical Pathology (ASCP) or National Credentialing Agency for Labs (NCA): Preferred

Essential Functions:

  • Employs positive patient identification procedures to ensure the integrity of each specimen for pre-analytical, analytical and post-analytical testing. Performs proper specimen collection (including phlebotomy procedures as necessary), labeling, handling, preservation or fixation, processing or preparation, transportation and storage. Adheres to Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act (HIPAA) and other patient confidentiality guidelines and regulations.
  • Prioritizes lab orders according to type (STAT, ASAP, routine and timed studies) and performs various testing (including chemistry, coagulation, hematology, special chemistry, urinalysis, blood bank, serology, immunology, bacteriology, microbiology, referral testing and more) following prescribed quality assurance policies and procedures. Performs, evaluates and documents quality control checks. Reviews testing results evaluating validity of test results in comparison to anticipated results indicated per procedure manual.
  • Reviews and evaluates the validity and accuracy of test results, recognizing the interdependency of tests, the physiological conditions affecting results, patient age and normal values, controls, linearity errors, instrument codes, delta checks and more. Correlates test results with diagnoses and questions incompatible results. Thoroughly documents and communicates test results, expediting all critical values and results to appropriate clinicians.
  • Disposes of contaminated materials and equipment in accordance with policy and assures that work area is properly cleansed after each test. Performs equipment and instrumentation maintenance, troubleshooting and calibration as needed. Inventories and restocks reagents, calibrators, controls and supplies as needed.
  • Participates in the collection and evaluation of data for Performance Improvement evaluations. Documents adverse events using incident reporting tool. Orients, instructs and supervises laboratory assistants and clerks as needed.
  • Performs other job-related duties as assigned.

Organizational Requirements:

Adventist Health is committed to the safety and wellbeing of our associates and patients. Therefore, we require that all associates receive all required vaccinations as a condition of employment and annually thereafter, where applicable. Medical and religious exemptions may apply.

This AFSCME-represented position is classified as a Court Operations Associate. Typical hours for this position are 8:00 a.m. - 4:30 p.m., Monday-Friday, with some flexibility based on business needs.
